Cave Recorder (caverec) User Manual

Multitrack Rehearsal Recording, Live Studio Tracking, Full Stagebox Mixer, Virtual Analog Groovebox & Studio Sampler, MIDI Sync, Multi-Camera Video, Phase Alignment, Cave Companion Mobile & Studio CLI

Part I · Chapter 1

Overview & Studio Philosophy

The Human Musicianship Manifesto, the Anti-Bloat Curated Console Philosophy, Plain Studio Language across all four surfaces, the toggleable [?] Studio Coach and 450 ms hover tooltips, global SOLO CLEAR and Async Job status bar, independent t=0 Takes, 30-minute retroactive memory, live stereo Prints, track-level Overdub Passes, full Stagebox mixing, gridless MIDI Sync, Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments, the 6-archetype Groovebox and Studio Sampler, sample-accurate 50 FPS multi-camera studio video, Cave Companion Mobile with Bonjour discovery and Sample Studio Session, and the caverec-cli studio automation suite.

1.1 Why Cave Recorder Exists: The Human Musicianship Manifesto#

Cave Recorder (caverec) is a multitrack studio recorder, live mixing console, automatic phase-alignment processor, and band collaboration workstation purpose-built for rehearsal rooms, live tracking spaces, and project studios.

Modern music production has drifted toward sterile isolation. In an era of AI-generated tracks and hyper-commercial pop production, performances are routinely recorded one person at a time to a rigid click track, snapped to a mathematical bar/beat grid, and stripped of pitch and timing micro-variations. That pipeline works for synthetic programmed audio, but it destroys the soul of music that depends on human interaction in a shared room.

Across jazz, folk, stoner rock, doom, psychedelic and space rock, krautrock, blues, soul, and punk, the magic of a great record lives in the unrepeatable human moment: the shared eye contact before a dynamic breakdown, the collective tempo push of a rhythm section leaning into a chorus, the natural acoustic bleed of drums and cranked amplifiers breathing in the same room, and the spontaneous twenty-minute jam that nobody planned.

Cave Recorder takes a clear philosophical stand:

  1. Human Musicianship First, Zero Timeline Grid or Pitch-Correction Bloat: Cave Recorder intentionally omits timeline MIDI tracks, piano-roll editors, session beat grids, tempo-warping elastic audio, and robotic vocal pitch correction. Every Session Take is measured in real physical seconds, milliseconds, and sample frames (00:00:00.000) so the band's natural tempo fluctuations and groove breathe without a visual metronome dictating the performance. When musicians perform with hardware floor loopers, external drum machines, live-played CLAP or macOS Audio Unit (AU) virtual instruments, or the native Virtual Analog Drum Machine, Cave Recorder synchronizes them through its gridless MIDI Sync bridge and prints their audio pre-tape directly into standard 32-bit float Pass stems (rec/*.wav) just like live microphones.
  2. Technology as an Invisible Studio Assistant, Never a Replacement: Historically, capturing a full band live in one room with the punch and clarity of classic analog studio records required a dedicated recording engineer, an isolated control room, and two days spent moving microphone stands by millimeters to eliminate phase cancellation and amplifier buzz. Self-recording bands in rehearsal caves and basements rarely have a second person at the desk or hours to spend on technical setup. Cave Recorder acts as an invisible studio engineer that handles rolling 30-minute memory capture, one-click -18 dBFS gain staging, multicore spectral phase and polarity alignment, bleed-aware drum and amplifier gating, and non-destructive mistake surgery automatically. Musicians stay focused on their instruments and each other.
  3. Curated Analog-Inspired Console Instead of 90 Confusing Plugins: General-purpose workstations overwhelm musicians with dozens of overlapping legacy plugins, floating windows, and arcane parameter matrices. Cave Recorder provides a single, deeply integrated studio console and rack suite where every processor opens on a musical sweet spot for immediate results, while exposing deep physical controls underneath when an experienced mix engineer wants surgical precision.

Traditional digital audio workstations are modeled around a single linear timeline designed for solo production at a desk. When a full band plugs into an 18-channel audio interface for a three-hour rehearsal or live tracking session, a single continuous timeline creates immediate studio bottlenecks: finding a specific song run-through requires scrolling through hours of waveforms, spontaneous jams are lost when nobody remembers to press Record, bandmates wait days for someone to bounce rough mixes, and multi-microphone phase cancellation hollows out the drum kit and bass rig.

Cave Recorder solves four foundational studio and rehearsal problems:

1.1.1 Independent Zero-Based Takes Instead of a 3-Hour Linear Timeline#

In a band rehearsal or tracking session, musicians play multiple run-throughs of songs alongside spontaneous improvisations. In Cave Recorder, every time you press Record (R) with Overdub Mode turned off, the transport creates a brand-new, self-contained Take (Take 001, Take 002, Take 003, ...) that starts at its own zeroed timeline origin (00:00:00.000, sample 0).

Two different Takes are never appended end-to-end down a multi-hour timeline and are never stacked on top of one another in the same timeline view. Instead, switching the active Take in the Top Transport Deck (< TAKE 001 >) or via ALT + [ and ALT + ] immediately switches the Waveform Timeline and Mix Console playback to that song's 00:00:00.000 origin while keeping the room's microphone assignments, channel names, subgroup routing, and console mix intact.

1.1.2 30-Minute Retroactive Capture Memory (● RETRO & SAVE RETRO)#

The best moments in a rehearsal room often happen when the transport is stopped while the band is warming up or exploring a groove between songs. Whenever the audio interface is active and the ● RETRO indicator is lit in the Top Transport Deck, Cave Recorder continuously retains the last 30 minutes of live multi-channel audio across all record-armed channels in dedicated system memory.

Pressing the SAVE RETRO button in the Top Deck (or pressing SHIFT + R) immediately rescues the rolling 30-minute capture memory to disk as a new numbered Take (Take<NNN>), complete with individual pre-fader multitrack stems and a reference stereo file.

1.1.3 Simultaneous Live Console Print and Raw Multitrack Stems#

During every Take, Cave Recorder writes two distinct sets of audio files to disk in real time:

  1. Raw Pre-Fader Multitrack Stems (rec/): Every record-armed input channel (up to 32 input strips, CH01 through CH32) writes a discrete, uncompressed 32-bit floating-point mono or stereo .wav stem tapped directly after input gain trim and prior to channel insert processing and fader moves. This guarantees clip-free archival stems for later mixing or overdubbing.
  2. Live Stereo Master Bus Print (mix/): Simultaneously, when 2-TRK is armed on the MST MASTER BUS, a dedicated 2-track recorder tapped at the post-limiter output of the Master Bus captures the live stereo console mix (Print001.wav) with automatic Plugin Delay Compensation (PDC) latency trimming, including all channel EQ, VCA compression, tape saturation, subgroup processing, and auxiliary reverb and delay returns.

With a single click inside Export… (Convert Print to FLAC / MP3) in TAKES (CMD + 5 / CTRL + 5) or automatically upon cloud upload when AUTO-FLAC ON UPLOAD or AUTO-MP3 ON UPLOAD is enabled, Cave Recorder encodes the live stereo Print to 24-bit lossless .flac and/or 320 kbps CBR .mp3 (with a Xing/Info seek header for direct playback inside the Google Drive web browser player) and links it into the project-wide _Mixes/ folder. Band members walk out of rehearsal with finished stereo reference mixes ready for phone, browser, or car playback, while the engineer retains pristine 32-bit floating-point raw stems.

1.1.4 Console-First Layout and Automatic Multi-Mic Phase & Polarity Alignment#

Cave Recorder eliminates nested plugin windows and hidden routing matrices in favor of a fixed, dark-chassis studio console interface unified in Plain Studio Language across desktop, mobile phone, tablet, and dual-screen pad hardware. Input gain trim with one-click CALIBRATE TRIMS, polarity inversion (Ø), per-channel sub-sample delay (Φ) paired with a zero-slot 5-stage allpass Phase Align Network, an 8-slot reorderable processor rack (12-band parametric Dynamic EQ with dual-trace spectrum analyzer, multi-topology VCA/FET/Opto compressor, bleed- and harmonicity-aware noise gate, vocal rider, de-esser, transient shaper, micro-pitch doubler, 3-mode delay, 4-pole resonant ladder filter, studio plate reverb, 4-mode modulation, tape saturation, CLAP .clap plugins, and native macOS AUv3/AUv2 Audio Unit effects), stereo Aux Sends (RVB and DLY), Subgroup Bus routing (SUB 1..16), and 100 mm logarithmic faders are always accessible directly on the console faceplate.

When recording a drum kit or multi-miked guitar and bass cabinets, acoustic arrival-time differences and cabinet filter dispersion between close microphones, overheads, DI boxes, and room microphones cause comb filtering and 6 to 12 dB of low-frequency cancellation. Clicking ALIGN ALL in the Top Deck aligns acoustic arrival times to sub-sample accuracy (us / smp), while the two-tier Polarity & Phase Maximizer solves both instant broadband polarity inversions (Mode 1, completing in under 50 ms) and deep multicore frequency-dependent allpass phase rotation (Mode 2, 30 s to 30 min anytime solver with loudness-matched Candidates A, B, C, D auditioning) without moving a single microphone stand.

1.2 The Four-Tier Recording Hierarchy#

Cave Recorder organizes every recording into a strict four-tier studio hierarchy:

Project ---> Session ---> Take (t = 0) ---> Pass (Rec001 / Rec002-OD)

On disk, this hierarchy maps cleanly to human-readable folders and self-describing filenames inside your Cave Recorder Library Root:

Studio Entity Scope On-Disk Pattern Purpose & Studio Behavior
Project Band, artist, or musical venture <LibraryRoot>/<ProjectTag>/ Top-level workspace (for example, Grottfolk with tag GF, or Miscellaneous with tag MISC). Contains all Sessions for that band plus a unified _Mixes/ folder for rapid listening and cloud sharing. Managed via the PROJECT modal.
Session Single rehearsal night, tracking day, or studio gathering <ProjectTag>/<SessionID>_<Tag>/ Defines the room's physical microphone setup, channel strip names, input routing, subgroup buses, and console processing shared across every Take recorded that day. Session dates roll over at 08:00 local time so late-night recordings after midnight stay grouped with the same evening session.
Take Complete multitrack song run-through or jam (t = 0) Take<NNN>_<Stamp>[_<TakeTag>]/ An independent multitrack recording starting at 00:00:00.000. Pressing Record (R) when OVERDUB is off always creates a new numbered Take (Take 001, Take 002, ...) and switches the active timeline to that Take.
Base Pass (Rec001) Initial track-level recording inside a Take rec/*_<CC>-<Name>_Rec001_<Stamp>.wav The original 32-bit float pre-fader mono stem captured on an armed channel strip (PASS 01) when the Take was first recorded from 00:00:00.000.
Overdub Pass (Rec002-OD) Layered track-level recording inside an existing Take rec/*_<CC>-<Name>_Rec<MMM>-OD_<Stamp>.wav Additional track-level performance (OD 02, OD 03, ...) captured inside the currently active Take when OVERDUB (O) is latched on the transport bar.
Pass Lanes Expandable track sub-lanes in Timeline Stored in *_Take<NNN>_take.json Visual lanes (PASS 01 Base Pass and OD 02, OD 03 Overdub Passes) expanded in TIMELINE (CMD + 1 / CTRL + 1) with E (and collapsed with SHIFT + E) for auditioning (Use PASS 01 / ★ OD 02), muting (M), and removing (Del) passes within the active Take.
Video Angle & .vididx Index Sample-locked studio or mobile camera recording inside a Take video/*_Take<NNN>_Cam<CC>-<Name>_<Stamp>.<mp4|vididx> Constant Frame Rate (50 FPS or 25 FPS preferred, with automatic 30 FPS / 60 FPS CFR negotiation on cameras without 50 Hz modes) camera angle recorded from connected desktop USB/HDMI cameras or wireless Cave Companion Android and iOS mobile camera nodes, paired with a binary .vididx frame-to-sample index file locked to the 48.0 kHz audio clock. Local cameras stay physically powered off (hardware LED dark) whenever unarmed, playing back, session-closed, or behind fullscreen modals, and shift the Top-Deck ● CAMERA LED to Gold (live preview) or Crimson (recording) whenever active.
Print (Print<NNN>) Real-time post-Master-Bus stereo recording mix/*_Take<NNN>_Print<NNN>_<Stamp>.<wav|flac|mp3> Captured live alongside the raw stems while tracking a Take when 2-TRK PRINT is armed on the Master Bus. Converting a Print to 24-bit .flac and/or 320 kbps CBR .mp3 inside TAKES (Export…) links it into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/ for immediate band playback without waiting for an offline render.
Mixdown (Mix<NNN> / VideoMix<NNN>) Offline Master Bus stereo audio or split-screen video render mix/*_Take<NNN>_Mix<NNN>_<Stamp>.<wav|flac|mp3> / VideoMix<NNN>.mp4 Faster-than-real-time stereo Master Bus audio render (FLAC / MP3) or multi-camera split-screen .mp4 video mixdown (Single, Side-by-Side Crop, Side-by-Side 16:9, 3-Cam Band, Quad 2x2) of a Take linked into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/.
Stem Bounce (Bounce<NNN>) Offline post-processor track or subgroup render bounce/*_Take<NNN>_<Target>_Bounce<NNN>.wav Offline render of an individual channel strip or Subgroup Bus capturing all insert processing and phase alignment for delivery to external remixing workflows.
Snapshot (Snap<NNN>) Immutable console state capture snapshots/<SessionID>_Snap<NNN>_<UTC>.json Point-in-time capture of the entire Mix Console state (faders, pans, EQ bands, compressor thresholds, routing, and active Pass Lane selections), created automatically after every recording pass or manually via SNAP MANUAL (CMD + S / CTRL + S).
Live Mix (LIVE MIX) Automatic live console backup during Snapshot audition Held in working session memory Whenever you audition a historical Snapshot in TAKES, Cave Recorder preserves your current working console state in LIVE MIX and docks a global AUDITIONING SNAP NNN banner across every tab so you can click A/B Live Mix or Return to Live Mix (BACKSPACE) without losing a single fader move.
Distinguishing Session-Level Takes from Track-Level Passes

Cave Recorder maintains a strict separation between Takes and Passes. A Take (Take 001, Take 002) is an entire song or jam recorded across the studio room starting at 00:00:00.000, selected in the Top Transport Deck or TAKES (CMD + 5 / CTRL + 5). A Pass (PASS 01 Base Pass or OD 02 Overdub Pass) is an individual performance recorded on a single channel strip inside the currently active Take, displayed inside expandable Pass Lanes in TIMELINE (CMD + 1 / CTRL + 1).

1.3 Tour of the Studio Workspace#

Cave Recorder opens into a dark studio console workspace divided into three horizontal tiers: the persistent Top Transport & Session Header Deck (with optional [?] Studio Coach bar and global status banners), the Upper Inspector Wells, and the Lower Console Channel & Bus Strips. Newly created empty sessions (0 Takes) open directly on MIXER (CMD/CTRL + 2) so you can check input meters and arm strips immediately, while sessions that already contain recorded Takes open on TIMELINE (CMD/1).

  1. Top Transport & Session Header Deck (Top): Remains pinned across all workspace views (TIMELINE, MIXER, CHANNEL STRIP, MARKERS, TAKES, GROOVEBOX, PLUGINS, KEYMAP, STAGEBOX, and REMOTE) using fixed-width Plain Studio Language labels at every standard display width (>= 1366 px). Houses project and session selection, inline session renaming (✎), floating Google Drive CLOUD sync popover, 30-minute ● RETRO / SAVE RETRO controls, main transport buttons (▶, ■, ●, OVERDUB), the active Take selector, digital timecode and sample counters, global multi-mic phase alignment, one-click SOLO (N)·CLEAR, a global Async Job progress/cancel pill, AUDIO SETTINGS, KEYMAP, the [?] Studio Coach toggle, connected gear LED pills (● STAGEBOX, ● REMOTE, ● CONTROLLER, ● MIDI, ● CAMERA), and latency diagnostics (LATENCY 0.0 ms, LOW-LATENCY).
  2. Upper Inspector Wells (Middle): Displays four side-by-side real-time visualizers and editors for the currently selected channel strip or Subgroup Bus:
    • 8-Slot Reorderable Processor Rack & Tape Controls (Left Well): Shows slots 1 through 8 (1:PLUGIN, 2:12B EQ, 3:VCA CMP, 4:AUX SND, ...), per-slot bypass (B), up/down slot reordering arrows, a clean + ADD PROCESSOR ▾ picker menu, dedicated Tape saturator controls (DRV, WRM, BIAS, HC, OUT, MIX), SWAP EQ/CMP, and channel RESET.
    • 12-Band Parametric EQ & Dual-Trace RTA Spectrum Analyzer (Center-Left Well): Interactive Bode magnitude curve with draggable filter nodes (BELL, LSHF, HSHF, HPF, TILT, DYN) superimposed over a pre-EQ and post-EQ real-time spectrum trace (20 Hz to 20 kHz).
    • VCA Compressor & Gain Reduction Transfer Curve (Center-Right Well): Displays the compressor knee and transfer curve (-48 dB to 0 dB), topology switcher (VCA, FET, OPTO), SIDECHAIN source selector, SIDECHAIN LISTEN, TRIM, HPF, LPF, stereo link (LNK), and real-time Gain Reduction (GR) metering.
    • Upper Mini-Timeline & Multi-Tier Waveform Overview (Right Well): Displays the composite waveform of the active Take with playhead tracking, PASSES expansion shortcut, LOCK PLAYHEAD, → PLAYHEAD, and zoom controls (ZOOM +, ZOOM -, 1:1).
  3. Lower Console Strips (Bottom): Houses up to 32 Input Channel Strips (CH01..CH32, physical mics, stereo pairs, Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments, or Drum Stem Breakouts), up to 16 stereo Subgroup Bus Strips (DRUM BUS, INST BUS, ...), up to 8 dedicated stereo Aux Return Strips (AUX 1 REVERB with zero-latency convolution IR and AUX 2 TAPE DLY with 3-mode tempo-synced echo), and the permanently pinned MST MASTER BUS strip (snug beside the last Aux strip in compact sessions, pinned cleanly on the right edge with a vertical seam on overflow) featuring Master Tape, Master Compressor, brickwall Limiter, HW OUT | TAPE stagebox monitor toggle, live 2-TRK PRINT arm, independent FLAC and MP3 format toggles, and one-click BOUNCE offline Mixdown render controls. Across all four surfaces (Desktop, Mobile Phone, Tablet, and Dual-Screen Pad Controller), channel control buttons always follow the strict [M] (Mute Amber) -> [S] (Solo Gold) -> [R] (Record Crimson) order.

1.3.1 Top Deck Row 1: Session Identity, Transport, Timecode, Phase & Studio Coach#

The top row of the header deck (48 px) is organized into three functional clusters from left to right:

Cluster Control / Badge Keyboard Shortcut Studio Function
Left: Session & Cloud Active Session Pill (TEST_20..ession ✎) Click to Rename Displays the currently loaded Session name. Click to rename the active Session inline without opening a modal (ENTER saves, ESC cancels).
Left: Session & Cloud PROJECT CMD + O (macOS) / CTRL + O (Win/Linux) Opens the Project and Session Browser modal to switch Projects, create a new Session from a template, save the current console as a reusable Session Template (Save Template…), link a remote shared project, or open a recent Session.
Left: Session & Cloud CLOUD ▾ Mouse Click Opens the floating Cloud Sync Quick Controls popover (AUTO-FLAC ON UPLOAD, AUTO-MP3 ON UPLOAD, SYNC SESSION FULL, SYNC SESSION MIXES) and displays real-time Google Drive transfer status.
Center: Transport & Take ● RETRO Mouse Click (Bindable in KEYMAP) Enables or disables the continuous 30-minute retroactive capture memory across all armed input channels. Glows emerald green when active.
Center: Transport & Take SAVE RETRO SHIFT + R Flushes the rolling 30-minute retroactive capture memory to disk as a new numbered Take and switches the active timeline to the rescued Take.
Center: Transport & Take Play (▶) SPACE Starts or pauses playback of the active Take from the current playhead position. Glows green while transport is rolling.
Center: Transport & Take Stop (■) SHIFT + SPACE Stops playback or active recording immediately and finalizes open audio files and post-recording Snapshots. Pressing Stop a second time while already stopped performs Return-to-Zero (00:00:00.000) while keeping the timeline playhead visible at sample 0.
Center: Transport & Take Record (●) R Starts or stops multitrack recording. Creates a new t = 0 Take (Take<NNN>) when OVERDUB is off, or records a new Overdub Pass (Rec<MMM>-OD) inside the active Take when OVERDUB is latched.
Center: Transport & Take OVERDUB O Latches Overdub Mode (glows red when active and updates the timecode badge to OVERDUB → TAKE NNN). While latched, pressing Record (R) records new track-level Overdub Passes on armed channels while playing back existing tracks of the active Take.
Center: Transport & Take Cycle / Loop (⇄) C Toggles continuous loop playback and loop overdubbing across the active Take range.
Center: Transport & Take SCROLL Mouse Click (Bindable in KEYMAP) Keeps the Waveform Timeline viewport following the advancing playhead during playback and recording.
Center: Transport & Take < TAKE 001 > ALT + [ / ALT + ] Steps backward or forward through the Session's active Takes, immediately loading that Take's 00:00:00.000 timeline and Pass Lanes.
Center: Transport & Take 00:00:00.500 / 24,000 smp Readout High-contrast LED timecode readout (HH:MM:SS.mmm) paired with the exact sample frame position (24,000 smp), active recording mode (NEW TAKE or OVERDUB), and hardware sample rate (48.0 kHz).
Right: Phase, Safety & Help ● ALIGN ALL Mouse Click (Bindable in KEYMAP) Runs automatic multi-microphone arrival-time and polarity correlation across all active channels relative to the reference channel.
Right: Phase, Safety & Help PHASE A/B Mouse Click Toggles global phase alignment processing between active and bypassed for instant A/B listening.
Right: Phase, Safety & Help SOLO (N)·CLEAR Mouse Click Appears automatically in Solo Gold whenever one or more console strips are soloed or any compressor SIDECHAIN LISTEN is active. Click once to clear all solos and sidechain listens immediately.
Right: Phase, Safety & Help AUDIO SETTINGS CMD + , (macOS) / CTRL + , (Win/Linux) Opens the Audio Device & Latency Settings modal to configure interfaces, sample rate, buffer size, hardware loopback calibration, Studio Pad Surface diagnostics, and caverec-cli installation.
Right: Phase, Safety & Help KEYMAP CMD + 8 (macOS) / CTRL + 8 (Win/Linux) Opens the interactive Keymap shortcut reference and custom keybinding editor covering all 62 bindable studio actions.
Right: Phase, Safety & Help ? (Studio Coach) ? Toggles the docked 28 px Studio Coach readout strip below Row 2, displaying the hovered control's full studio role, keyboard shortcut, and drag modifiers (persisted across launches). Every major control also displays a delayed 450 ms hover micro-tooltip (suppressed automatically during active drags).

The second row of the Top Deck (32 px) provides fixed-width navigation across Cave Recorder's primary workspace tabs (CMD/CTRL + 1..7) on the left, live background job progress (⟳ EXPORT 64% ×) in the center-right whenever an offline render, plugin scan, cloud transfer, or sampler bounce is running, and connected hardware/companion gear pills (● STAGEBOX, ● REMOTE, ● CONTROLLER, ● MIDI, ● CAMERA) plus latency controls on the right:

TIMELINE CMD + 1 (macOS) / CTRL + 1 (Win/Linux) Multi-track 2D zoomable waveform editor, expandable Pass Lanes for overdub comping, marker flags, loop ranges, direct Range-to-Sampler import, Take splitting, and the Multi-Camera Video Monitor. Detailed in Chapter 6: Waveform Timeline, Pass Lanes, Markers & Ranges.
MIXER CMD + 2 (macOS) / CTRL + 2 (Win/Linux) Full studio mixing console with Upper Inspector Wells, up to 32 input strips (physical mics, Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments, or Drum Stem Breakouts), Subgroup Buses, Aux Returns, and the pinned Master Bus. Default landing tab for new 0-Take sessions. Detailed in Chapter 4: Mix Console, Stagebox Mixer, Signal Flow & Channel Strips.

Detailed in Chapter 5: Built-In Processors, Phase Alignment, Groovebox & Plugins (CLAP & AU).
MARKERS CMD + 4 (macOS) / CTRL + 4 (Win/Linux) Sortable tabular manager for all Take markers (M001..) and loop/export ranges (R001..), with inline click-to-rename, playhead jump (GO TO), and range-to-Take extraction (NEW TAKE). Detailed in Chapter 6: Waveform Timeline, Pass Lanes, Markers & Ranges.
TAKES CMD + 5 (macOS) / CTRL + 5 (Win/Linux) Session dashboard containing the Takes Catalog with clean 4-button rows ([Load], [Rename], [Export…], [⋯]), one-click FLAC and MP3 Print conversion, offline Mixdown and Stem Bounce rendering, undo history, Snapshots, Live Mix A/B comparison, and Cloud Sync controls. Detailed in Chapter 7: Takes Dashboard, Mixdowns, Snapshots, Companion Mobile & Cloud Sync.
GROOVEBOX CMD + 6 (macOS) / CTRL + 6 (Win/Linux) Native 6-archetype Virtual Analog Groovebox & Studio Sampler (4 coupled drum voices, the monophonic ANALOG BASS synthesizer, and the STUDIO SAMPLER voice across SEQUENCER, SYNTH & SCOPE, SAMPLER, and ARRANGER sub-views) with SuperFlux noise-robust transient slicing, live console resampling, triggered log-time Storage-CRT scope, Master Glue Bus, and individual voice console stem breakouts. Persistent Global Mode Banners (READ-ONLY PREVIEW & AUDITIONING SNAP)

Whenever a shared cloud session is opened while locked on another studio computer, or whenever you audition a historical Snapshot, Cave Recorder docks a persistent 28 px safety banner directly beneath the Top Deck across all workspace tabs (READ-ONLY PREVIEW (Locked by <Machine>) with [Save Local Copy…] and [Take Lock], or AUDITIONING SNAP NNN with [A/B Live Mix] and [Return to Live Mix]). You can move freely between MIXER, TIMELINE, and CHANNEL STRIP without ever losing sight of your live session state.

Non-Blocking Studio Responsiveness, Transactional Safety & Sustained Real-Time Reliability

Heavy studio operations (timeline audio repair, hum cancellation, spectral spot-healing, Take splitting, offline exports, Studio Sampler bank loading, third-party plugin scanning and reloading, and Project or Cloud Sync transfers) run asynchronously off the 60 Hz interface thread on both Desktop and Cave Companion mobile so console meters, faders, and live transport controls remain fluid throughout. Automatic session-switch safety guards discard stale background results cleanly whenever you load a different Take or Session mid-operation, and transactional file writes roll back automatically on disk or network interruption so active Sessions stay intact. During sustained multi-hour sessions, real-time audio underrun tracking, background voice and memory reclamation off the live audio path, and a non-blocking USB controller helper transport keep playback and recording glitch-free.

1.4 The Anti-Bloat Curated Console Philosophy#

General-purpose workstations and large commercial plugin bundles often ship with 70 to 90 separate effects plugins: five nearly identical equalizers, eight redundant compressors named after vintage circuit board revisions, four separate de-essers, and dozens of single-purpose utility modules. In a fast-moving band rehearsal or self-engineered tracking session, scrolling through huge plugin menus and juggling floating windows breaks musical momentum and causes decision fatigue.

Cave Recorder replaces plugin sprawl with a Curated Native Console & Rack Suite built around five engineering pillars:

1.4.1 Pillar 1: Fewer, Deeper Multi-Mode Instruments Instead of Redundant Clones#

Rather than cluttering the rack with dozens of single-purpose plugins, Cave Recorder consolidates classic studio hardware topologies into focused, multi-mode processors:

  • One 3-Topology Compressor (VCA, FET, Opto): Switches cleanly between feed-forward RMS bus glue (VCA), ultra-fast discrete transistor transient limiting with odd-harmonic grit (FET), and program-dependent dual-stage electroluminescent optical leveling (Opto).
  • One Context-Aware 3-Variant Gate (Expander, Drum Bleed, Amp Dynamic): Combines a smooth downward vocal/room expander, a differential sidechain tom/snare bleed gate with automatic fundamental lock ([LRN]), and a pitch-harmonicity and spectral-entropy amplifier gate built for high-gain stoner, doom, and psychedelic guitar rigs.
  • One Tempo-Synced 3-Mode Echo & Delay (Capstan Tape, BBD Analog, Pristine Digital): Covers saturating magnetic tape echo, dark bucket-brigade analog delay with compander breathe and clock noise, and clean stereo rhythmic delay with dynamic ducking and optional [SYNC] musical note subdivisions (1/64 through 4BAR).
  • One Tempo-Synced 4-Mode Studio Modulator (Through-Zero Flanger, Dimension Chorus, Optical Phaser, Harmonic Tremolo): Covers tape-style through-zero flanging, motionless stereo dimension widening, 4/6/8/12-stage photocell phasing, and dual-band crossover harmonic tremolo with [SYNC] beat subdivisions and clickless downbeat phase locking ([LCK]).
  • One 6-Archetype Virtual Analog Groovebox & Studio Sampler (GROOVEBOX): Synthesizes analog kicks, snares, claps, metallic hi-hats, rides, modal percussion, and monophonic ANALOG BASS synth basslines alongside the STUDIO SAMPLER voice (SuperFlux noise-robust transient slicing, live console resampling, Timeline Range import, bipolar DJ filter and tuned comb resonator, assignable LFO, and reversible versioned bounces), paired with a polymetric and melodic [2D | NOTE | VEL] Step and Scene Sequencer, chromatic MIDI keyboard input, triggered Storage-CRT oscilloscope, Master Glue Bus, individual voice console stem breakouts, and wireless Cave Companion tablet and phone control.

1.4.2 Pillar 2: Immediate Musical Sweet Spots with Deep Custom Power Underneath#

Every native processor in Cave Recorder is tuned so that engaging it on a channel strip immediately improves the sound without requiring five minutes of parameter tweaking:

  • One-Click Calibration & Auto-Setup: Clicking CALIBRATE TRIMS sets every channel's input gain to the -18 dBFS RMS console sweet spot with a -6 dBFS peak ceiling. Clicking [LRN] on the Drum Bleed gate listens to a single tom hit and automatically locks the resonant key filter to that drum's fundamental pitch (55 Hz to 350 Hz, default 110 Hz). Engaging Vocal Rider with Breath / Bleed Freeze holds the fader steady during pauses so drum bleed is never boosted between vocal lines.
  • Full Surgical Depth When Needed: Beneath these immediate defaults, mix engineers have full access to per-band Dynamic EQ thresholds, 16-sample smoothed filter trajectories, sidechain Tilt EQ, smooth gate ballistics, 5-stage allpass frequency/Q coordinates, and loudness-matched AUTO LEVEL bypass auditioning.

1.4.3 Pillar 3: Solving Real Live-Room Physics (Phase Dispersion, Bleed & High-Gain Sustain)#

Plugins designed for isolated bedroom overdubs fall apart when an entire band plays loud in an untreated room. Cave Recorder's processors are engineered specifically for the acoustic realities of live band tracking:

  • Multi-Mic Phase Cancellation & Allpass Dispersion: Combining a bass DI with a miked ported bass cabinet, or blending 8 microphones across a drum kit, introduces both acoustic time-of-flight delays and frequency-dependent phase rotation across cabinet ports and crossover networks. Every channel strip includes a zero-slot top-of-strip Phase Align Network driven by the two-mode Polarity & Phase Maximizer (Mode 1 instant binary polarity solver in under 50 ms, and Mode 2 multicore spectral allpass solver).
  • Snare-into-Tom Spill & Cymbal Wash: The Drum Bleed gate uses a differential key detector (comparing the target tom against a snare or overhead reference) and a dynamic decay low-pass filter (20 kHz sweeping down to 250 Hz to 800 Hz, default 380 Hz) so tom hits ring out naturally without sucking bursts of hi-hat and cymbal wash into the mix.
  • Stoner, Doom & Psychedelic High-Gain Guitar Dynamics: Standard threshold noise gates destroy quiet clean fingerpicking (-34 dBFS) and chop off intentional harmonic amplifier feedback bloom, or else sit wide open while stacked fuzz pedals roar at -22 dBFS. The Amp Dynamic gate measures autocorrelation pitch periodicity (H ∈ [0, 1]) and spectral flatness so whispered clean passages and 1.5 s to 5.0 s feedback sustain pass untouched while 60 Hz hum and fuzz hiss clamp shut in 15 ms to 40 ms (default 18 ms to 22 ms) on a palm-mute stop.

1.4.4 Pillar 4: Non-Destructive Live-Take Salvage and Mistake Surgery#

When a band captures a once-in-a-lifetime live groove, you cannot ask them to play the exact same improvisation again just because a snare rimshot clipped an preamp converter for 12 samples, a vintage combo amp buzzed at 60 Hz, or the guitarist hit a wrong chord in bar 42.

Cave Recorder treats live-take rescue as a core console workflow rather than an external audio restoration chore. Directly inside TIMELINE and CHANNEL STRIP, you can reconstruct clipped ADC peaks ([REPAIR CLIPPING] using smooth spline and spectral waveform interpolation), notch out 12 harmonics of 50/60 Hz power-line hum without dulling guitar tone, comp a single bar from an Overdub Pass ([USE OD 02 IN RANGE]), graft a clean chord from another bar ([PATCH FROM SOURCE...]), or apply a spectral spot-heal ([SMOOTH OVER ARTIFACT]) while leaving the original 32-bit floating-point recording on disk completely untouched.

1.4.5 Pillar 5: Strict Separation Between Master Bus Printing and Control Room Monitoring#

In a rehearsal or tracking room, engineers constantly need to check mono fold-down compatibility (MONO), solo the stereo side difference (STEREO DIFF), isolate the sub-bass (SUB < 90 Hz) or midrange (MID 350 Hz - 3.5 kHz) across studio monitors, dim the speakers (DIM -20) to talk to the band, or A/B a heavy processing chain at matched loudness (AUTO LEVEL).

In Cave Recorder, the Control Room Monitor Bar (MONITOR:) is wired strictly downstream of the Master Bus 2-TRK PRINT live tap and offline BOUNCE engine. You can solo frequency bands, flip to mono, or dim the control room speakers right in the middle of recording a live Take without ever altering or interrupting the stereo Print001.wav being written for the band.

Live-Room Studio Challenge Why Traditional DAWs Struggle Cave Recorder Curated Console Solution
Hollow drums and thin bass from multi-mic phase cancellation Requires manual sample nudging or expensive external phase plugins inserted on every track Top-of-strip zero-slot Phase Align Network + ALIGN ALL sub-sample delay + Mode 1 (< 50 ms) & Mode 2 multicore spectral allpass solver
Fuzz/tube amp hum vs. quiet clean picking and feedback sustain Amplitude noise gates choke quiet clean notes and chop off harmonic feedback tails Amp Dynamic gate using pitch harmonicity and spectral flatness (Feedback Bloom Lock + 18 ms Palm-Mute Clamp + HF Tame)
Snare and cymbal spill triggering rack and floor tom gates Standard gates false-trigger on loud snare hits and let harsh cymbal wash through on tom decay Drum Bleed gate with differential key rejection, [LRN] fundamental auto-detection, and dynamic decay low-pass filter
Inconsistent input trim levels across 18 live mics Slow manual trim riding before rehearsal can start One-click CALIBRATE TRIMS (Gain Utility) normalizing channels to -18 dBFS RMS with a -6 dBFS peak ceiling

Hardware Setup, Audio Connections & First Session

Connecting multi-channel USB and ADAT interfaces, automatic studio interface selection, macOS Direct Download vs. Mac App Store App Sandbox setup (native Open/Save panels, persistent folder bookmarks, and isolated out-of-process Audio Units), locking digital clocks, calibrating roundtrip loopback latency, persistent Hardware Direct Monitoring preferences, connecting 50 FPS / 25 FPS studio cameras with the 3-Second Optical & Audio Flash Latency Calibration modal, connecting and managing full OSC Stageboxes (X-Air UDP 10024 including XR18V2 and X32 UDP 10023 across the 4-tab STAGEBOX workspace and USB-to-Aux-to-Main L/R output routing), configuring bidirectional MIDI Clock, Looper Sync, MIDI Learn footswitches, and 1-click Hardware MIDI Latency Ping calibration, setting up a Dual-Screen Studio Pad Surface (CONTROLLER pill), installing caverec-cli and Studio Engineering Skills, and creating your first Project and Session.

2.1 Connecting Multi-Channel Audio Interfaces (USB, Thunderbolt & ADAT)#

Cave Recorder supports up to 32 simultaneous mono or stereo-linked input tracks (CH01 through CH32), making it an ideal match for rackmount 18-in / 20-out or 32-channel USB and Thunderbolt studio interfaces paired with 8-channel ADAT optical microphone preamp expanders.

A standard 18-channel rehearsal and tracking rig combines three physical input groups into a single unified audio device:

  1. Inputs 1-8 (Primary Interface Onboard Mic/Line Preamps): Eight XLR/TRS combo preamps on the main rack unit, typically dedicated to close drum microphones, guitar cabinet mics, rack and floor toms, and stereo drum overheads.
  2. Inputs 9-10 (Coaxial S/PDIF or Auxiliary Line Return): Two digital coaxial S/PDIF channels or line inputs used for stereo hardware synthesizers, stage pianos, or drum machines (SpdifSynthL and SpdifSynthR).
  3. Inputs 11-18 (8-Channel ADAT Optical Preamp Expander): Eight additional microphone and instrument preamps fed from an external 8-channel ADAT expander into the primary interface's ADAT OPTICAL IN port over a TOSLINK fiber-optic cable, dedicated to BassDi, BassAmp, GuitarL, GuitarR, KeysL, KeysR, LeadVocal, and RoomAmbience.
