2.8.2 Standalone Helper Distribution & Operating System Setup#

Cave Recorder communicates with the USB controller through a lightweight standalone helper (extras/encdr-daemon/encdr-daemon) packaged alongside the direct desktop release outside Cave Recorder.app/Contents/. Cave Recorder launches and supervises this helper automatically on startup (or you can point the CAVEREC_ENCDR_DAEMON_BIN environment variable to a custom build). Pad strikes, rotary encoder turns, LED feedback, and dual-screen 480×272 display frames stream across a non-blocking real-time controller transport so sustained live performance never stalls the audio engine or the 60 Hz console display.

  • macOS (Direct Distribution): Plug in the controller over USB and launch Cave Recorder. If a third-party background USB agent (NIHardwareAgent or NIHostIntegrationAgent) holds exclusive access to the display interface, Cave Recorder flags a red LED on ● CONTROLLER and reports the exact remediation banner inside AUDIO SETTINGS. Quit or unload the conflicting agent and reconnect the USB cable.
  • macOS (Mac App Store Edition): Because Mac App Store sandboxing prohibits launching external USB helper binaries, the Studio Pad Surface helper is intentionally disabled in the Mac App Store edition. Use the direct macOS distribution release for Dual-Screen Pad Controller support.
  • Linux (udev Permissions): Copy the bundled extras/encdr-daemon/60-encdr-maschine.rules file into /etc/udev/rules.d/ so your active desktop user receives non-root USB and HID access (uaccess), then reload rules using the commands below.
  • Windows (WinUSB Display Interface): Keep USB Interface 0 on the standard Windows HID driver for pads and buttons, and bind USB Interface 1 (bulk display output) to the WinUSB driver. If Interface 1 is unbound, Cave Recorder lights the Top Deck pill LED red and shows step-by-step WinUSB guidance inside AUDIO SETTINGS.
sudo cp extras/encdr-daemon/60-encdr-maschine.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
sudo udevadm trigger

2.8.3 Reading the Top Deck ● CONTROLLER Status Indicator#

Row 2 of the Top Deck displays a dedicated hardware surface indicator pill (● CONTROLLER):

  • Lit LED (Emerald in [DRUM STUDIO], Gold in [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE]): Dual-Screen Pad Controller connected and active. Clicking the pill toggles cleanly between [DRUM STUDIO] and [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] (matching SHIFT + CHANNEL on hardware).
  • Amber LED: Helper process running and probing USB connection.
  • Dim LED: Standby (no controller connected, clicking toggles personality) or disabled in Mac App Store sandbox builds (clicking opens AUDIO SETTINGS to display the App Store sandbox notice). Hover (or turn on [?] Studio Coach) to inspect full status text and active personality.
  • Red LED (Driver, Clock, or Permission Fault): Exclusive USB interface contention (macOS background agent), missing Linux udev rule, missing Windows WinUSB driver, or an OS monotonic clock domain mismatch (ClockMismatch). Clicking the pill opens AUDIO SETTINGS directly to the red diagnostic banner with exact platform instructions.
Three-Way Studio Synchronization

Hardware Pad Surface controls, the desktop Mix Console and Drum Machine views, and wireless Cave Companion tablets and phones all observe the same studio engine state. Turning a fader, muting a voice, switching a Pattern, or launching a Scene from any of the three surfaces updates the other two immediately with unified reversible Undo history.

Part I · Chapter 3

Typical Studio & Rehearsal Workflows

Step-by-step guides for band rehearsal capture, 30-minute retroactive memory rescue, multi-mic phase alignment and Polarity Maximizer optimization, overdub comping, live-take salvage, multi-camera rehearsal video capture with Cave Companion wireless mobile camera nodes and split-screen mixdowns, live looping with Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments, the Groovebox, and Studio Sampler resampling and slicing, hands-on Studio Pad Surface dual-personality tracking and performance ([DRUM STUDIO], SAMPLING, and [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE]), full Stagebox live FOH/IEM mixing with MY MONITOR and Virtual Soundcheck, and scripted studio automation via caverec-cli.

This chapter walks through ten end-to-end studio workflows that cover the day-to-day operation of Cave Recorder: capturing a full-band rehearsal with instant stereo reference mixes, rescuing an unrecorded jam from the 30-minute retroactive memory, phase-aligning a multi-microphone drum kit and guitar rig, tracking and comping layered overdubs in Pass Lanes, mixing with non-destructive Snapshots and Google Drive synchronization, salvaging a live band Take with non-destructive mistake surgery, capturing multi-camera 50 FPS studio and wireless Cave Companion mobile video with split-screen .mp4 and .fcpxml v1.9 multicam exports, jamming live with hardware floor loopers, Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments, Tempo-Synced effects, and the native Groovebox & Studio Sampler, running eyes-up dual-personality tracking on a Dual-Screen Pad Controller, and managing a live Stagebox FOH/IEM mix alongside scriptable caverec-cli automation.

3.1 Workflow 1: Full-Band Rehearsal Capture & Instant Reference Prints#

Studio Scenario: A four- or five-piece band gathers for a two-hour evening rehearsal. You want to record every song run-through across 12 to 18 channels without slowing down the room, mark strong sections on the fly, and hand every band member compact 24-bit .flac and 320 kbps .mp3 stereo mixes before they finish packing up their gear.

3.1.1 Rehearsal Capture Procedure#

  1. Launch the Session from Your Rehearsal Template:
    • Press CMD + O (macOS) or CTRL + O (Windows/Linux) to open the PROJECT modal.
    • Select your band's Project pill, click Template: XR18Base001 or Template: GuitarBassDrumTrio001 (or your custom saved room template), type a Session Name (Tuesday Night Rehearsal) and Session Tag (Rehearsal), and click New Session.
  2. Arm All Active Input Channels:
    • Press CMD + 2 (macOS) or CTRL + 2 (Windows/Linux) to view MIXER.
    • Confirm that CH01 through CH18 (or all active mic and DI channels) have their crimson Record Arm (R) buttons engaged (click R on each strip, or select a strip and press SHIFT + A).
    • Verify that OVERDUB in the Top Transport Deck is off (unlit) so each recording starts a fresh t = 0 Take.
  3. Dial a Quick Monitor and Live Print Balance:
    • While the band warms up, verify input levels average around -18 dBFS RMS with peaks around -6 dBFS.
    • Set channel faders and stereo pans (OverheadL/OverheadR, GuitarL/GuitarR, KeysL/KeysR), blend in AUX 1 REVERB (RVB) on snare and vocals, and engage TAPE SAT, the brickwall LIM (CEIL -0.3dB), and the 2-TRK PRINT button on the MST MASTER BUS strip. Because the live stereo Print records directly from the Master Bus output whenever 2-TRK PRINT is armed, this monitor balance becomes your immediate reference mix.
  4. Start Recording Song 1 (Take 001):
    • Just before the drummer counts in, press R (or click Record ● in the Top Deck).
    • Cave Recorder creates Take 001 at 00:00:00.000 and simultaneously writes raw 32-bit float pre-fader stems (Rec001) into Take001/rec/ and the live stereo Master Bus mix (Print001.wav) into Take001/mix/.
  5. Drop Cue Markers on the Fly (M):
    • Whenever a chorus groove locks in, a bridge arrangement changes, or a solo stands out during the performance, press M on the keyboard.
    • Cave Recorder drops a timestamped standalone marker (M005, M006, ...) at the exact live playhead sample without interrupting recording.
  6. Stop at the End of the Song (SPACE):
    • When the final chord rings out, press SPACE (or SHIFT + SPACE).
    • Cave Recorder closes all open audio files for Take 001 and automatically captures a post-recording console Snapshot (Auto-Save (Post-Recording)).
  7. Capture Subsequent Songs as Independent Takes (Take 002, Take 003, ...):
    • When the band counts in the next run-through or the next song, simply press R again.
    • Cave Recorder automatically increments to Take 002 with a brand-new 00:00:00.000 timeline origin. Repeat R, play the song, and press SPACE for every song of the night.
  8. Tag Keeper Takes and Convert Live Prints to .flac and .mp3:
    • At the end of rehearsal, press CMD + 5 (macOS) or CTRL + 5 (Windows/Linux) to open TAKES.
    • In the TAKES CATALOG, click Rename (or click the Take title inline) to assign a descriptive song tag (such as NewSong_Run1 or ChorusKeeper).
    • Click Export… on individual Takes (Convert Print to FLAC / MP3), or click FLAC ALL PRINTS and MP3 ALL PRINTS in the TAKES header bar to batch-encode every live stereo .wav Print to 24-bit lossless .flac and 320 kbps CBR .mp3 (with a Xing/Info seek header) and link both into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/. (If you adjusted faders after recording and want an updated offline render instead of the live Print, toggle FLAC and/or MP3 on the MST MASTER BUS strip and click BOUNCE to render an offline Mix001.<flac|mp3> Mixdown).
  9. Sync Reference Mixes to Bandmates' Phones and Browsers:
    • Click Upload Session Mixes in the TAKES header (or open the Top Deck CLOUD ▾ popover and click SYNC SESSION MIXES).
    • Cave Recorder uploads the compact .flac and .mp3 reference mixes to Google Drive in seconds so every band member can stream .mp3 mixes directly inside the Google Drive web browser preview player or download lossless .flac masters on the drive home.
Automatic FLAC and MP3 Encoding on Cloud Upload

Enable the AUTO-FLAC ON UPLOAD and AUTO-MP3 ON UPLOAD toggles in TAKES (CMD + 5 / CTRL + 5) or the Top Deck CLOUD ▾ popover. Whenever you click Upload Session Mixes or Upload Session Full, Cave Recorder automatically converts any uncompressed .wav Prints into 24-bit .flac and/or 320 kbps CBR .mp3 files and populates <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/ prior to uploading.

3.2 Workflow 2: Rescuing an Unrecorded Jam with 30-Minute Retroactive Capture (SAVE RETRO)#

Studio Scenario: Between rehearsed songs, the transport is stopped while the guitarist tunes. The drummer and bassist start an improvised groove, the rest of the band joins in, and eight minutes later they finish the best song idea of the night. Nobody pressed Record.

Because Cave Recorder continuously maintains a rolling 30-minute retroactive capture memory across all armed inputs whenever ● RETRO is active, the entire multi-channel performance is still in system memory waiting to be saved.

3.2.1 Retroactive Rescue Procedure#

  1. Keep ● RETRO Active and Channels Armed During Rehearsal:
    • At the start of your session, verify that the ● RETRO button in the Top Transport Deck is illuminated green and all live studio channels (CH01..CH18) have their crimson R (Record Arm) buttons engaged.
    • Even while the transport is stopped (■), Cave Recorder continuously retains the most recent 30 minutes of incoming 32-bit float audio from every armed channel in memory.
  2. Trigger Retroactive Capture (SAVE RETRO):
    • As soon as the unrecorded jam finishes (or even while the band is still playing), click the SAVE RETRO button in the Top Transport Deck, or press SHIFT + R.
  3. Verify the Rescued Take:
    • Cave Recorder immediately flushes the rolling multi-channel capture memory to disk as a new numbered Take (Take<NNN>), builds the multi-tier waveform overview, and switches the active console and timeline to the rescued Take.
  4. Trim Pre-Jam Room Chatter into a Clean Song Take (SPLIT TAKE):
    • Press CMD + 1 (macOS) or CTRL + 1 (Windows/Linux) to switch to TIMELINE.
    • Scrub or zoom (ZOOM + or =, or vertical/horizontal drag on the timeline ruler) to find the exact moment the drummer counted in the jam, and click to place the playhead just before the first beat.
    • Click SPLIT TAKE in the Timeline toolbar (or press M to drop a marker, open MARKERS with CMD + 4 / CTRL + 4, and click NEW TAKE -> END on that marker row).
    • Cave Recorder extracts the jam from that marker forward into its own clean 00:00:00.000 Take and lets you move the earlier tuning Take to the archived list via [⋯] -> Archive… (or convert/purge an unwanted retroactive Take) in TAKES (CMD + 5 / CTRL + 5).

3.3 Workflow 3: Multi-Mic Drum & Guitar Cab Phase Alignment (ALIGN ALL & Φ)#

Studio Scenario: You are tracking a full band across 18 channels (CH01 01KickIn, CH02 02SnrTp, CH03 03OvrhdL, CH04 04GtrAmp, CH05 TomRack, CH06 TomFloor, CH07 OverheadL, CH08 OverheadR, CH09 SpdifSynthL, CH10 SpdifSynthR, CH11 BassDi, CH12 BassAmp, CH13 GuitarL, CH14 GuitarR, through CH18 RoomAmbience). Because acoustic wavefronts from the kick and snare travel several feet through the air before reaching the overhead and room microphones, and because a bass amp microphone lags behind a direct Bass DI box, summing the raw channels causes phase cancellation that thins out low-end punch and smears transient focus.

3.3.1 Multi-Mic Phase Alignment Procedure#

  1. Record a 10-to-15 Second Full-Kit & Band Reference Pass:
    • Arm all drum and multi-miked instrument channels (R) in MIXER (CMD + 2 / CTRL + 2).
    • Press R and have the drummer play a 10-to-15 second groove that hits the kick, snare, toms, hi-hat, and cymbals clearly while the bassist and guitarist play locked eighth notes.
    • Press SPACE to stop recording.
  2. Verify the Timing Reference Channel (0us):
    • Look at the phase delay readout directly beneath each channel strip's top identifier badge (CH01 01KickIn shows -2.4dB 0us).
    • By default, CH01 (01KickIn or Overhead L) serves as the 0us acoustic timing anchor against which correlated channels are measured.
  3. Run Automatic Multi-Mic Phase Alignment (● ALIGN ALL):
    • Click the emerald ● ALIGN ALL button in the Top Transport Deck.
    • To align only a single channel strip (such as aligning CH12 BassAmp to CH11 BassDi), select that strip and click its individual Φ button. Both Trigger Global Multi-Mic Phase Align and Trigger Phase Align on Inspected Track can also be bound to custom keyboard shortcuts in KEYMAP (CMD + 8 / CTRL + 8).
    • To manually flip 180-degree polarity (Ø) on the currently inspected channel strip at any time, click Ø or press SHIFT + P while in MIXER.
  4. Inspect Sub-Sample Delay (µs) and Polarity (Ø) Corrections:
    • Cave Recorder cross-correlates the recorded multi-channel waveforms and engages the green Φ phase button and blue Ø polarity button where needed:
    • On CH02 02SnrTp, notice the readout updates to +1.5dB 420us with both polarity inversion (Ø blue) and phase delay (Φ green) engaged to lock the snare transient in phase with the kick and overheads.
    • On CH03 03OvrhdL, notice the readout updates to +0.0dB 1850us with Φ engaged to compensate for the acoustic propagation distance between the close mics and overheads.
  5. A/B Audition the Phase Alignment (PHASE A/B):
    • Press SPACE to play back the drum recording through your studio monitors.
    • Click PHASE A/B in the Top Deck to toggle global phase alignment active vs. bypassed.
    • Listen to the low-frequency weight of the kick drum, the body of the snare, and the phantom center image of the kit snap into focus when phase alignment is engaged. All subsequent Takes in the Session inherit these aligned delay and polarity settings automatically.
  6. Run the Two-Mode Polarity & Phase Maximizer (POLARITY MAX: Mode 1 Instant Binary & Mode 2 Multicore Allpass Solver):
    • Click POLARITY MAX in the Control Room bar for an immediate < 50 ms broadband polarity check across connected acoustic groups (such as all drum mics in Group 1 and a bass DI + mic'd bass cabinet pair in Group 2) via Mode 1: Instant Binary Polarity Maximizer, selecting Low-End Weight (30-200 Hz Punch), Broadband Loudness (ITU-R BS.1770-4 K-Weighted LUFS), Transient Crest & Impact (60 Hz - 6 kHz + Top-K Crest Re-Scoring), or Anti-Comb Spectral Smoothness. Your original manual Ø, delay, and allpass settings are automatically preserved for A/B comparison.
    • When mixing a dispersive ported bass cabinet (bass DI + mic'd cabinet) or an 8-mic drum kit where simple time delay cannot align both 60 Hz sub-bass resonance and 2.5 kHz stick attack, switch to Mode 2: Deep Multicore Spectral Phase & Allpass Solver (30 s to 30 min anytime budget).
    • Toggle [GAIN-MATCH AUDITION] on, click between [CANDIDATE A: PURE Ø - ZERO DISPERSION] (optimal 180° polarity flips only, 0 allpass stages, 0.0 us time shift), [CANDIDATE B: TIGHT LOW-END LOCK - MINIMAL POLES] (polarity plus at most 1st-order LF rotator and 1 low-frequency biquad allpass stage <= 250 Hz, group delay < 2.5 ms), [CANDIDATE C: DEEP MULTI-BAND ALLPASS] (polarity plus up to 5-stage allpass cascade, group delay <= 6.0 ms), and [CANDIDATE D: FULL WAVEFRONT + ALLPASS] (causal microsecond time-of-flight alignment 0..25,000 us on unlocked spot mics plus polarity and sparse allpass cascade) with click-free 10 ms crossfades, and click [APPLY SELECTED TO CONSOLE] to program the top-of-strip zero-slot 5-stage Phase Align Network across the console.

3.4 Workflow 4: Layered Guitar & Vocal Overdubs with Pass Lane Comping (OD)#

Studio Scenario: The band has tracked a solid rhythm section performance in Take 001. Now the guitarist or lead vocalist wants to loop the chorus section, record three alternate solo or vocal passes (Rec002-OD, Rec003-OD, Rec004-OD) inside Take 001, and select the best performance using Pass Lanes.

3.4.1 Overdub Tracking & Pass Lane Comping Procedure#

  1. Select the Target Take (TAKE 001):
    • Use < TAKE 001 > in the Top Deck (ALT + [ / ALT + ]) or click Load on Take 001 in TAKES (CMD + 5 / CTRL + 5) so the rhythm Take is loaded at 00:00:00.000.
  2. Disarm Rhythm Tracks and Arm Only the Overdub Channel:
    • In MIXER (CMD + 2 / CTRL + 2), click the crimson R buttons on the drum and bass strips (CH01..CH03, CH05..CH12) to disarm them so they play back their PASS 01 (Rec001) stems from disk.
    • On the target overdub channel (for example, CH04 04GtrAmp or CH17 LeadVocal), engage both R (Record Arm, or press SHIFT + A while the strip is selected in MIXER) and I (Input Monitor, or press SHIFT + I) so the performer hears their live input blended with playback.
  3. Latch OVERDUB and LOW-LATENCY:
    • Click OVERDUB in the Top Transport Deck (or press O) so the button illuminates bright crimson and the timecode readout confirms OVERDUB → TAKE 001.
    • Click LOW-LATENCY in Row 2 of the Top Deck so any high-latency plugins on non-armed buses are bypassed in the live monitoring path.
  4. Define the Section Loop Range (K, L & ⇄):
    • Press CMD + 1 (macOS) or CTRL + 1 (Windows/Linux) to open TIMELINE.
    • Place the playhead two bars before the solo or chorus entrance and press K (or click RANGE START (K)).
    • Place the playhead a bar after the section ends and press L (or click RANGE END (L)).
    • Press C (or click Cycle/Loop ⇄ in the Top Deck) to enable loop playback across the range.
  5. Record Multiple Overdub Passes (OD 02, OD 03, OD 04):
    • Press R to start overdub recording inside Take 001. While the rhythm tracks play back, Cave Recorder captures the new performance onto CH04 as Rec002-OD (displayed as OD 02) and automatically applies your calibrated roundtrip loopback offset (-640 smp (-13.3ms)).
    • Press SPACE at the end of the pass, return to the start of the range, and press R again to capture OD 03 (Rec003-OD) and OD 04 (Rec004-OD).
  6. Expand Pass Lanes in TIMELINE (E):
    • In TIMELINE (CMD + 1 / CTRL + 1), press E (or click EXPAND ALL PASSES in the timeline toolbar, or click the red pass-count pill v (2) on an individual track header) to expand the track's Pass Lanes. Press SHIFT + E (or click COLLAPSE ALL PASSES) at any time to fold them back into a single compact track row.
    • The top slice of the expanded track displays PASS 01 (BASE PASS), followed by stacked slices for each recorded Overdub Pass (OD 02, OD 03, OD 04, each badged OVERDUB with its sample span Span: 0..48000 smp and net record-offset -640 smp (-13.3ms)). Notice that the Mixer channel strip badge also updates to show OD 02 in amber when an Overdub Pass is active.
  7. Audition and Select Active Pass Lanes (Use PASS 01 / ★ OD 02):
    • The currently selected pass on a track is badged ACTIVE COMP LANE and displays a green star button (★ PASS 01 or ★ OD 02), while every other pass is badged STANDBY COMP LANE with a clickable Use PASS 01 or Use OD 02 button.
    • While looping playback (SPACE), click Use PASS 01, Use OD 02, or Use OD 03 on any Pass Lane row to promote that pass immediately as the active playback lane for the track.
    • To silence a pass temporarily without changing selection, click M (Mute) on that Pass Lane row, or click Del to remove a flawed pass from the Take.

3.5 Workflow 5: Mixing, Non-Destructive Snapshots & Band Cloud Sharing#

Studio Scenario: Tracking and overdub selection are complete. Now you want to shape a polished mix using Subgroup Buses and Aux Sends, save several mix variations as Snapshots, compare a vocal-up mix against an earlier Snapshot using Live Mix (LIVE MIX), render an offline Mixdown and Stem Bounces, and synchronize the project to Google Drive.

3.5.1 Bus Mixing, Snapshot A/B & Cloud Sync Procedure#

  1. Organize Channels into Subgroup Buses (DRUM BUS & INST BUS):
    • In MIXER (CMD + 2 / CTRL + 2), click the output routing selector (OUT: SUB 1 ▾) on all drum channels (CH01..CH08, CH18) to route them to SUB 1 (DRUM BUS).
    • Route synths, bass, guitars, and keys (CH09..CH16) to OUT: SUB 2 ▾ (INST BUS), and route lead vocals (CH17) directly to OUT: MST ▾ (MASTER BUS).
  2. Apply Bus Processing and Spatial Aux Sends (RVB & DLY):
    • Click SEL on the DRUM BUS strip to load its 8-slot processor rack into the Upper Inspector Wells.
    • In the 12-Band Parametric EQ well (2:12B EQ), sculpt a low-shelf boost around 60 Hz and a gentle presence lift at 4.5 kHz while watching the pre/post Dual-Trace RTA spectrum.
    • In the VCA Compressor well (3:VCA CMP), select a 4:1 ratio, engage the sidechain high-pass filter (HPF), and set MIX 50% for punchy New York-style parallel drum compression.
    • Use each channel's RVB and DLY send sliders (toggling POST for post-fader send operation) to feed AUX 1 REVERB (EMT 140 Plate zero-latency convolution reverb) and AUX 2 TAPE DLY (CAPSTAN TAPE echo with WOW 18%, DMP 4.2k, and PP ping-pong stereo widening).
  3. Save Named Mix Variations as Manual Snapshots (SNAP MANUAL):
    • Press CMD + S on macOS (CTRL + S on Windows and Linux) from any workspace view, or press CMD + 5 / CTRL + 5 to open TAKES and click SNAP MANUAL in the HISTORY toolbar, to capture your baseline mix as Snap 004 [MANUAL].
    • Return to MIXER (CMD + 2 / CTRL + 2) and try a more aggressive mix variation (for example, pushing DRIVE +4.5 dB on the Master Tape saturator and riding the lead guitar +2.0 dB).
  4. A/B Compare Historical Snapshots with Your Live Mix (A/B Live Mix):
    • In TAKES (CMD + 5 / CTRL + 5), scroll to the SNAPSHOTS table and click AUDITION SNAP 001 (or AUDITION SNAP 004).
    • Cave Recorder automatically backs up your live, unsaved console adjustments into Live Mix (LIVE MIX) and docks the global AUDITIONING SNAP 001 banner directly under the Top Deck across all workspace views.
    • While playback is rolling, click A/B Live Mix repeatedly to toggle instantaneously between the historical Snapshot and your live working mix with zero audio dropouts.
    • Click Return to Live Mix (or press BACKSPACE) to restore your live working mix, or click LOAD SNAPSHOT if you prefer the historical Snapshot and want to adopt it as the new working session state.
  5. Render Offline Mixdowns and Stem Bounces:
    • When your mix is finished, select FLAC (24-bit lossless), MP3 (320 kbps CBR), or both on the MST MASTER BUS strip in MIXER (CMD + 2 / CTRL + 2) and click BOUNCE to render an offline stereo Mixdown (Mix001.flac / Mix001.mp3) linked directly into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/ (with live progress and [✕] cancel visible in the Top Deck Async Job Status Bar), or trigger offline per-track Stem Bounces (Bounce001.wav) for archival delivery.
  6. Synchronize to Google Drive (Upload Session Mixes / Upload Session Full):
    • Click Upload Session Mixes in TAKES (CMD + 5 / CTRL + 5) to push all stereo .flac and .mp3 Prints and Mixdowns to Google Drive for rapid band review.
    • Click Upload Session Full to synchronize the entire session folder (including 32-bit float rec/ stems, snapshots/, and session history) so remote bandmates who have linked the project can open the full multitrack session on their own studio workstations.

3.6 Workflow 6: Live-Room Gain Calibration, Bleed Gating & Rescuing a Magic Band Take#

Studio Scenario: A stoner/psych-rock four-piece has just played an electrifying 9-minute live run-through in Take 003 with everyone in the same room. The groove and collective tempo push are unrepeatable, so re-recording the song is out of the question. However, the raw tracking session has five real-world rehearsal-room flaws:

  1. Preamplifier gains were set unevenly during warm-up.
  2. Loud snare rimshots are bleeding into the rack and floor tom microphones, while stacked fuzz pedals on CH13 GuitarL hum at -22 dBFS during stops even though the guitarist plays a whisper-quiet -34 dBFS clean fingerpicked bridge and holds a 4-second harmonic feedback bloom at the outro.
  3. One monster snare rimshot in the climax clipped the hardware ADC converter for 16 samples.
  4. The vintage bass amp picked up 60 Hz mains buzz.
  5. The guitarist hit one wrong chord in bar 42 of Chorus 2.

3.6.1 Step-by-Step Live-Room Cleanup & Mistake Surgery Procedure#

  1. One-Click Console Gain Calibration (CALIBRATE TRIMS):
    • Open MIXER (CMD/CTRL + 2) and click CALIBRATE TRIMS in the Control Room bar. Cave Recorder scans the active Pass stems of Take 003 and sets every channel's input trim so average playing level hits -18.0 dBFS RMS with a -6.0 dBFS peak ceiling clamp.
  2. Isolate Toms with Drum Bleed ([LRN] & Dynamic Decay LPF):
    • Select CH05 TomRack, assign the Noise Gate in its processor rack, and switch the gate mode to Drum Bleed.
    • Solo a single rack tom hit on the timeline and click [LRN]. The resonant key filter (55 Hz to 350 Hz, default 110 Hz, Q = 4.0) locks onto the drum's 118 Hz fundamental pitch while the differential detector rejects snare and hi-hat spill. As each tom hit rings out, the dynamic decay low-pass filter sweeps from 20 kHz down to 250 Hz..800 Hz (default 380 Hz), removing harsh cymbal wash from the tom tail. Repeat on CH06 TomFloor.
  3. Tame Fuzz Roar While Preserving Clean Picking & Feedback (Amp Dynamic):
    • Select CH13 GuitarL and switch its Noise Gate to Amp Dynamic.
    • During the -34 dBFS clean fingerpicked bridge, the autocorrelation pitch periodicity detector (H > 0.65) automatically engages Whisper Clean Lock, keeping every quiet note wide open without manual automation.
    • During the outro's 4-second harmonic feedback swell, Feedback Bloom Lock (H > 0.80, release 1.5 s..5.0 s, default 2.5 s) holds the gate open until the guitarist slams the final palm-mute stop, where Palm-Mute Clamp silences the 60 Hz fuzz roar in 15 ms..40 ms (default 18 ms..22 ms) along a click-free S-curve. Enable HF Tame to shelf down > 3.5 kHz fuzz fizz on fading chord tails.
  4. Level the Live Vocal Without Boosting Drum Spill (Vocal Rider + De-Esser):
    • On CH17 LeadVocal, enable Vocal Rider (Target -18 dBFS, Range ±6 dB) with Breath / Bleed Freeze set to -46 dBFS so the fader rides quiet verses and loud choruses smoothly but freezes whenever the singer steps back from the mic between lines. Follow with De-Esser to catch 120 Hz P/B plosives and 6.5 kHz sibilance before the Opto compressor.
  5. Reconstruct the Clipped Snare Rimshot ([REPAIR CLIPPING]):
    • Switch to TIMELINE (CMD/CTRL + 1), select CH02 02SnrTp, bracket the clipped rimshot with K and L, and click [REPAIR CLIPPING]. Cave Recorder's spectral waveform interpolation reconstructs the missing 16-sample transient peak cleanly.
  6. Strip 60 Hz Mains Buzz (Hum Canceller) & Graft the Clean Bar 42 Chord ([PATCH FROM SOURCE...]):
    • On CH12 BassAmp, enable the 60 Hz 12-Harmonic Comb Hum Canceller (45 Hz..65 Hz fundamental, Q = 20..100, default Q = 60) to notch out 60 Hz .. 720 Hz transformer buzz without thinning out the bass cabinet low-mids.
    • On CH13 GuitarL, bracket the 1-bar wrong chord in Chorus 2 (K and L), click [PATCH FROM SOURCE...], and point to the matching bar in Chorus 1. Cave Recorder micro-aligns the phase and transient correlation within ±50 ms and crossfades the clean chord in place while leaving the original Rec001.wav stem untouched on disk.
  7. Check Translation on the Control Room Monitor Bar & Bounce:
    • Audition the mix through the MONITOR: Control Room Bar (SUB, MID + MONO, STEREO DIFF, and AUTO LEVEL bypass) while verifying that the Master Bus Broadcast Metering Suite (METER SUITE) shows -11.5 LUFS Short-Term, -0.5 dBTP True Peak, and a punchy 8.5 dB PSR crest factor. Click BOUNCE with FLAC and MP3 enabled to publish the rescued live performance to _Mixes/.

3.7 Workflow 7: Multi-Camera Rehearsal Video Capture, Cave Companion Mobile Camera Nodes & Split-Screen Video Mixdowns#

Studio Scenario: Your band wants to capture a live rehearsal performance on video from three angles (a desktop USB/HDMI overhead drum camera, plus two bandmates' companion devices mounted on mic stands as wireless 1080p50 Cave Companion camera nodes), trigger recording remotely from across the room, and export both a 3-camera split-screen .mp4 video with console-mixed audio and a Final Cut .fcpxml v1.9 multicam timeline before leaving the studio.

3.7.1 Step-by-Step Multi-Camera & Mobile Companion Procedure#

  1. Pair Bandmates' Companions in the REMOTE Workspace (CMD/CTRL + 0):
    • Click ● REMOTE in Row 2 of the Top Deck (or press CMD/CTRL + 0) to open the dedicated Cave Companion workspace on the desktop workstation. Cave Recorder advertises itself automatically over local Wi-Fi via Bonjour (_caverec._udp) and UDP discovery, while also displaying a large, integer-aligned caverec://pair QR code (with a one-click ENLARGE QR studio-distance lightbox), a one-click COPY PAIRING URL clipboard button, a 6-digit Studio PIN fallback, and app download QR codes for Android and iOS.
    • Each bandmate can either scan the studio QR code inside Cave Companion or tap PAIR ON WI-FI when their tablet or phone auto-discovers the studio workstation on the local network, then verify the matching 6-digit MATCH CODE and click APPROVE right in the global desktop Top Deck approval banner without leaving MIXER. Assign Full Control + Camera to the drummer's companion device (so the drummer can start and stop Takes from behind the kit) and Camera + Player to the guitarist's companion device.
  2. Verify 50 FPS CFR Lock & Calibrate Camera Latency (3-Second 4-Pulse Flash, Full-Window Flash or Clapper):
    • Arm the desktop USB/HDMI drum camera (Cam01-Drums) at 1080p50 CFR (960 audio samples/frame at 48.0 kHz, or 30/60 FPS CFR fallback on cameras without 50 Hz modes). If calibrating the camera for the first time, click ● CAMERA and run the 3-Second Camera Latency Calibration modal using 4-Pulse Vernier Flash (external cameras), Full-Window White Flash (built-in laptop webcams facing the room), or Interactive Clapper / Hand Clap so Cave Recorder stores its exact sub-frame optical latency.
    • On both companion devices, switch to the CAMERA tab and verify the green Clock Lock Badge shows < 0.5 ms wireless clock lock alongside live 16-channel peak meters. Arm the mobile camera so the HUD displays CAMERA ARMED • AUTO-REC WITH DAW (both Full Control + Camera and Camera + Player companions record and upload automatically when the desktop DAW tracks a Take, and Full Control devices can also tap RECORD DAW TAKE / STOP TAKE & SYNC directly from the camera HUD). For first-time optical calibration, open the collapsible FLASH SYNC ▾ drawer and trigger the Rear LED Torch 4-Pulse Calibration, which measures sensor delay directly against wireless studio-clock timestamps with no phone speaker or microphone audio loop.
  3. Trigger Multi-Track Audio + Multi-Camera Video Recording Remotely:
    • From behind the drum kit, the drummer taps Record (●) on the Cave Companion TRANSPORT or MIXER Top Deck (or RECORD DAW TAKE in CAMERA).
    • Desktop Cave Recorder creates Take 001 at 00:00:00.000, turns the Top-Deck ● CAMERA LED crimson along with the red Recording Tally Border across the desktop Video Monitor and both mobile camera screens, and records up to 32 channels of 32-bit float audio stems (rec/*.wav), the live Master Bus stereo Print (mix/Print001.wav), and sample-locked CFR video streams (video/*.mp4 + .vididx frame indices).
  4. Automatic Wireless Camera Ingest When Recording Stops:
    • When the song ends, the drummer taps Stop (■) (or STOP TAKE & SYNC).
    • Both companion devices immediately finalize their local 1080p50 .mp4 and .vididx index files and transfer them automatically over local Wi-Fi (when AUTO-PUSH ON STOP is active, with integrity verification and automatic resume) into <TakeFolder>/video/ on the desktop workstation.
    • As each camera transfer completes, Cave Recorder automatically ingests the new angle into Take 001's stacked multi-lane Video Timeline Strip time-anchored frame-accurate filmstrip (with 35 mm sprocket tick rails and 16:9 Frame Loupe skimming) in TIMELINE (CMD/CTRL + 1). If any angle needs a fine visual tweak, drag its Camera Trim Offset slider while watching the real-time Video Monitor.
  5. Render a Split-Screen .mp4 Video Mixdown & .fcpxml v1.9 Multicam Timeline:
    • Open Export… on Take 001 in TAKES (CMD/CTRL + 5) to launch the Export Video Mixdown & Multicam FCPXML modal.
    • Select the 3-Cam Band layout (or Side-by-Side Crop with horizontal camera pan adjustments, Side-by-Side 16:9, or Quad 2x2) and click RENDER VIDEO MIXDOWN (.MP4). Cave Recorder's split-screen video compositor and hardware video encoder render <TakeFolder>/mix/GF_20261020-1_Take001_VideoMix001.mp4 (combining 50 FPS video with AAC-LC stereo console audio) alongside gapless 48.0 kHz .flac and .mp3 audio prints, linking them into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/.
    • Click EXPORT MULTICAM FCPXML (.FCPXML) to write both a stacked split-screen timeline (<adjust-crop>, <adjust-transform>, and <timeMap> clock-drift tables) and a native <mc-clip> multi-camera switching timeline into <TakeFolder>/export/.
  6. Review Multi-Angle Video & Audio Prints on Mobile (PLAYER & Google Drive Sync):
    • Bandmates open the PLAYER tab in the Cave Companion app (or download from Google Drive Cloud Sync, which automatically skips already-uploaded files and resumes interrupted transfers) to switch live between all three camera angles (Cam01-Drums, Cam02-GtrMobile, Cam03-RoomMobile) and .flac/.mp3 audio prints with sample-locked audio-video playback.

3.8 Workflow 8: Live Looping, Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments & Groovebox Jamming#

Studio Scenario: You are jamming in the rehearsal room with a guitar floor looper, a USB MIDI keyboard driving a Pre-Tape virtual electric piano, and Cave Recorder's native Groovebox & Studio Sampler controlled either on desktop or wirelessly from a tablet running Cave Companion. You want all effects and drums locked tightly to your live groove, zero double-triggering when playing back recorded Takes, and full 30-minute SAVE RETRO rescue if an improvised jam catches fire.

3.8.1 Step-by-Step Gridless Sync, Pre-Tape Synth & Groovebox Procedure#

  1. Assign Pre-Tape Instruments on Console Strips ([INST]):
    • In MIXER (CMD/CTRL + 2), click the input selector (IN 01 ▾) on CH01, switch to the INSTRUMENT tab, and choose [NATIVE] CAVE DRUM MACHINE. (Optionally assign a second strip's OUT breakout to STEM for Kick or Snare so that drum voice gets its own dedicated console strip EQ, compressor, Aux Sends, and raw .wav stem.)
    • On CH02, switch the input overlay to INSTRUMENT, select a CLAP or macOS Audio Unit (AU) synthesizer or electric piano, choose your MIDI input port and channel filter (OMNI or CH 01..16), and confirm STEREO width. Click GUI in Zone 2 whenever you want to tweak the synth's floating editor window.
    • Arm (R) and enable monitoring (I) on your guitar, synth, and drum strips, and verify ● RETRO is green in the Top Deck so stereo retroactive memory captures every note live.
  2. Establish Live Groove Tempo (● MIDI or STUDIO CLK):
    • Option A (Hardware Floor Looper Master): Click ● MIDI in Top Deck Row 2 to open MIDI SYNC & HARDWARE CALIBRATION, pick your loop length (2 BARS or 4 BARS), and stomp your MIDI-learned footswitch (CC 80 by default) to start and close your guitar loop. Outbound MIDI Clock stays silent while you record the loop and locks immediately on Stomp 2 (Emerald LED).
    • Option B (4-Tap Count-In): Press T four times inside the MIDI Sync modal (optionally latching AUTO-REC ON BEAT 1 so Take recording begins automatically on Beat 1).
    • Option C (Groovebox Tempo Master): Press CMD/CTRL + 6 to open GROOVEBOX, confirm STUDIO CLK is lit, dial in your tempo (BPM), and press SEQ PLAY to roll a live rehearsal jam feeding the 30-minute ● RETRO memory without even starting a Take yet.
  3. Sync Console Delay & Modulation to the Room Groove ([SYNC] & [LCK]):
    • On the AX2 Aux 2 Delay strip, engage SYNC so the delay time switches from milliseconds (TM) to musical subdivisions (DV, defaulting to dotted eighth 1/8D). Try toggling 0.5x or 2.0x in ● MIDI to hear authentic analog capstan pitch glides follow your tempo change.
    • Insert 4-Mode Modulation on your electric piano or guitar strip and engage both SYNC (default 1/2 bar) and LCK so optical phaser or harmonic tremolo swells lock smoothly to Beat 1 with zero clicks.
  4. Perform Live Drum Variations (Desktop or Cave Companion Tablet GROOVEBOX):
    • In GROOVEBOX (or on a paired tablet's GROOVEBOX tab), click STASH KIT to bookmark your base drum sound before mangling the kit live with CTRL ALL, MORPH, HOLD FILL, and momentary SLIP BEAT-REPEAT (1/8, 1/16, 1/32, REV GRAIN, TAPE STOP). Click RELOAD KIT (Q:BAR) to snap the entire kit back cleanly on the next downbeat.
    • If you want to audition a different Factory Kit across the pinned METRONOME preset or the symmetric 12-kit [POCKET | CLUB] 2-bank suite (STUDIO ANALOG, DESERT ROCK, SOUL POCKET, BOOM BAP, MOTORIK DRY, MODAL METAL, TECHNO PUNCH, DEEP SUB ELECTRO, BREAKS 174, HALFTIME SUB, PSY MATRIX, and ACID & FUNK) mid-jam, keep +GROOVE turned OFF so swapping drum and bass sounds preserves all 64 of your Patterns and 16 Scenes untouched.
    • To add a live or sequenced monophonic bassline alongside the kit, select an ANALOG BASS slot (such as slot 12 ANALOG BASS in STUDIO ANALOG or SOUL POCKET, or 11 LADDER FUNK and 12 ACID SQUELCH in ACID & FUNK). Drag vertically on active bass steps to dial 12-TET pitches (holding SHIFT for octave leaps) or drag horizontally in 2D mode to paint tied notes, or play the focused bass voice directly from an external MIDI keyboard with MIDI: CHRM active while drum pads stay silenced. Break the bass lane out to its own STEM console strip whenever you want dedicated console EQ, compression, or Aux Sends on the bassline.
  5. Sample Live Rehearsal Moments & Slice Them in the STUDIO SAMPLER (GROOVEBOX -> SAMPLER):
    • To grab a live drum break, guitar chord swell, or percussion loop without creating extra Take clutter, either bracket a recorded phrase in TIMELINE (K..L) and click -> SAMPLER (DRY PASS for instant < 20 ms stem extraction or POST-FX for a rendered console bounce), or switch to the SAMPLER tab inside GROOVEBOX (CMD/CTRL + 6), open RECORD, choose any TRACK, SUBGROUP, AUX BUS, MASTER, or ADC IN source (POST-FX default), and capture directly with THRESHOLD (10 ms pre-roll), BAR SYNC (1B..16B), or MANUAL trigger.
    • Switch to SLICE, sweep SENSITIVITY in TRANSIENT mode (SuperFlux onset detector tuned for unisolated rehearsal rooms and amp bleed) or tap pads live in LIVE PAD mode, then click APPLY TO KIT (spreading up to 16 chops across Groovebox pads with automatic Choke Group assignment) or APPLY TO TRACK (SLICE-LOCK across up to 64 slices on one track with 1-click LINEAR LOCKS or RANDOM LOCKS). Shape any slice with the 2 x 4 macros (Pitch, Start / Slice, Length, Attack, Decay / Rel, Filter / Tune, Reso / Fdbk, Grit / Crush), DJ FILTER / COMB RES, and per-voice LFO, or commit CROP, NORM, BPM FIT stretch, or COMMIT FX BOUNCE with full reversible Undo managed via the Sample History (N)… drawer.
  6. Print Clean Audio Pass Stems & Play Back with Pass Isolation:
    • Punch Record (R) mid-jam (or press SHIFT + R for SAVE RETRO rescue). Cave Recorder prints the Groovebox (including any STUDIO SAMPLER voices), any individual STEM breakouts, the stereo Pre-Tape virtual instrument, and your live guitars as standard 32-bit float .wav Pass stems inside Take001/rec/.
    • When you disarm (R off) and disable monitoring (I off) on the Groovebox and virtual instrument strips and press Play (SPACE), Cave Recorder plays back the exact recorded .wav stems (preserving every live CTRL ALL, Scene jump, Sampler chop, and Slip Beat-Repeat move) while automatically silencing the live synth and sequencer so instruments never double-trigger. Idle virtual instruments drain their natural tails to -120 dBFS and enter INST: SLEEP at 0% CPU automatically.

3.9 Workflow 9: Eyes-Up Rehearsal & Tracking with a Dual-Screen Studio Pad Surface#

Studio Scenario: You want to stay hands-on at your Dual-Screen Pad Controller during band rehearsal and studio tracking, building beats and monophonic basslines in [DRUM STUDIO], flipping in one stroke to [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] to ride console balances, adjust Stagebox mic preamps, start a full-band Disk Take, drop live Cue Markers and Loop Ranges on the fly, and even drop out the drum machine mid-Take without stopping the multitrack recorder.

3.9.1 Step-by-Step Dual-Personality Performance & Tracking Procedure#

  1. Build the Groove Eyes-Up in [DRUM STUDIO]:
    • Confirm ● CONTROLLER is active in [DRUM STUDIO] mode (Emerald LED in Top Deck Row 2, or press SHIFT + CHANNEL on hardware).
    • Tap BROWSE to audition the pinned METRONOME kit or any of the 12 [POCKET | CLUB] factory kits (keeping F7: +GROOVE off when swapping sounds over an existing pattern).
    • Play all 16 voices live in PAD MODE (F2: FIXED VEL for uniform velocity, F3: 16 VEL to spread 16 stepped velocities of the focused voice across all 16 pads, F4: AUTO-FOCUS, or NOTE REPEAT for pressure-driven hi-hat and snare rolls where > 85% pad pressure triggers Accent).
    • Press SHIFT + PAD MODE (KEYBOARD) on an ANALOG BASS voice to play legato 1V/oct basslines across the 16 pads (contiguous 16-semitone default or folded musical scales via E1: SCALE and E2 / F5 layout mode, plus ARP via NOTE REPEAT in KEYBOARD mode).
    • Tap REC ([● PAT OVR] in cyan) to overdub live finger drumming or bass notes directly into the active Pattern with quantized or unquantized timing (QUANTIZE snaps micro-nudge to 0%, SHIFT + QUANTIZE tightens by 50%). Remember that REC in [DRUM STUDIO] only records Pattern Overdubs and never starts or stops a Disk Take.
    • Press STEP MODE to toggle the 64-step sequencer grid: turn bare E1..E8 to edit step Velocity, Gate, Micro-Nudge, Note, Tie/Slide, Flam/Ratchet, and Condition, or hold any step pad and turn E1..E8 to write per-step macro Parameter Locks (hold ERASE and touch an encoder to clear a single lock).
    • Hold ALL ([CTRL ALL], or ALL + F1 to pin) while turning E1..E8 to sweep filter cutoff or decay across every unmuted drum voice at once, or hold ALL + NOTE REPEAT to fire live Slip Beat-Repeat fills (Pads 1..6 divisions, Pad 7: REV GRAIN, Pad 8: TAPE STOP) while true song phase continues underneath. Bookmark your starting kit first with F5: STASH KIT and snap back immediately via F6: RELOAD KIT (or quantized to the next bar downbeat via SHIFT + F6).
    • Press bare SAMPLING in [DRUM STUDIO] to open the dual-screen STUDIO SAMPLER (F1: RECORD | F2: EDIT | F3: SLICE | F4: ZONE) with full-sample overview on the Left Screen, split zero-crossing zoom (E5 Start / E6 End) on the Right Screen, live pad-tap chopping on unlit pads, and F8: APPLY to assign slices to Kit or Track. Press SHIFT + SAMPLING (or CHANNEL -> F3: STEM PATCH) whenever you want the Pre-Tape STEM & SYNC breakout view.
  2. Flip to [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] for Stagebox Gains & Mix Balance (SHIFT + CHANNEL):
    • Press SHIFT + CHANNEL (or SHIFT + PLUG-IN to open the visual Surface Picker, then F8). Both screens immediately frame themselves in 4 px Console Burgundy (#962836) so you know at a glance that the surface now drives the Mix Console and Disk Take Transport.
    • Press MIX twice to flip into STAGEBOX PREAMPS & +48V (framed in 4 px Warm Preamp Copper). Dial up to 8 Stagebox mic preamp gains in parallel with E1..E8 (SHIFT + Turn for 0.5 dB precision) and hold any soft key F1..F8 for 600 ms to safely engage +48V phantom power on condenser mics.
    • Press MIX again to return to MAIN FADERS (using the universal [M][S][R] Solo Gold tally styling), bank across Tracks 1..32, Subgroups 1..16, Aux Returns 1..8, and Master via GROUPS A..H, and hold MUTE, SOLO, or REC + Pads 1..16 (or Hold + F1 to pin) to arm band tracks cleanly.
  3. Start a Guarded Disk Take & Drop Live Markers/Ranges:
    • Tap bare REC in [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] (with BROWSE -> F8: OVERDUB or E8: REC MODE off for a brand-new t = 0 Session Take, or on for a track-level Overdub Pass). Both displays switch to a Crimson ● TAKE REC header badge.
    • Drop Live Cue Markers (PAD MODE): Press PAD MODE (Cyan) and tap any unlit pad during the live Take to stamp a cue marker (M001..M016) at the rolling Playhead without interrupting recording.
    • Capture Live Song Sections (SCENE) & Send to Sampler: Press SCENE (Amber) and tap an unlit pad (Pads 2..16) once at the start of the chorus (RANGE START) and once at the end (RANGE END) to create a labeled Range on the fly. Holding any lit Range pad lets you send that phrase straight into the Studio Sampler via F5: -> SAMPLER (Dry Pass) or F6: POST-FX -> SMP (Post-FX Bounce), or press SAMPLING in [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] to open CONSOLE CAPTURE & RESAMPLE (F1: RESAMPLE STRIP, F2: RESAMPLE BUS, F3: RANGE -> SAMPLER, F7: RETRO 30M).
    • Perform Mid-Take Drum Dropouts Safely: Press SHIFT + CHANNEL back into [DRUM STUDIO] while the band is still rolling. While a Disk Take is recording, pressing bare PLAY in [DRUM STUDIO] toggles a clean Drum Sequencer Dropout/Re-Entry without stopping the multitrack Disk Take.
  4. Stop Cleanly, Comp Pass Lanes & Audition Console Snapshots:
    • Return to [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] (SHIFT + CHANNEL) and stop the Disk Take intentionally via F8: END TAKE, SHIFT + PLAY, or SHIFT + REC (bare PLAY and bare REC are locked by the Active Take Stop Guard so an accidental bump can never ruin a great take, while pressing SHIFT + ERASE twice arms and confirms discarding a false start).
    • Press PATTERN (PASS COMPING) and tap Pads 1..16 during playback or Cycle Loop (SHIFT + Tap a lit Range pad in SCENE) to audition PASS 01 vs. OD 02..OD 16 on the focused track clicklessly.
    • Press BROWSE (SNAPSHOTS & TAKES) to switch active Takes directly on the Left Screen (E1, or browse and confirm with Jog Wheel + Push) and capture (F5) or audition (F6) Console Snapshots on the Right Screen (while auditioning, F7 switches to A/B LIVE and F8 switches to LIVE MIX).

3.10 Workflow 10: Live Stagebox FOH/IEM Mixing, Virtual Soundcheck & Scriptable Studio Automation (STAGEBOX & caverec-cli)#

Studio Scenario: Your band plays live through an XR18 / XR18V2 digital stagebox feeding both room PA speakers and four personal in-ear monitor buses (BUS 1..4) while Cave Recorder captures raw 18-channel multitrack Takes over USB. After soundcheck, you want each musician to dial their own IEM mix safely from their phone without touching Main PA faders, run a Virtual Soundcheck against Take 001 once the band leaves the stage, and verify your final Mixdown loudness and spectral balance with caverec-cli.

3.10.1 Step-by-Step Stagebox Live Mix, Virtual Soundcheck & CLI Workflow#

  1. Connect & Sync Channel Labels in STAGEBOX (CMD/CTRL + 9):
    • Click ● STAGEBOX in Row 2 of the Top Deck and connect via SCAN /xinfo in 4. SCENES & SETUP. Remember that connecting never overwrites live hardware settings.
    • In 2. ROUTING, verify USB SENDS (1-18) shows Copper AIN on all active recording channels (or click 1:1 RAW ANALOG) so your multitrack Take stems record dry, untouched microphone signals regardless of PA EQ or compression.
    • In 1. MIXER, click MIXER → STAGEBOX to push your Cave Recorder track names and colors onto the stagebox scribble strips.
  2. Build Personal Monitor Mixes & Hand Out Safe MY MONITOR Access:
    • In 1. MIXER, click BUS 1 through BUS 4 in the SENDS ON FADERS row (the fader caps turn amber and the exit banner displays EXIT SENDS ON FADERS) to dial initial wedge/IEM balances, then click OFF to return to the MAIN LR FADER LAYER.
    • In 4. SCENES & SETUP, assign each bandmate's paired Cave Companion device to MY MONITOR pinned to their assigned monitor bus (BUS 1..6). Musicians can adjust their personal instrument levels, sweep MORE ME, and raise AUX USB backing/click level with zero exposure to +48V phantom power, Main PA faders, or routing. Keep FULL MIXER protected behind MIXER LOCK for the front-of-house engineer's tablet.
  3. Ring Out Wedges with 100-bin RTA & 31-Band GEQ, Then Run VIRTUAL SOUNDCHECK:
    • Select MAIN LR or BUS 1..6 in 1. MIXER to open the docked Stagebox DSP Inspector with live 100-bin RTA behind the 4/6-band PEQ and 31-Band GEQ / TruEQ. Notch feedback resonances cleanly and patch vocal plate reverb or tap-tempo delay in 3. FX RACK.
    • Once you have captured a 2-minute live Take 001 and the musicians step offstage, open 2. ROUTING -> CH INPUTS & VSC, click VIRTUAL SOUNDCHECK, and press SPACE to play Take 001 back through the stagebox's hardware DSP, FX rack, and PA speakers. Fine-tune every EQ, gate, compressor, and monitor bus calmly, save the finished setup into <SessionFolder>/stagebox_scene.json via CAPTURE HARDWARE -> SESSION, and click 1:1 RAW ANALOG before the band returns to the stage.
  4. Automate Metering, Phase Audits & Offline Renders via caverec-cli:
    • From any terminal (or Python script using extras/python/caverec.py), attach directly to your running Cave Recorder session (--live) or process a closed session offline at 20x–100x speed (--offline --session <dir>), then consult Section 8.6 in Chapter 8 for the complete 30-command CLI, sample-clocked Probe pipeline, POSIX FIFO bridge, Python client, and 6 embedded Studio Engineering Skills reference:
caverec-cli --live state summary --json
caverec-cli --live meter capture --range 0:10..0:40 --meters lufs,true_peak,crest,phase --json
caverec-cli --offline --session GF/GF_20261020-1_Rehearsal bounce mixdown --take 1 --flac --mp3
Part II · Chapter 4

Mix Console, Stagebox Mixer, Signal Flow & Channel Strips

Dynamic console topology (up to 32 mono, stereo-linked, Pre-Tape Virtual Instrument, or Drum Stem Breakout input tracks, 16 Subgroup Buses, and 8 Aux Returns), universal [M][S][R] Mute Amber, Solo Gold, and Record Crimson order across all four surfaces, 3-tab Input Routing (MONO, STEREO, INSTRUMENT), Master Bus Zone 2 HW OUT stagebox monitor faders and mutes, the full-featured desktop STAGEBOX workspace (1. MIXER with SENDS ON FADERS, MUTE GRP, Auto-Mix X/Y, and pinned MAIN LR / SOLO PHONES, 2. ROUTING 4-domain crosspoint matrix with 1:1 RAW ANALOG and VIRTUAL SOUNDCHECK, 3. FX RACK with 55 hardware FX, 4. SCENES & SETUP with stagebox_scene.json dual persistence and 64-slot hardware snapshots, and docked PEQ / 100-bin RTA / 31-Band GEQ inspector), automatic trim calibration, top-of-strip phase alignment, multi-instance reorderable 8-slot racks, Channel Strip large processor views, Control Room Monitor Bar, Broadcast Metering Suite, and [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] control on a Studio Pad Surface.

The Cave Recorder Mixer (CMD + 2 on macOS, CTRL + 2 on Windows and Linux) models an in-line large-format studio recording and mixing desk, paired with a full-featured STAGEBOX hardware mixer workspace (CMD/CTRL + 9) for live FOH, IEM, and Virtual Soundcheck control over digital stageboxes. Every input channel, subgroup bus, stereo auxiliary return, and master bus stage is visible on a single dark-chassis surface using Plain Studio Language and a universal [M] (Mute Amber) -> [S] (Solo Gold) -> [R] (Record Crimson) control order across Desktop, Mobile Phone, Tablet, and Dual-Screen Pad Controller surfaces.

This chapter details the end-to-end audio signal path from physical preamplifiers to disk stems and main monitors, the seven functional zones of an Input Track channel strip, Subgroup Buses, Aux Returns, the pinned Master Bus (HW OUT | TAPE), the Control Room Monitor Bar and Broadcast Metering Suite, precision fader gestures, [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] pad-controller operation, and the complete 4-tab desktop STAGEBOX workspace.

4.1 Console Architecture & End-to-End Signal Flow#

Understanding where audio is tapped for multitrack disk capture versus monitor and bus mixing is fundamental to operating Cave Recorder with confidence during live band tracking.

+====================================================================+
|             CAVE RECORDER END-TO-END CONSOLE SIGNAL FLOW           |
+====================================================================+
  PHYSICAL AUDIO INPUT (IN 01..32), PRE-TAPE VIRTUAL INSTRUMENT (INST),
  OR DRUM MACHINE VOICE STEM BREAKOUT (STEM)
         |
         v
  [Input Trim (TRM: -24.0 to +24.0 dB / CALIBRATE TRIMS -18 dBFS)]
         |
         v
  [Polarity Invert (Ø: 180°)] -> [Sub-Sample Delay (Φ: 0..50,000 us)]
         |
         v
  [Zero-Slot Phase Align Network (5-Stage Allpass Rotator, 10 ms X-Fade)]
         |
         +-------------------------------+
         | (Armed [R] + Record)          | (When Input Mon [I] is OFF)
         v                               v
  +=============================+ +==================================+
  | RAW PRE-FADER STEM RECORDER | | DISK PASS LANE PLAYBACK READER   |

4.1.1 Dual-Path Capture: Raw Pre-Insert Stems Plus Live Processed Prints#

In traditional rehearsal spaces and project studios, engineers face a dilemma when tracking a full band:

  1. The Safe But Uninspiring Approach: Record flat tracks with zero processing so nothing can be ruined by an overly aggressive compressor or EQ setting, leaving the band with dry, unmixed rough bounces at the end of the night.
  2. The Inspiring But Risky Approach: Print heavy compression, EQ, and tape saturation directly onto the multitrack stems, risking permanent distortion or pumping if a guitarist boosts a pedal mid-song.

Cave Recorder resolves this dilemma through a split capture topology:

  • Raw Pre-Fader Multitrack Stems (<TakeFolder>/rec/): Every armed Input Track (R) writes its 32-bit floating-point WAV file (Rec001 Base Pass or Rec002-OD Overdub Pass) immediately after Input Trim (TRM), Polarity (Ø), and Phase Alignment (Φ), before the 8-slot insert rack and channel fader. You can dial in aggressive 8:1 drum compression, heavy tape drive, high-pass filters, or external CLAP and macOS Audio Unit plugins on the console during rehearsal knowing the underlying multitrack stem on disk remains 100% clean and unclipped.
  • Concurrent Live Stereo Master Print (<TakeFolder>/mix/): Simultaneously, while the transport is recording a Take, the Master Bus (2-TRK enabled) captures the complete post-fader, post-subgroup, post-reverb, and post-limiter stereo mix in real time to a Print<NNN> WAV file with automatic Plugin Delay Compensation (PDC) latency trimming. Selecting FLAC and/or MP3 and clicking BOUNCE on the Master Bus renders a 24-bit .flac mix file, a 320 kbps CBR .mp3 mix file, or both simultaneously and links them into the Project's _Mixes/ folder for immediate band sharing and cloud sync, while you retain every raw multitrack stem for later remixing or offline stem bouncing (covered in Chapter 7: Session Reel, Mixdowns, Snapshots, Disk Layout & Cloud Sync).
Input Trim (TRM), Polarity (Ø), and Phase (Φ) Feed the Stem Recorder

Because TRM, Ø, and Φ sit upstream of the multitrack stem tap, calibrating preamp gain mismatches and aligning multi-mic drum phase at the top of the channel strip ensures your recorded stems are already phase-coherent and properly gain-staged on disk. All downstream insert slots (TAPE, 12B EQ, VCA CMP, PLUGIN), Aux Sends, Faders, and Subgroup processors remain non-destructive during playback and remixing.

4.2 Input Track Channel Strips & Dynamic Console Topology (0..32 Tracks)#

Cave Recorder supports a dynamic console topology of 0 to 32 mono or stereo-linked Input Track channel strips (CH01 through CH32) alongside 0 to 16 stereo Subgroup Buses (SUB 1 through SUB 16), 0 to 8 stereo Auxiliary Return Buses (AUX 1 through AUX 8), and the Master Bus (MST MASTER BUS):

  • Adding & Removing Strips (+ TRACK, + SUB, + AUX, RENAME, DELETE STRIP): Click + TRACK in the console toolbar to append a new Input Track (up to 32 tracks), + SUB to add a stereo Subgroup Bus (up to 16 subgroups), + AUX to add a stereo Aux Return bus (up to 8 Aux returns), RENAME to edit the selected strip's scribble-strip label inline, or DELETE STRIP to remove it. Removing a track, subgroup, or Aux return is fully reversible via UNDO (CMD/CTRL + Z), preserving its complete strip settings, routing, and Pass Lane state in the undo history.
  • Inline Scribble-Strip Renaming: Click any Track, Subgroup, or Aux Return nameplate header (01KickIn, DRUM BUS, AUX 1 REVERB) to edit its name inline and press ENTER.
  • Mono & Stereo-Linked Input Channels (IN 01 vs. IN 01-02): Each Input Track can be bound to a single mono hardware input (IN 01 through IN 32) or configured as a Stereo-Linked Input Pair (IN 01-02, IN 03-04, ...) for stereo synthesizers, stage pianos, drum overheads, or stereo room microphones. Stereo-linked tracks record 2-channel interleaved Broadcast Wave .wav stems and process left and right channels together through a single stereo channel strip.

Each Input Track strip is organized vertically from top to bottom in strict signal-flow order.
