4.2.2 Zone 1 & Zone 2: Track Header, Input Routing, Polarity, Phase & Trim#

At the top of each Input Track strip (CH01 through CH18), the Track Header displays the channel badge (CH01 highlighted in emerald when selected) and the custom scribble-strip name (01KickIn, 02SnrTp, 03OvrhdL, 04GtrAmp). A crimson outline borders the entire selected channel strip to show at a glance which track is currently loaded into the four Upper Console Wells (on the MIXER view, CMD/CTRL + 2) and the full-screen CHANNEL STRIP view (CMD/CTRL + 3). Immediately beneath the track name, a compact dual telemetry line reports the current fader gain and the sub-sample phase delay offset in microseconds (such as -2.4 dB 4 µs on CH01, +1.5 dB 0 µs on CH02, and +0.0 dB 92 µs on CH03).

Clicking the Input Source Selector (IN 01 v or INST v) opens the 3-tab floating input routing overlay (MONO | STEREO | INSTRUMENT):

  • MONO & STEREO Tabs (Hardware Inputs, Phase Role & External MIDI): Bind the strip to any mono physical input (IN 01 through IN 32), any stereo-linked pair (LINK STEREO IN 01+02, ...), a Drum Machine individual voice breakout, or NONE (PLAYBACK). Two compact footer rows sit below the hardware input grid:
    • PHASE ROLE: (ACOUSTIC MIC | ISOLATED DI): Marks whether the channel participates in automatic multi-microphone ALIGN ALL phase correlation (ACOUSTIC MIC, default for microphones) or stays excluded at 0 us (ISOLATED DI, ideal for bass/guitar DI boxes and external synthesizers).
    • EXT MIDI: (NONE | <MIDI Output Port> + CONSOLE / HW MIX): Binds an analog return strip to a calibrated external hardware synthesizer or drum machine MIDI output port so Cave Recorder automatically compensates its measured microsecond MIDI-to-ADC delay across first-generation Takes and Overdub Passes.
  • INSTRUMENT Tab & Pre-Tape Virtual Instrument Strip Layout ([INST v] & [GUI]): Assigns the native [NATIVE] CAVE DRUM MACHINE or any indexed CLAP instrument or macOS Audio Unit ('aumu') virtual instrument directly at the Track Input Stage (upstream of the 30-minute stereo RETRO memory, the 32-bit float rec/*.wav stem recorder, and the 8-slot insert rack). Configure the MIDI Input Port (ALL MIDI INPUTS or a specific controller port), Channel Filter (OMNI, CH 01..16, or SYNC ONLY), and Output Width (STEREO or MONO). When an instrument is assigned, Zone 2 preserves the exact same strip height while adapting cleanly in place:
    • Row 1: [INST v] (illuminated cyan when ready, amber if ! MISSING), [GUI] (opens the floating instrument editor window or jumps to the DRUM MACHINE tab), [Ø], and [Φ] (automatically isolated for virtual instruments).
    • Row 2 (Live MIDI & Sleep Status Bar): Shows the active MIDI filter (MIDI: OMNI, MIDI: CH01, or SYNC ONLY) with an emerald note-activity indicator lamp, switches to INST: SLEEP at 0% CPU once the instrument is disarmed and unmonitored and its natural voice tail decays below -120 dBFS (sending Sustain Off and All Notes Off cleanly so notes never chop mid-decay), or displays ! MISSING if an instrument plugin is uninstalled on another computer.
    • Row 3 (TRM): Retains the -24.0 dB to +24.0 dB digital trim bar post-instrument, pre-rack.
  • Pass Playback Isolation on Pre-Tape Instrument Strips: When playing back an existing Take on a disarmed, non-monitored [INST] strip (R off, I off) that has a recorded audio Pass (Rec001.wav), Cave Recorder streams the recorded .wav stem and silences the live instrument engine so recorded synth or drum performances never double-trigger. Re-enabling R (with OD) or I wakes the live instrument instantaneously.

Directly to the right of the input dropdown sit two phase-conditioning switches paired with a zero-slot top-of-strip allpass phase rotator:

  • Ø (Polarity Invert, SHIFT + P on the inspected strip): Reverses the positive and negative waveform excursions by 180°. It illuminates cyan when active (for example, on CH02 02SnrTp when phase-aligning a snare microphone against overheads or a bottom snare mic, or after running the Mode 1 Instant Binary Polarity Maximizer).
  • Φ (Sub-Sample Phase Alignment & Zero-Slot Phase Align Network): Illuminates emerald when automatic or manual multi-mic phase alignment is active on the channel. In addition to applying a sub-sample time-of-flight delay between 0.00 ms and +50.00 ms (0 us to 50,000 us), every channel strip contains a built-in, zero-slot 5-stage Phase Align Network (one 1st-order 20-500 Hz low-frequency rotator plus four 2nd-order 20-12,000 Hz biquad allpass stages with a clickless 10 ms dual-branch preset crossfade) driven by the Mode 2 Deep Multicore Spectral Phase & Allpass Solver. Because the Phase Align Network lives at the top of the channel strip alongside Ø and Φ, all eight insert slots remain completely free for creative mixing. See Chapter 5: Built-In Processors, Phase Alignment & External Plugins (CLAP & AU) for the complete multi-mic alignment and Polarity Maximizer workflow.

Below the input and phase row, the horizontal Input Trim (TRM) bar adjusts pre-insert gain from -24.0 dB to +24.0 dB around a center 0.0 dB detent. Use TRM (or click CALIBRATE TRIMS in the Control Room bar to automatically calibrate all active channels to -18 dBFS RMS with a -6 dBFS peak ceiling in one step) so that raw stems hit disk and analog-modeled insert processors in their optimal dynamic sweet spot.

When a Stagebox (X-Air OSC UDP 10024 or X32 OSC UDP 10023) is connected (see Section 2.6 in Chapter 2 and Section 4.6), Zone 2 also exposes direct hardware preamp controls above digital TRM:

  • PRE / PRE! (-12.0 dB to +60.0 dB in 0.5 dB Steps) & SB Quick-Jump: Adjusts the physical analog microphone preamp on the stagebox (or -12.0 dB to +20.0 dB on stereo line inputs 17/18). Displays OFF when no stagebox is paired, switches to PRE! if the stagebox channel's USB send tap is not set to raw analog, and shows an amber Δ delta indicator whenever the live stagebox gain differs from the saved Session value. Clicking SB opens that channel directly inside the desktop STAGEBOX workspace (CMD/CTRL + 9).
  • 600 ms Hold-to-Toggle 48V Phantom Power Interlock: To prevent accidental single-click phantom power switching on ribbon microphones or live studio monitors, toggling 48V on either the desktop strip or the Cave Companion mobile MIXER / STAGEBOX view requires a continuous 600 ms press-and-hold with a live crimson progress fill indicator (releasing early cancels the toggle without changing hardware phantom power state).

4.2.3 Zone 3 & Zone 4: Multi-Instance Insert Rack Summary, Active Pass Badge & Aux Sends#

Zone 3 provides instant status feedback for both multi-instance insert processing and track-level Pass selection:

  • N OF 8 SLOTS (Multi-Instance Reorderable 8-Slot Rack): Reports how many of the channel's eight reorderable processor slots are currently populated (for example, 3 OF 8 SLOTS when 12B EQ, VCA CMP, and AUX SND are active). Any built-in studio processor (12-Band Dynamic EQ, VCA/FET/Opto Compressor, Tape Saturation, Context-Aware Gate, Guitar/Bass Amp Rig, standalone Cab IR Speaker Cabinet & Linear IR Loader, De-Esser, Vocal Rider, Transient Shaper, Ladder Filter, Modulation, Micro-Pitch Doubler, Gain Utility, or Signal Repair) or external CLAP / macOS Audio Unit plugin can be inserted in multiple slots simultaneously on the same channel or Subgroup Bus. For example, you can place a surgical 12-Band Dynamic EQ in Slot 1 before an Amp Rig head (HEAD ON/BYP) in Slot 2, insert stereo Modulation in Slot 3, follow it with a standalone Cab IR speaker cabinet in Slot 4, and add a post-cabinet 12-Band Dynamic EQ and dual FET + Opto compressors in Slots 5 through 7, with independent per-slot parameter state, bypass, and real-time telemetry in CHANNEL STRIP (CMD/CTRL + 3).
  • Active Pass Badge (PASS 01 / OD 02): Displays in gold which track-level Pass is currently active inside the loaded Session Take. PASS 01 indicates the original Rec001 Base Pass captured when the Take began at 00:00:00.000, while OD 02, OD 03, and higher indicate subsequent track-level Overdub Passes (Rec002-OD, Rec003-OD) recorded inside that same Take.
Takes vs. Passes on the Channel Strip

Never confuse a session-level Take (TAKE 001 in the Top Deck transport bar, representing an entire song performance starting at 00:00:00.000) with a track-level Pass (PASS 01 or OD 02 on the channel strip, representing an individual recording pass on that single track within the active Take). Expanding and comping Pass Lanes is covered in Chapter 6: Waveform Timeline, Pass Lanes, Markers & Ranges.

Zone 4 houses the Banked Stereo Auxiliary Sends (AUX 1..8):

  • RVB / AUX 1 & DLY / AUX 2 (Plus Banked Sends AUX 3..8): Feeds the console's stereo Aux Return buses (AUX 1 REVERB, AUX 2 TAPE DLY, and up to six additional stereo Aux Return buses AUX 3 through AUX 8), adjustable from -inf (-60.0 dB) to +12.0 dB by dragging horizontally across the crimson send bar. When a session uses more than two Aux Return buses, Zone 4 displays banked send selectors on the channel strip while CHANNEL STRIP (CMD/CTRL + 3) exposes the full 8-bus Aux Send matrix simultaneously.
  • 3-Way Send Tap Selector (PRE / EQ / POST): Clicking the tap button to the right of any send cycles through three pickoff points in the channel signal path:
    • PRE (Pre-Insert / Pre-Fader): Taps the signal immediately after TRM, Ø, and Φ, unaffected by channel EQ, compression, fader moves, or channel Mute (M). Ideal for feeding a dedicated musician headphone cue mix.
    • EQ (Post-EQ / Pre-Fader): Taps the signal immediately after the 12B EQ slot (so low-cut filters and resonant notch cuts clean up the send) but before the VCA compressor and channel fader.
    • POST (Post-Fader, Default): Taps the signal after the channel insert rack, fader, and Mute switch so that riding the channel fader up or down naturally scales its wet reverb and delay contribution in proportion.

4.2.4 Zone 5, Zone 6 & Zone 7: Output Routing, Switch Bank, Fader & 40-Segment Meter#

Zone 5 controls where the channel's post-fader stereo image is summed:

  • Output Bus Selector (OUT: SUB 1 ▾, OUT: SUB 2 ▾, OUT: MST ▾): Assigns the channel to a stereo Subgroup Bus (illuminated in crimson when routed to a Subgroup such as OUT: SUB 1 ▾ for DRUM BUS) or directly to the stereo Master Bus (OUT: MST ▾). In the expanded CHANNEL STRIP view (CMD/CTRL + 3), clicking the Output Bus selector opens the multi-bus routing popover, where a single track or subgroup can route to multiple Subgroup Buses and the Master Bus simultaneously for parallel bus processing.
  • Stereo Pan Bar (PAN): Positions the signal between left (L 100%), center (C), and right (R 100%) using a studio -3.0 dB constant-power panning law so a signal panned hard left or right maintains the same perceived loudness as when centered.

Zone 6 provides the four primary console switches in the universal 4-surface order [M] (Mute Amber) -> [S] (Solo Gold) -> [R] (Record Crimson) -> [I] (Input Monitor). All four switches can be clicked directly on any strip or toggled via SHIFT shortcuts on the currently inspected channel (leaving unmodified single keys free for global transport and marker actions):

  1. M (Mute Amber, SHIFT + M on inspected strip): Silences the post-fader output and POST aux sends. Unmodified M drops a cue marker on the timeline without muting audio, and muting a channel on the Mixer never interrupts pre-fader multitrack stem recording on an armed track.
  2. S (Solo Gold, SHIFT + S on inspected strip): Engages Solo-in-Place on the monitor bus (illuminating bright Solo Gold with dark text and activating SOLO (N)·CLEAR in Top Deck Row 1) so you can inspect an individual microphone or subgroup in stereo context while keeping multitrack recording untouched.
  3. R (Record Arm Crimson, SHIFT + A on inspected track): Arms the track for multitrack WAV capture when transport Record (R) is engaged, and includes the channel in the rolling 30-minute retroactive memory capture (● RETRO / SAVE RETRO, triggered via SHIFT + R). Even when software Input Monitoring (I) is off, any record-armed track (R) continuously feeds live physical input signal to its 40-segment LED meter and the Dual-Trace Pre/Post-EQ RTA so you can verify preamp headroom and spectral balance during zero-latency hardware direct-monitoring sessions without doubling the monitor signal in the headphones.
  4. I (Input Monitor, SHIFT + I on inspected track): Switches the channel strip's audible monitor source between automatic disk playback of the active Pass Lane (PASS 01 / OD 02) and live audible monitoring of the physical hardware input (IN 01..IN 18) through the channel's insert rack and fader. Enable I when rehearsing parts through console effects or checking microphone placement while playing back an existing Take.

Zone 7 contains the Logarithmic Studio Fader and 40-Segment Peak/RMS Meter:

  • Fader Cap, Scale & Direct Numeric Entry: Provides smooth logarithmic resolution around the 0.0 dB unity gain mark, ranging from +12.0 dB down to -inf (-60.0 dB), with a dedicated numeric dB readout at the bottom of the meter well (-2.4 dB, +1.5 dB, +0.0 dB). Clicking the numeric dB readout below any fader opens an inline text entry box where you can type an exact decibel value (such as -3.5 or 0) and press ENTER.
  • 40-Segment LED Bargraph: Combines instantaneous digital sample peak detection (including a floating yellow peak-hold segment and red 0.0 dBFS overload latch) with continuous RMS loudness ballistics:
    • Emerald Segments (-48 dB to -12 dB): Nominal tracking and mixing operating zone.
    • Amber Segments (-12 dB to -3 dB): Healthy transient peak zone.
    • Red Cap (-3 dB to 0.0 dBFS): Digital full-scale peak warning. Click CLR CLIP on the Master Bus or in the Channel Inspector (or press X in the Channel Inspector) to clear latched clip indicators.

4.3 Subgroup Buses, Aux Returns & Master Bus#

To the right of the Input Track strips sit the console's stereo summing and return strips: Subgroup Buses (DRUM BUS, INST BUS, expandable from 0 to 16 stereo subgroups via + SUB), Stereo Aux Returns (AUX 1 REVERB and AUX 2 TAPE DLY by default, expandable from 0 to 8 stereo Aux Return bays via + AUX), and the Master Bus (MST MASTER BUS).

4.3.1 Stereo Subgroup Buses (DRUM BUS / SUB 1, INST BUS / SUB 2 .. SUB 16)#

Subgroup Buses let you sum related Input Tracks (such as all drum microphones into DRUM BUS, or guitars and keys into INST BUS) so you can process the entire group through a shared 8-slot insert rack and control its overall level with a single stereo fader.

Each Subgroup Bus strip provides:

  • Crimson Bus Header & Stereo Readout: Displays the custom bus name (DRUM BUS, INST BUS) and current stereo fader gain (+0.0dB STEREO).
  • SEL (Select Bus for Inspection): Clicking SEL loads the Subgroup Bus into the four Upper Console Wells (CMD/CTRL + 1) and the CHANNEL INSPECTOR view (CMD/CTRL + 3). Every Cave Recorder Subgroup Bus owns a full 8-Slot Reorderable SUB RACK with its own Tape Saturation stage, 12-Band Parametric EQ with Dual-Trace RTA, Analog VCA Bus Compressor, and third-party CLAP and macOS Audio Unit (AUv3 / AUv2) plugin slots.
  • LINK (Stereo Dynamics & Gain Link): Illuminates crimson when enabled, locking left and right detector sidechains and gain stages across the stereo bus so off-center floor tom or guitar hits never skew the stereo center image.
  • Subgroup Trim (TRM, -24.0 dB to +24.0 dB): Gain-stages the summed multi-channel signal before it enters the Subgroup's 8-slot SUB RACK. If summing eight hot drum tracks drives the subgroup bus compressor too hard, pull back TRM on DRUM BUS rather than disturbing your individual drum fader balance.
  • SUB RACK Status (3 OF 8 SLOTS): Indicates how many processors are active in the subgroup's insert rack.
  • Subgroup Aux Sends (RVB & DLY): Sends the entire post-rack subgroup mix to AUX 1 REVERB (default -12.0 dB) or AUX 2 TAPE DLY (default -15.0 dB, range -inf to +12.0 dB) to place a whole drum kit or horn section into the same acoustic room.
  • Output Bus Selector (OUT: MST v) & Stereo Balance (BAL): Routes the subgroup to the MASTER BUS (or cascades into downstream higher-numbered subgroups via the multi-bus routing popover in the Channel Inspector) and adjusts left/right stereo balance (L 100%..C..R 100%).
  • Bus Mute (M), Solo (S), Fader (-inf to +12.0 dB) & 40-Segment Meter: Controls final subgroup level and solo isolation. Soloing a Subgroup Bus automatically solos its contributing post-fader input channels in the monitor path.

4.3.2 Dedicated Stereo Aux Returns (AUX 1 REVERB & AUX 2 TAPE DLY)#

Cave Recorder includes two hardwired, zero-latency stereo effect return strips so you never have to sacrifice Input Track slots or configure third-party plugins just to set up studio plate reverb and tape slapback during a session:

Return Strip Header & Engine Readouts Interactive Strip Drag Bars Strip Switches & Routing
AUX 1 REVERB EMT 140 Plate impulse response name, LC 90Hz input low-cut readout (20 Hz to 1000 Hz), and FFT CONV IR / ZERO-LATENCY engine status. PD (Pre-Delay): 0 ms to 200 ms (e.g., 18ms). DCY (Decay Time): 0.20 s to 12.00 s (e.g., 2.40s), dynamically rebuilding and swapping the stereo plate impulse response in real time. OUT: MST v routing, WET 100% readout, Mute (M), WET button (toggles 100% full wet vs. 50% blend), Return Fader (-6.0 dB), and 40-segment meter.
AUX 2 TAPE DLY STEREO DLY (CAPSTAN TAPE, BBD ANALOG, or PRISTINE DIGITAL) model header with WOW/DMP readout and DLY + FX RACK slot summary. SYNC + TM / DV (Delay Time or Musical Subdivision): Click SYNC to toggle between free milliseconds (TM, 1 ms to 2000 ms, e.g., 320ms) and tempo-synced musical subdivisions (DV, 1/64 to 4BAR, default 1/8D, plus R.DV independent right-channel division in Pristine Digital). FB (Feedback): 0% to 95% strip drag bar (98% engine max, e.g., 35%). OUT: MST v routing, Mute (M), Solo (S), Solo-Safe (SAFE), Return Fader (-9.0 dB), and 40-segment meter.

For complete acoustic modeling details and studio tuning recipes for AUX 1 REVERB and AUX 2 TAPE DLY, see Section 5.5 in Chapter 5.

4.3.3 The Pinned Stereo Master Bus (MST MASTER BUS)#

The rightmost strip on the Mixer is the Master Bus (MST MASTER BUS), which stays snug beside the last Aux strip in compact sessions (4 tracks) and pins permanently on the right edge behind a crisp 6 px seam whenever a wider session (18 or 32 tracks) scrolls horizontally. It sums all Subgroup Buses, direct Input Tracks, and Stereo Aux Returns into the final stereo program bus feeding your control room monitors and the concurrent Live Stereo Print Recorder.

+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                   MST MASTER BUS PROCESSING CHAIN                 |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
  Summed Stereo Bus (Subgroups + Direct Tracks + Aux Returns)
         |
         v
  [1] MASTER TAPE SATURATION ([TAPE SAT] Toggle)
      * DRIVE: 0.0 dB to +24.0 dB (default +4.5 dB)
      * WARM:  0% to 100% harmonic density (default 35%)
         |
         v
  [2] MASTER BUS GLUE COMPRESSOR ([COMP] Toggle)
      * Stereo VCA bus compression controlled by THR (-48.0..0.0 dB)
         |
         v
  [3] LOOKAHEAD BRICKWALL LIMITER ([LIM] Toggle, Crimson when Active)
      * THR (Threshold): -48.0 dB to 0.0 dB (default -12.0 dB)
      * CEIL (True-Peak Ceiling): -6.0 dB to 0.0 dB (default -0.3 dB)
         |
         v
  [4] MASTER FADER (-inf to +12.0 dB) & MASTER MUTE ([M])
         |
         +---> Main Hardware Monitor Outputs (Channels 1 & 2)
         +---> [2-TRK PRINT] Live Stereo Print WAV + [FLAC]/[MP3] + [BOUNCE]

Every control on the MST MASTER BUS strip is designed for immediate tactile operation during tracking and mixing:

  • DRIVE & WARM Drag Bars: Adjust the input drive (0.0 dB to +24.0 dB, shown at +4.5 dB) and analog transformer/oxide warmth (0% to 100%, shown at 35%) of the Master Tape stage.
  • TAPE SAT, COMP & LIM Processor Toggles: Independently engage or bypass the Master Tape stage (TAPE SAT), Master Bus Glue VCA Compressor (COMP), and Lookahead Brickwall Limiter (LIM).
  • THR (Threshold) & CEIL (Brickwall Ceiling) Drag Bars: THR (-48.0 dB to 0.0 dB, default -12.0 dB) sets the compression and limiting threshold, while CEIL (-6.0 dB to 0.0 dB, default -0.3 dB) locks the absolute digital output ceiling so live rehearsal Print files and offline Mixdown renders never clip inter-sample converter reconstructions.
  • 2-TRK PRINT (Live 2-Track Print Toggle): When enabled, every transport Record pass automatically records the post-Master-Bus stereo mix in real time to <TakeFolder>/mix/<SessionID>_Take<NNN>_Print<PPP>_<Stamp>.wav with automatic Plugin Delay Compensation (PDC) latency trimming so the printed stereo master aligns sample-accurately with the recorded multitrack stems.
  • FLAC, MP3 & BOUNCE (Master Mixdown Format Toggles & Trigger): The FLAC and MP3 buttons independently toggle 24-bit lossless .flac and 320 kbps CBR .mp3 export formats (either or both can be enabled at once). Clicking BOUNCE renders a faster-than-realtime master mixdown of the active Take (<SessionID>_Take<NNN>_Mix<MMM>_<Stamp>.<flac|mp3>, with live progress and cancel in the Top Deck Async Job Status Bar and a Xing/Info seek header on .mp3 files for instant scrubbing in the Google Drive web player) and links the output files into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/ for immediate band listening and Google Drive synchronization.
  • CLR CLIP (Clear Clip Latches): Resets latched red peak-overload indicators across the Master Bus and all channel meters.
  • Master Mute (M), Master Fader (-inf to +12.0 dB) & Stereo 40-Segment Meter: Provides final control room level control and high-resolution peak/RMS metering.
  • Stagebox Hardware Monitor Quick Controls (HW OUT | TAPE in Master Strip Zone 2): Whenever a Stagebox (X-Air OSC or X32 OSC) is paired, Zone 2 of the MST MASTER BUS strip presents a compact HW OUT | TAPE mode toggle (defaulting to HW OUT so hardware monitor trim stays within one click). In HW OUT mode, compact horizontal MAIN + M (Mute) and AUX + M (Mute) controls ride the stagebox's physical Main L/R and Aux Return output levels directly from the Master Strip (dimming to read-only while a stagebox reconnects, and flipping back to DRIVE/WARM whenever you select TAPE). Full USB -> Aux -> Main L/R pair selection and vertical faders remain available in STAGEBOX (Section 2.6.3 in Chapter 2).

4.3.4 Control Room Monitor Bar (MONITOR:) & AUTO LEVEL Loudness-Matched Bypass#

Across the Console Toolbar sits the MONITOR: Control Room Bar alongside POLARITY MAX, CALIBRATE TRIMS, and METER SUITE. Crucially, the Control Room Monitor Bar is wired strictly downstream of the Master Bus 2-TRK PRINT live stereo Print tap and the offline BOUNCE mixdown engine. You can engage any speaker-check filter, fold the monitors to mono, or dim the control room volume while a live Take is recording without ever affecting the Print001.wav file being written to disk.

Monitor Bar Control Acoustic / DSP Specification Studio Mixing Purpose
MONO Unity-gain (L + R) × 0.5 sum (-6.02 dB per channel) Verifies single-speaker translation (club PA systems, smart speakers, and phone playback) and immediately reveals any hollow comb filtering or out-of-phase stereo guitars.
STEREO DIFF (L - R) × 0.7071 (-3.01 dB) stereo side difference Solos only the stereo side information (panned guitars, wide overheads, dimension chorus, and plate reverb tails) while canceling dead-center kick, snare, bass, and lead vocals.
SUB Band Solo 4th-order (24 dB/oct) Linkwitz-Riley (LR4) low-pass < 90 Hz Isolates sub-bass fundamentals so you can hear whether the kick drum and bass guitar are fighting each other or rumbling out of phase below 90 Hz.
LOW Band Solo LR4 band-pass 90 Hz - 350 Hz Isolates the lower-midrange warmth and mud zone (snare body, rhythm guitar palm-mutes, bass upper harmonics, and room boom).
MID Band Solo LR4 band-pass 350 Hz - 3.5 kHz Isolates the core midrange where vocal intelligibility, snare crack, and guitar attack live, emulating a classic small single-cone studio cube speaker check.
HIGH Band Solo LR4 high-pass > 3.5 kHz Isolates cymbal air, vocal sibilance, pick transient click, and high-gain amplifier fizz.
DIM -20 Smooth -20.0 dB default control room attenuation (-40.0 dB to -6.0 dB configurable) Drops studio monitor volume by 20 dB for low-level balance checking (where vocal-to-snare balance is easiest to judge) or talking with bandmates between songs.
AUTO LEVEL Bypass Input vs. output RMS tracker (300 ms integration window, gated below -60 dBFS, clamped to ±18.0 dB safety range) Automatically matches the output loudness of a processor or entire 8-slot rack to its pre-insert input loudness when toggling bypass (B), defeating the human ear's "louder sounds better" psychoacoustic bias.
Checking Mix Translation with MID + MONO

Engaging MID (350 Hz - 3.5 kHz) and MONO together emulates a single-driver midrange studio cube speaker. If your lead vocal, snare drum, bass harmonics, and lead guitar are all clearly audible and balanced in MID + MONO, your mix will translate reliably across everything from car stereos and laptops to festival PA systems.

4.3.5 Broadcast & Phase Studio Metering Suite (Meter Probe & Console Metering Deck)#

In addition to per-strip 40-segment Peak/RMS bargraphs, Cave Recorder provides a comprehensive Broadcast Loudness, Crest-Factor & Spectral Phase Metering Suite accessible on the Master Bus metering deck and insertable at any point in a channel or subgroup signal path via the Meter Probe rack processor:

  1. ITU-R BS.1770-4 K-Weighted Loudness (LUFS & LRA):
    • Cascaded two-stage K-weighting filter (Stage 1: +4.0 dB high-shelf head-acoustics pre-filter at 1681.97 Hz, Stage 2: 2nd-order RLB high-pass filter at 38.13 Hz).
    • M (Momentary Loudness, 400 ms sliding window): Tracks fast phrase-level loudness swings.
    • S (Short-Term Loudness, 3.0 s sliding window): Primary reference for balancing chorus-to-verse intensity.
    • I (Integrated Loudness, Dual-Gate -70 LUFS absolute + -10 LU relative): Measures overall song loudness from start to finish with a one-click reset button.
    • LRA (Loudness Range in LU): Measures the macroscopic dynamic spread between quiet verses and loud climaxes (10th to 95th percentile of short-term loudness).
  2. 4x Oversampled True-Peak Meter (dBTP):
    • Uses a 4x oversampled FIR interpolator (48 taps, 12 taps per phase) to reconstruct the continuous analog waveform between digital samples and catch inter-sample clipping that standard 0.0 dBFS sample-peak meters miss. Keep Master Bus CEIL at -0.3 dBTP to -1.0 dBTP when encoding FLAC and 320 kbps MP3 files so consumer DACs and streaming transcoders never distort.
  3. Crest Factor & Micro-Dynamic Ballistics (PSR & PLR):
    • Continuously computes Peak-to-Short-Term Loudness Ratio (PSR = TruePeak - LUFS_S) and Peak-to-Integrated Loudness Ratio (PLR = TruePeak - LUFS_I) to show at a glance whether your Master Bus Limiter is preserving drum punch or crushing the life out of the band:
    • PSR > 10.0 LU (Emerald, OPEN / DYNAMIC): Uncompressed acoustic, jazz, folk, and dynamic live-room recordings with full transient snap.
    • PSR 6.0 to 10.0 LU (7 dB to 9 dB target, Gold, PUNCHY): Competitive modern rock and heavy live-band loudness that still retains visceral kick and snare punch.
    • PSR < 6.0 LU (Crimson, CRUSHED Warning): Heavy brickwall limiting is squashing drum transients flat and inducing listener ear fatigue. Back off LIM THR or raise subgroup drum dynamics.
  4. Stereo Lissajous Goniometer & 32-Band Spectral Phase Scope (-1.0 to +1.0):
    • Displays a real-time 45°-rotated Mid/Side Lissajous vectorscope alongside a vertical 32-Band Log-Spaced Spectral Phase Correlation Display driven by 32 2nd-order state-variable bandpass filters (20 Hz to 20 kHz, Q = 2.2).
    • Each frequency band from 20 Hz to 20 kHz plots its normalized left-right cross-correlation C(b) ∈ [-1.0, +1.0]. Points near +1.0 (center spine) are tightly mono-compatible, +0.2 to +0.8 indicate healthy stereo width, and excursions toward -1.0 glow amber/red to pinpoint the exact frequency band where out-of-phase overheads, room mics, or stereo widening processors will cancel out when summed to mono.
  5. 31-Band 1/3-Octave ANSI/ISO RTA with Visual Spectral Tilt (-4.5 dB/oct Studio & -3.0 dB/oct Pink):
    • Offers selectable Peak/RMS, Fast (125 ms) / Slow (1.0 s) ballistics, and three visual reference tilt slopes: -4.5 dB/oct (Modern Studio Reference), -3.0 dB/oct (Pink Noise Reference), and 0.0 dB/oct (Flat). In -4.5 dB/oct Studio mode, a well-balanced full-band mix appears as a near-horizontal line across the analyzer, making booming 120 Hz room resonances or harsh 4 kHz cymbal build-ups effortless to spot visually.

4.4 Precision Mouse & Keyboard Modifiers for Faders, Knobs & 2D XY Pads#

All faders, horizontal value bars (TRM, RVB, DLY, PAN, BAL, PD, DCY, TM, FB, DRIVE, WARM, THR, CEIL), tiered rotary knobs, interactive EQ/compressor graph nodes, and 2D XY Control Pads across the Mix Console and Channel Inspector Large Processor Views share a unified set of studio mouse gestures and modifier keys.

Interaction / Gesture macOS Modifier Windows / Linux Modifier Console Behavior
Standard Adjustment Click + Drag (Vertical on faders/knobs, Horizontal on bars, 2D on XY pads) Click + Drag Smoothly sweeps the parameter (or paired X/Y parameters on a 2D XY pad) across its studio operating curve.
10x Fine Precision Adjustment SHIFT + Click + Drag SHIFT + Click + Drag Engages 10x fine-gear resolution (0.1 dB steps on faders, trim, and thresholds, 0.1 Hz on low-frequency EQ bands, 0.01 on Q, 1% on mix/pan bars, and 10x fine gearing on 2D XY control pads without cursor jumping).
Instant Reset to Unity / Default Double-Click or OPT + Click Double-Click or ALT + Click Resets any fader, horizontal value bar, rotary knob, EQ node, or 2D XY pad puck directly to its exact unity or factory default value (updating the engine and formatted unit readout immediately).
Keyboard Numeric Value Entry Right-Click any value bar or knob (or Click fader/knob readout), type value, press ENTER Right-Click any value bar or knob (or Click fader/knob readout), type value, press ENTER Opens an inline numeric entry field showing the current formatted readout so you can type an exact target value (such as -2.5, 56.3, or 0.0) and press ENTER (or ESC to cancel).
Stepped Wheel Adjustment Mouse Scroll Wheel Mouse Scroll Wheel Increments or decrements the hovered fader, bar, or knob in calibrated steps. Hovering over an EQ node and scrolling adjusts filter bandwidth (Q).
Live Rack Slot Reordering Drag :: Handle or click ^ / v Drag :: Handle or click ^ / v Moves a processor slot up or down inside the 8-slot channel or subgroup rack in real time with clickless crossfading and zero audio dropouts.
Quick Slot Bypass Click [B] next to any slot Click [B] next to any slot Bypasses that individual rack slot (illuminates amber when bypassed) for instant A/B comparison without unloading the processor.
Holding SHIFT Mid-Drag for Surgical Sweet Spots

You do not need to press SHIFT before clicking a control. Start dragging a fader, rotary knob, EQ node, compressor threshold, or 2D XY pad puck normally to get close to the target sound, then press and hold SHIFT without releasing the mouse button to drop directly into 10x fine-tuning mode with zero position jump.

When your Dual-Screen Pad Controller is switched to [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] (SHIFT + CHANNEL, or SHIFT + PLUG-IN then F8, or clicking ● CONTROLLER in Top Deck Row 2), both 480×272 displays render a 4 px Console Burgundy perimeter frame (switching to Warm Preamp Copper in STAGEBOX PREAMPS) and put the entire Mix Console under your hands.

4.5.1 8-Channel Faders, Stagebox Preamps (600 ms +48V) & Dual-Screen AUX SENDS#

  1. MAIN FADERS (MIX):
    • Displays 4 vertical console fader strips on the Left Screen (E1..E4) and 4 on the Right Screen (E5..E8) in exact 1:1 encoder column alignment, with 20-segment Peak/RMS/Gain-Reduction meters and universal [M] (Mute Amber) / [S] (Solo Gold) / [R] (Record Crimson) status badges.
    • Turning E1..E8 rides strip faders (touching any capacitive encoder opens a single coalesced Undo gesture that commits cleanly when released, and CLEAR + Touch resets any parameter to unity 0.0 dB or center pan). Holding SHIFT + E1..E8 adjusts stereo Pan/Balance.
    • Press GROUPS A..H to jump instantly between Tracks 1..32 (A..D), Subgroups 1..16 (E..F), Aux Returns 1..8 (G), and Master & Control Room (H). Soft keys F1..F8 focus any strip in the active bank.
  2. STAGEBOX PREAMPS & +48V (Press MIX Again to Flip):
    • Frames both screens in Warm Preamp Copper (#C85A32), mapping E1..E8 directly to the 8 corresponding Stagebox Hardware Preamp Gains (dB) (SHIFT + Turn = 0.5 dB fine step) with live Pre-ADC input peak and clip meters. Strips without a mapped hardware headamp fall back automatically to silver-cyan Digital Input Trim (TRIM badge).
    • Guarded 600 ms +48V Phantom Power: Soft keys F1..F8 sit 1:1 above strips 1..8. Holding a soft key fills a Crimson progress bar inside that key's display cell and toggles +48V only after 600 ms. Short taps never toggle phantom power (flashing HOLD 0.6s). Press SHIFT + F1..F8 to invert polarity (Ø) on any strip.
  3. CHANNEL Detail & Dual-Screen AUX SENDS (F1: AUX SENDS):
    • Press CHANNEL to inspect the focused strip's Preamp Gain / Digital Input Trim, Fader, Pan/Balance, Phase Alignment Delay (µs), Aux Send levels (AUX 1..8) and TAP: POST (PRE/EQ/POST), +48V Phantom (600 ms hold), Polarity Ø, Record Arm, Mute/Solo, and Stagebox Gain Reconciliation (CAPTURE HW / PUSH GAINS).
    • Press F1: AUX SENDS on any Input Track or Subgroup Bus to engage dual-screen AUX SENDS (amber frame across both displays), mapping AUX 1..4 across Left E1..E4 and AUX 5..8 across Right E5..E8 (F2: TAP:POST, CLEAR + Touch resets any send to -inf).
  4. Hardware Level Meters, Control Room & Guarded Channel Modifiers:
    • Press MST, CUE, GRP, or IN 1..4 in the Level Section to switch the dual 16-LED hardware stereo meters between Master Bus, Control Room Cue, the currently focused strip (GRP), and raw hardware ADC pairs 1-2..7-8. Pressing the LEVEL knob while MST or CUE is selected toggles -20 dB Control Room DIM.
    • Bare pad taps in [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] operate strictly on Ranges, Cue Markers, or Pass Lanes so you never accidentally arm or mute a live channel mid-take. Hold SELECT, MUTE, SOLO, or REC while tapping Pads 1..16 to address Channels 1..16 (and hold any modifier + F1 (PIN) to pin it until re-tapped).

4.5.2 16-Pad Ranges, Cue Markers, Pass Lane Comping, BROWSE & Disk Take Transport#

  • SCENE (16 Ranges & Cycle Loop): Pad 1 addresses R001 Full Take, while Pads 2..16 map custom sub-ranges R002..R016. Tap a lit pad to select that Range, SHIFT + Tap a lit pad to select and engage Cycle Loop (⇄) in one stroke, or tap an unlit pad twice live (Tap 1 sets RANGE START, Tap 2 sets RANGE END) without stopping playback. Hold a lit Range pad to fine-trim Range Start (E1) and Range End (E2), zoom the waveform overview (F3: ZOOM RANGE), extract the Range to a brand-new t = 0 Take (F4: NEW TAKE), or send that Range straight into the Studio Sampler via F5: -> SAMPLER (Dry Pass) or F6: POST-FX -> SMP (Post-FX Bounce). Press CLEAR + Pad to delete a custom Range (with Undo) or cancel a pending start.
  • PAD MODE (16 Cue Markers): Lit cyan pads jump directly to M001..M016 (when stopped or playing). Unlit pads drop a new timestamped Cue Marker at the rolling Playhead (including during active Disk Take recording, persisted on Keep Take and cleanly purged on Discard Take). Press FUNC < / > in EDIT jog mode to jump between previous and next markers.
  • PATTERN (Pass Lane Comping): Maps Pads 1..16 to the focused track's recorded Pass Lanes (PASS 01, OD 02..OD 16) so tapping pads clicklessly promotes the active comp lane with full Undo support.
  • BROWSE (SNAPSHOTS & TAKES): Left Screen switches active Session Takes directly via E1 (or scrolls a highlight cursor with Jog Wheel + Push to confirm) and cycles focused track Pass Lanes via E2. Right Screen captures manual Console Snapshots (F5), auditions saved Snapshots (F6), and shows F7: RETRO 30M and F8: OVERDUB when idle (switching to F7: A/B LIVE and F8: LIVE MIX while auditioning a Snapshot).
  • Guarded Disk Take Transport, CONSOLE CAPTURE & RESAMPLE & 60 Hz Jog Scrub: Tap REC to start a new Disk Take (or Overdub Pass when OVERDUB is enabled). While recording, bare PLAY, bare REC, and the Jog Wheel are locked by the Active Take Stop Guard. Stop intentionally via F8: END TAKE, SHIFT + PLAY, or SHIFT + REC, or arm/confirm a 2-step discard via SHIFT + ERASE twice. Press SAMPLING in [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE] to open CONSOLE CAPTURE & RESAMPLE (F1: RESAMPLE STRIP, F2: RESAMPLE BUS, F3: RANGE -> SAMPLER, and F7: RETRO 30M to commit the rolling 30-minute retroactive memory to a new Take). When not recording, turning the Jog Wheel in EDIT mode scrubs the waveform timeline smoothly at 60 Hz.

4.6 Full-Featured Stagebox Mixer Workspace (STAGEBOX, CMD/CTRL + 9)#

When connected to a digital stagebox (X-Air OSC UDP 10024 including XR18, XR18V2, MR18, X18, XR16, XR12, MR12, or X32 OSC UDP 10023), pressing CMD/CTRL + 9, clicking ● STAGEBOX in Top Deck Row 2, or clicking any DAW strip's SB quick-jump keycap opens the dedicated STAGEBOX workspace. Its Warm Preamp Copper (#C85A32) accent distinguishes live hardware PA and monitor mixing clearly from Cave Recorder's recording console (MIXER).

4.6.1 1. MIXER: Layers, SENDS ON FADERS, Mute Groups, Auto-Mix & SOLO / PHONES#

  • 4 Channel Layers (ALL IN 1-18 | FX RTN 1-4 | BUS 1-6 & FX | DCA & GRP): Switch cleanly across physical analog/USB input strips, stereo FX return strips, monitor/FX send masters, and 4 DCA groups. Every strip follows the exact [M] (Mute Amber) -> [S] (Solo Gold) -> [LR] layout with brushed silver fader caps, PRE hardware gain, 600 ms hold 48V phantom power, Ø polarity, USB return toggle, HPF, and PAN.
  • SENDS ON FADERS (OFF | B1(1/2) | B2(1/2) | BUS 3..6 | FX 1..4): Click any monitor bus (or stereo-linked bus pair such as B1(1/2) with linked Level + Pan) or hardware FX bus (FX 1..4) to flip all channel faders into amber SENDS ON FADERS mode (displaying EXIT SENDS ON FADERS and per-channel send taps IN, PEQ, PSEQ, PRE, POST, GRP). Click OFF or EXIT SENDS ON FADERS to return immediately to MAIN LR FADER LAYER.
  • Console Governance & Name Sync: Toggle hardware MUTE GRP (MG 1..4), STEREO LINK (PREAMP, EQ, DYNAMICS, FADER), and AUTO-MIX X/Y automatic mic sharing, or click MIXER → STAGEBOX / STAGEBOX → MIXER to synchronize channel names and scribble colors bidirectionally between Cave Recorder and the hardware stagebox.
  • Pinned MAIN LR & SOLO / PHONES Panel: Keeps MAIN LR (STEREO PA, PEQ, DYN, BAL, M, S), CLEAR SOLO, PHONES rotary level, DIM -20 dB, MONO, MUTE, D-PFL, PFL/AFL mode selectors (CH | BUS | DCA), and MONITOR SOURCE (LR, LR PFL, LR AFL, AUX, USB17/18, BUS 1..6, stereo pairs) pinned permanently on the right edge.

4.6.2 Docked Stagebox DSP Inspector (PEQ, 100-bin RTA, 31-Band GEQ, Gate & Comp)#

Clicking any Stagebox strip opens the docked Stagebox DSP Inspector at the top of 1. MIXER, clearly badged MONITOR / PA DSP - USB REC RAW (or amber ! RECORDING POST-DSP if the selected channel's USB tap is post-DSP) so you always know whether hardware EQ and dynamics affect only the PA/IEM speakers or also your USB recording:

  • 4-Band PEQ (6-Band on Bus & Main) + Live 100-bin RTA: Interactive curve with draggable nodes superimposed over the stagebox's live 100-band Real-Time Analyzer for ringing out room resonances and stage monitors.
  • 31-Band GEQ / TruEQ (Bus 1..6 & Main L/R): Full 31-band graphic equalizer for live PA and wedge feedback control.
  • Gate / Expander / Ducker & Compressor / Expander: Complete hardware dynamics controls including SIDECHAIN / INSERT key selection and real-time gain-reduction telemetry.

4.6.3 2. ROUTING, 3. FX RACK & 4. SCENES & SETUP#

  • 2. ROUTING (4-Domain 2D Crosspoint Matrix): Visualizes and patches USB SENDS (1-18) (showing mapped DAW track name, arm LED, and Copper AIN vs. Amber post-DSP tap badge), CH INPUTS & VSC (with 1-click 1:1 RAW ANALOG and VIRTUAL SOUNDCHECK presets to feed recorded Cave Recorder Takes back through the hardware stagebox), ANALOG OUTS (MAIN + AUX 1-6), and ULTRANET P16 (1-16).
  • 3. FX RACK (4 Stereo Hardware FX Slots, 55 Algorithms): Loads and edits all 55 internal stagebox algorithms across Reverb, Delay, Modulation, Eq, Dynamics, Enhancer, and AmpPitch categories (using clean acoustic/circuit descriptions such as Program Tube EQ and Vari-Mu Tube Comp), toggles SEND/RTN vs. INSERT patching, provides TAP TEMPO, and displays live input/output and gain-reduction meters.
  • 4. SCENES & SETUP (Network, Dual Scene Sync & Companion Governance): Houses multi-NIC /xinfo discovery (169.254.x.x link-local diagnostics), 48 kHz / 44.1 kHz sample-rate and 18x18 / 2x2 USB mode guardrails, Dual Scene Persistence (<SessionFolder>/stagebox_scene.json via CAPTURE HARDWARE -> SESSION and ramped PUSH SCENE -> HARDWARE with opt-in APPLY +48V, plus the 64-slot hardware snapshot browser with FETCH ALL 64 and recall-scope filters), and Cave Companion stagebox role governance (MY MONITOR personal IEM bus pinning vs. FULL MIXER protected by MIXER LOCK / RELEASE MIXER LOCK and BUS SELF-SEL).
Part II · Chapter 5

Built-In Processors, Phase Alignment, Groovebox & Plugins (CLAP & AU)

Channel Strip Large Processor Views, interactive XY control pads, and collapsible Mini-Timeline, 12-Band Dynamic EQ, VCA/FET/Opto Compressors with plain-language SIDECHAIN and SIDECHAIN LISTEN controls, Drum Bleed and Stoner/Doom Amp Dynamic Gates, Guitar and Bass Amp Rig with 2x/4x oversampling, HEAD ON/BYP, and native .nam Neural Amp Capture, standalone Speaker Cabinet and Impulse Response Loader, Vocal Rider, De-Esser, Transient Shaper, Micro-Pitch Doubler, Tempo-Synced 3-Mode Delay, 4-Pole Ladder Filter, Studio Plate Reverb, Tempo-Synced & Phase-Locked 4-Mode Modulation, Polarity & Phase Maximizer, Audio Restoration, CLAP and isolated out-of-process macOS Audio Unit effects and Pre-Tape instruments, Low-Latency Monitoring and persistent Hardware Direct Monitoring warnings, the 6-Archetype Groovebox and Studio Sampler (SuperFlux transient slicing, live console resampling, creative pitch/filter/comb/LFO shaping, and Sample History versioned commits), and tactile dual-screen control on a Studio Pad Surface.

Every Input Track (CH01 through CH32) and every stereo Subgroup Bus (SUB 1 through SUB 16) in Cave Recorder includes a zero-slot top-of-strip 5-Stage Allpass Phase Align Network and a dedicated, multi-instance reorderable 8-Slot Processing Rack powered by Cave Recorder's Curated Native Console & Rack Suite (12-Band Dynamic EQ, VCA/FET/Opto Compressor, Tape Saturation, Guitar & Bass Amp Rig with HEAD ON/BYP and native .nam Neural Amp Capture, standalone Cab IR Speaker Cabinet & Linear Impulse Response Loader, Vocal De-Esser, Context-Aware Gate, Signal Repair, Vocal Rider, Transient Shaper, Ladder Filter, Studio Plate Reverb, Tempo-Synced 4-Mode Modulation, Micro-Pitch Doubler, Gain Utility, and Aux Send Tap) alongside cross-platform third-party CLAP (.clap) effects and Pre-Tape instruments (on direct macOS, Windows, and Linux downloads), native macOS Audio Unit (AUv3 and AUv2) effects ('aufx', 'aumf') and Pre-Tape Music Device instruments ('aumu'), automatic multi-mic phase and polarity alignment, up to eight dedicated stereo Auxiliary Returns (AUX 1 through AUX 8, including Tempo-Synced AUX 2 Stereo Delay), and the native 6-Archetype Groovebox & Studio Sampler (GROOVEBOX, CMD/CTRL + 6).

This chapter covers the dual-view inspection workflow (Upper Console Wells vs. full-screen CHANNEL STRIP with Large Processor Views, 2D XY Control Pads, and Collapsible Mini-Timeline), Tape Saturation (TAPE), Gain Utility & Differential Transient Shaper, the 12-Band Dynamic Parametric EQ & Dual-Trace Spectrum Analyzer (EQ & RTA), Vocal Rider, Split-Band De-Esser & Micro-Pitch Doubler, Multi-Topology VCA / FET / Opto Compressors (with External SIDECHAIN Key Routing & SIDECHAIN LISTEN), the Context-Aware 3-Variant Noise Gate (Expander, Drum Bleed, Amp Dynamic), Guitar/Bass Amp Rig ([CIR] Tube Models, HEAD ON/BYP & [NAM] Neural Amp Capture) & Standalone Cab IR Speaker Cabinet / Linear IR Loader, Stereo Convolution Reverb (AUX 1 REVERB), Tempo-Synced 3-Mode Delay (Capstan Tape, BBD Analog, Pristine Digital), 4-Pole Non-Linear Ladder Filter, Studio Plate Reverb & Tempo-Synced / Phase-Locked 4-Mode Modulation, Automatic Multi-Mic Phase Alignment (● ALIGN ALL) & the Two-Mode Multicore Polarity & Phase Maximizer (POLARITY MAX), CLAP & Isolated Out-of-Process macOS Audio Unit Effects & Pre-Tape Instrument Hosting (1:PLUGIN, INST, PLUGINS Manager, PLUGIN GUI, Ghost Slots, LATENCY PDC Breakdown, LOW-LATENCY & Persistent Hardware Direct Monitoring), Non-Destructive Audio Restoration (ADC De-Clipper & 12-Harmonic Hum Canceller), and the Native Groovebox & Studio Sampler (GROOVEBOX).

5.1 Upper Console Wells vs. Dedicated CHANNEL STRIP View#

Cave Recorder provides two complementary workspaces for viewing and shaping the processors on any Input Track or Subgroup Bus:

  1. The Four Upper Console Wells (MIXER View, CMD/CTRL + 2): Docked permanently along the upper deck of the Mixer so you can adjust inserts, EQ curves, and compression while keeping all channel faders and bus meters in view.
  2. The Dedicated CHANNEL STRIP View (CMD/CTRL + 3): Expands the selected channel or subgroup across the entire screen with a high-resolution Dual-Trace Real-Time Spectrum Analyzer, dedicated rotary parameter knobs, multi-bus output routing popovers, and a scrolling Gain Reduction history trace.

5.1.1 The Four Upper Console Wells (MIXER)#

Clicking any Input Track header (CH01..CH18) or clicking the SEL button on any Subgroup Bus (DRUM BUS, INST BUS) immediately binds the four Upper Console Wells to that strip:

Upper Well Header Label Core Controls & Displays
Well 1 (Far Left) <Track/Bus Name> (e.g., 01 Kick In or DRUM BUS) Quick action buttons (+ ADD PROCESSOR ▾, SWAP EQ/CMP, RESET), the 8-Slot Reorderable Rack (Slots 1..8 with :: drag handles, B bypass switches, and ^ / v move arrows), and the 6-parameter Tape Saturation bar bank (DRV, WRM, BIAS, HC, OUT, MIX).
Well 2 (Center-Left) EQ & RTA: <Track Name> (12-Band Parametric) Interactive 20 Hz to 20 kHz parametric response graph (-18 dB and +18 dB reference gridlines with full -24 dB to +24 dB band range), draggable band nodes, real-time spectrum trace, and filter shape pills (BELL, LSHF, HSHF, HPF, TILT, DYN).
Well 3 (Center-Right) VCA COMPRESSOR & GR (T:-18.0dB 4.0:1) Interactive transfer curve (-48 dB to 0 dB), threshold and knee handles, live crimson Gain Reduction (GR) shading, topology selector (VCA, FET, OPTO), SIDECHAIN source dropdown, SIDECHAIN LISTEN, TRIM, HPF, LPF, and LNK.
Well 4 (Far Right) TIMELINE & WAVEFORM (48 smp/px) Multi-resolution scrolling waveform monitor for the selected channel with Pass Lane and zoom triggers (PASSES, LOCK PLAYHEAD, → PLAYHEAD, ZOOM +, ZOOM -, 1:1).

5.1.2 Full-Screen CHANNEL STRIP View, Large Processor Decks, 2D XY Pads & Collapsible Mini-Timeline (CMD/CTRL + 3)#

Pressing CMD + 3 (macOS) or CTRL + 3 (Windows/Linux) switches to the dedicated CHANNEL STRIP view. Along the top selector bar, single-click pills (01 Kick In, 02 Snare Top, 03 Overhead L, 04 Guitar Amp, DRUM BUS, INST BUS, AUX 1, MST) let you step across every Input Track, Subgroup Bus, Aux Return, and Master Bus strip in the session without returning to MIXER.

In the CHANNEL INSPECTOR view, the left column anchors a full-height channel strip (complete with active Pass selector * PASS 01 on Input Tracks or STEREO SUBGROUP / SUBGROUP BUS badges on Subgroups, Output Bus selector, M, S, REC, MON, Ø, Φ, TRIM, rotary PAN, full-scale calibrated meter with +12 dB to -48 dB markings, and CLR CLIP), while the right-hand instrument workspace is governed by the top Signal-Flow Chain & Layout Mode Bar:

  • Signal-Flow Chain Bar & Three Workspace Layout Modes (SPLIT, CHAIN LANE, EQ+CMP):
    • Interactive Signal-Flow Chain Pills (Slots 1..8): Displays the active processors across the strip's 8 rack slots in exact top-to-bottom signal evaluation order. Clicking any slot pill in the chain bar immediately focuses that slot's dedicated Large Processor View and telemetry (even when multiple instances of the same processor type are loaded in different slots).

    • EQ+CMP Mode: Collapses the right-hand Large Processor Card so the 12-Band Parametric EQ and Compressor graphs span the full width of the inspector.
  • Full-Height Large Processor Views & Interactive 2D XY Control Pads: Every built-in processor (STUDIO TAPE SATURATION, CONTEXT-AWARE EXPANDER GATE, VOCAL DE-ESSER & PLOSIVE, AUTOMATIC VOCAL RIDER, TRANSIENT SHAPER & FOCUS, GUITAR / BASS AMP RIG & NAM, SPEAKER CABINET & IR LOADER, LADDER FILTER, ANALOG MODULATION SUITE, STEREO MICRO-PITCH DOUBLER, HUM & DE-CLIP REPAIR, GAIN & M/S UTILITY), the stereo Aux Return engines (AUX RETURN STEREO REVERB, AUX RETURN STEREO DELAY), the Master Bus Brickwall Limiter (MASTER TRUE-PEAK LIMITER), and external plugin slots (EXTERNAL CLAP PLUGIN SLOT) feature a dedicated three-zone hardware faceplate:
    • Zone A (Interactive 2D XY Control Pad & Real-Time Telemetry Bridge): Combines a real-time transfer curve, envelope trace, or spectral response contour with a draggable 2D XY Control Pad that sweeps two paired studio parameters simultaneously (such as DRIVE × WARMTH on Tape Saturation, ATTACK × SUSTAIN on Transient Shaper, CUTOFF × RESONANCE on Ladder Filter, MIC HPF × MIC LPF on Amp Rig and Cab IR, or THRESHOLD × CEILING on the Master True-Peak Limiter), flanked by a dedicated input/output/attenuation LED telemetry bridge. Hold SHIFT while dragging the XY puck for 10x fine precision without cursor jumps, or Double-Click (OPT/ALT + Click) to reset both axes to unity defaults.
    • Zone B (Hero Rotary Control Bay): Large-diameter Hero and Standard rotary knobs for the processor's primary sonic controls.

  • Multi-Bus Output Routing Popover: Clicking the green OUT: MST or crimson OUT: SUB 1 button in the left inspector strip opens the OUTPUT BUSES popover ([x] MASTER BUS, [ ] SUB 2: INST BUS), allowing any track or subgroup to feed multiple buses in parallel.
  • Collapsible Single-Track Mini-Timeline (HIDE TL / SHOW TL): Below the processor decks, the inspector waveform strip provides quick Pass Lane actions for the active Take (PASSES or E to expand Pass Lanes, PASS 01 to select the active pass, AUD P1 to audition, MUTE P1 to mute, and DEL P1 to deactivate). Clicking HIDE TL in the top-right corner of the Chain Bar (or in the mini-timeline header) collapses the bottom waveform strip down to a compact 28 px summary bar (SHOW TL) so the upper EQ, Compressor, and Large Processor Views reclaim the full vertical height of your display.
  • Dedicated Inspector Keyboard Shortcuts: While inspecting any strip, press H to toggle the compressor Sidechain High-Pass Filter (SC HPF), X to clear the channel peak overload latch (CLR CLIP), E to expand or collapse Pass Lanes (PASSES), or SHIFT + M / S / A / I / P to toggle Mute, Solo, Record Arm, Input Monitor, or Polarity (Ø).

5.1.3 Multi-Instance 8-Slot Rack, Reordering, SWAP EQ/CMP & RESET#

In Well 1 (01 Kick In or DRUM BUS) and in the left rack column of CHANNEL INSPECTOR, the eight processing slots (1 through 8) execute sequentially from Slot 1 down to Slot 8:

  • Multi-Instance Slot Assignment (SLOT N PROCESSOR Overlay): Clicking any slot pill (1 through 8) opens the floating SLOT N PROCESSOR selector menu. Any built-in zero-latency studio processor (12-Band Dynamic EQ, VCA Compressor, Tape Saturation, Vocal De-Esser, Context-Aware Gate, Signal Repair, Guitar/Bass Amp Rig, Speaker Cabinet & IR, 2P/4P Ladder LPF, Vocal Rider, Transient Shaper, Micro-Pitch Doubler, Gain & Polarity Utility, Studio Modulation, or Aux Send Tap) or external Plugin (CLAP or macOS Audio Unit) can be assigned to any number of slots on the same strip. Each slot maintains its own independent parameter state, bypass switch (B), and real-time metering telemetry. Clicking a slot in the rack or in the Inspector Chain Bar focuses that specific slot instance for editing.
  • Dragging :: or Clicking ^ / v: Reorders any processor (1:PLUGIN, 2:12B EQ, 3:VCA CMP, 4:AUX SND, 5:AMP RIG, 6:CAB IR) to an earlier or later slot in real time without audio clicks or dropouts. Moving 4:AUX SND above 3:VCA CMP, for example, taps the channel's Aux Sends before compression even when the send is set to rack-tap mode.
  • SWAP EQ/CMP Button: Instant one-click macro in the top-left rack header that swaps the slot positions of the 12B EQ and VCA CMP processors. Use SWAP EQ/CMP to audition whether filtering low-end mud before the compressor detector (EQ -> CMP) or shaping tonal balance after dynamic peak control (CMP -> EQ) sounds more natural on a vocal, bass, or drum bus.
  • B (Slot Bypass) & RESET: Clicking B next to any slot (or on the 12B EQ / VCA CMP badge) bypasses that single processor in place (illuminated amber). Clicking the crimson RESET button returns all built-in processors on the selected strip to their flat factory defaults.

5.2 Tape Saturation & Input Drive (TAPE)#

Located in Well 1 beneath the 8-slot rack, the built-in Tape Saturation (TAPE) processor models the non-linear magnetic hysteresis, transformer core warmth, bias asymmetry, and head-bump high-frequency roll-off of a calibrated analog multitrack tape machine running at 15 or 30 IPS.

Click the TAPE pill in the Well 1 header to engage or bypass the tape stage on the selected Input Track or Subgroup Bus.

5.2.3 Gain Utility: One-Click Trim Calibration (CALIBRATE TRIMS), Elliptical Bass-Mono & Allpass Dispersion#

In a self-recorded rehearsal or tracking session, microphone preamplifiers are often set hastily while musicians are warming up, leaving some channels peaking near -1 dBFS while others sit down at -32 dBFS. Feeding uncalibrated levels into analog-modeled compressors, tape saturators, and gates forces you to fight every threshold knob on the console.

The Gain Utility processor solves gain staging and stereo-field conditioning at the top of the rack:

Parameter / Action Range / Specification Default Studio Application
CALIBRATE TRIMS One-click console-wide auto-trim (-18.0 dBFS RMS target, -6.0 dBFS peak ceiling clamp) Action Button Analyzes active Pass audio across the Take and sets every channel's input trim so average energy sits at the -18.0 dBFS analog console sweet spot without any transient exceeding -6.0 dBFS.
Coarse Gain & Fine Trim Coarse Gain: -36.0 dB to +36.0 dB (5 ms smoothed ramp)
Fine Trim: -3.0 dB to +3.0 dB (0.05 dB steps)		 0.0 dB / 0.00 dB Clean digital level staging prior to downstream dynamics or saturation, with 0.05 dB vernier precision for exact A/B gain matching.

Channel Routing Mode Stereo, Mono Sum, Swap L/R, Left Only, Right Only, Side Diff Only Stereo Collapses a stereo input to mono, swaps reversed overhead channels, isolates one side of a dual-mic guitar cab, or solos the stereo difference (L - R) component.
Mid/Side Width 0% (Mono) to 200% (Super-Wide) 100% Scales the Side ((L - R) * 0.5) signal relative to Mid ((L + R) * 0.5) to narrow an overly wide keyboard patch or expand a stereo bus.

(Note: Zero-slot 5-stage allpass phase dispersion and rotation is built directly into the top of every channel strip via the dedicated Phase Align Network alongside Ø and Φ, as detailed in Section 5.6.4.)

5.2.4 Differential Envelope Transient Shaper#

Unlike compressors that depend on an absolute decibel threshold (and therefore react differently to quiet ghost notes versus loud rimshots), the built-in Transient Shaper uses a level-independent differential envelope detector. It compares a fast envelope follower (E_fast, 1.0 ms attack / 25.0 ms release) against a slow envelope follower (E_slow, 25.0 ms attack / 150.0 ms release) in the logarithmic decibel domain:

Δ_dB(n) = 20 log10(E_fast(n) + ε) - 20 log10(E_slow(n) + ε)

Because the difference Δ_dB(n) depends only on the rate of change of the envelope and not its absolute volume, every ghost note and loud accent receives consistent transient shaping:

  • Attack (-12.0 dB to +12.0 dB): Positive values amplify the initial 1 ms to 20 ms stick crack, kick beater click, or acoustic guitar pick attack. Negative values soften overly spiky transients or push close mics deeper into the room.
  • Sustain (-24.0 dB to +24.0 dB): Positive values bring up the decaying drum shell ring, room ambience, or guitar chord bloom after the initial attack has passed. Negative values tighten boomy rehearsal rooms and shorten long tom or kick tails cleanly without hard gate chatter.
  • Detector Focus Band (20 Hz to 16,000 Hz): Focuses the differential detector on a specific frequency zone (for example, 2.5 kHz to trigger only on snare wire snap while ignoring low-frequency kick bleed).
  • Soft Clip Output Guard: Engages a zero-overshoot tanh saturator on the output stage so boosting Attack by +8 dB adds visceral drum impact without clipping downstream buses.

5.3 12-Band Parametric EQ & Dual-Trace Spectrum Analyzer (EQ & RTA)#

Each Input Track and Subgroup Bus features a precision 12-Band Parametric Equalizer (2:12B EQ) paired with a Dual-Trace High-Resolution Real-Time Spectrum Analyzer (EQ & DUAL-TRACE RTA). Designed for zero-zipper-noise live adjustment, the equalizer handles everything from steep sub-bass rumble filtering and surgical snare-ring notch removal to broad, musical spectral tilt shaping.

5.3.2 Operating Interactive EQ Nodes & Reading the Dual-Trace RTA#

You can shape EQ either via the right-hand rotary knobs (FREQ, GAIN, Q) in the CHANNEL INSPECTOR view (CMD/CTRL + 3) or by manipulating the colored band nodes directly inside the EQ & RTA graph on both the Mix Console and Channel Inspector:

  • Click + Drag Node Horizontally / Vertically: Sweeps FREQ (20 Hz to 20 kHz) and GAIN (-24.0 dB to +24.0 dB) simultaneously.
  • Mouse Scroll Wheel (or SHIFT + Vertical Drag) Over a Node: Narrows or widens the filter Q (0.10 to 18.00).
  • SHIFT + Drag Node: Engages 10x fine precision (0.1 dB gain steps and sub-Hz frequency resolution) for locking onto exact room resonances.
  • Double-Click Node (or OPT/ALT + Click): Resets the band's GAIN to 0.0 dB.

Behind the white composite EQ curve, the Dual-Trace High-Resolution Real-Time Spectrum Analyzer (DUAL-TRACE RTA) renders two live acoustic traces simultaneously:

  1. Pre-EQ Input Spectrum (Darker Shaded Trace): Shows the raw frequency energy entering the 12B EQ slot.
  2. Post-EQ Output Spectrum (Bright Emerald Trace): Shows the resulting frequency energy leaving the 12B EQ slot after all active bands are applied.

Because the high-resolution analyzer resolves narrow intervals down into the lowest bass octaves (20 Hz to 250 Hz), you can visually distinguish between the 55 Hz fundamental of a kick drum and the 82 Hz low E string of a bass guitar, place a narrow BELL or NTCH node directly on a ringing 480 Hz snare overtone spike, and watch the emerald post-EQ trace flatten out in real time. On any record-armed track (R), the Dual-Trace RTA remains active even when software Input Monitoring (I) is turned off, allowing you to inspect live microphone spectrum and dial in high-pass or notch filters during zero-latency hardware direct-monitoring sessions.

5.3.3 Per-Band Dynamic EQ (Threshold-Driven Resonance & Mud Control)#

In a live rehearsal or tracking room, a problematic frequency is rarely constant. A rhythm guitar cabinet might sound balanced during open chords but boom violently at 165 Hz only on chugged palm-mutes. A lead vocalist might sound warm in the verse but turn piercing at 3.2 kHz only when belting the chorus. Cutting 165 Hz or 3.2 kHz by -6 dB with a static EQ fixes the loud peaks at the cost of leaving the instrument thin and lifeless for the rest of the song.

To solve this, any of the 12 parametric bands (B1 through B12) in 12B EQ can be switched into Dynamic EQ Mode:

Dynamic Band Parameter Range Default Acoustic Behavior
DYN (Dynamic Enable) Off (Static) / Active Off Activates envelope-driven gain modulation on the selected EQ band (BELL, LSHF, or HSHF).
DYN THRESH (Threshold) -60.0 dB to 0.0 dB -24.0 dB Sets the sidechain bandpass level at which the band begins moving from its static GAIN toward DYN RANGE.
DYN RANGE (Max Excursion) -18.0 dB to +18.0 dB -6.0 dB Sets the maximum dynamic cut (negative values) or dynamic upward expansion boost (positive values) applied when the band's frequency energy exceeds DYN THRESH.
DYN ATTACK 0.5 ms to 100.0 ms 8.0 ms Controls how fast the filter node dips or boosts once the narrow-band sidechain detector crosses threshold.
DYN RELEASE 5.0 ms to 1000.0 ms 80.0 ms Controls how smoothly the EQ band returns to its resting gain after the resonance or boom subsides.

Each active dynamic band runs its own dedicated state-variable bandpass sidechain detector tuned to that band's exact FREQ and Q, updating the audio filter coefficients smoothly every 16 samples. On the EQ & RTA graph, a shaded dynamic excursion halo around the node shows the real-time decibel deflection on every beat.

5.3.4 Vocal Rider: Automatic Zero-Latency Vocal Leveler with Breath & Bleed Freeze Gate#

When a singer performs live in the same room as a loud band, their distance from the microphone capsule naturally shifts between intimate verses and full-voice choruses. Feeding those 12 dB level swings directly into a compressor forces the compressor into heavy -12 dB gain reduction on loud notes while leaving quiet lines buried. Worse, if you try to use a standard automatic gain rider in a live rehearsal room, the rider mistakes the pause between vocal lines for a "quiet vocal" and cranks the fader up by +6 dB, flooding the mix with loud snare and cymbal bleed.

Cave Recorder's Vocal Rider is engineered specifically for live-room vocals, bass, and solo instruments:

  • Target Level (-36.0 dBFS to -6.0 dBFS, default -18.0 dBFS) & Range (±6.0 dB): Smoothly rides the pre-compressor channel level by up to +6.0 dB on quiet phrases and -6.0 dB on loud phrases with zero lookahead latency, delivering a consistent -18 dBFS vocal into your downstream compressor.
  • Speech-Weighted Sidechain Detector (250 Hz to 4.0 kHz): Filters out low-frequency kick/bass thump below 250 Hz and hi-hat sizzle above 4.0 kHz so the gain rider reacts strictly to fundamental vocal body and presence.
  • Breath & Bleed Freeze Gate (Freeze Threshold, -70.0 dBFS to -24.0 dBFS, default -48.0 dBFS): Whenever the speech-weighted vocal energy drops below Freeze Threshold (such as when the singer steps back or takes a breath between phrases), the rider immediately freezes its gain fader (or glides gently toward 0.0 dB unity) so live drum and amplifier room spill is never boosted into the mix.

5.3.5 Split-Band De-Esser & Dynamic Low-Shelf Plosive Arrestor#

Close vocal microphones in rehearsal and live tracking rooms suffer from two distinct transient faults at opposite ends of the spectrum: low-frequency P and B breath blasts (plosives) that thump the subwoofers, and piercing high-frequency S, Sh, and T sibilance (4.5 kHz to 9.0 kHz) that turns harsh when pushed through vocal saturation or plate reverb.

The built-in De-Esser solves both problems in a single zero-latency processor:

  1. Stage 1: Dynamic Low-Shelf Plosive Arrestor (120 Hz): An 80 Hz low-pass transient detector monitors sub-bass air blasts. Normal vocal chest resonance (110 Hz to 250 Hz) passes through completely untouched, but the instant a P or B microphone pop hits below 80 Hz, a fast (0.5 ms attack, 60 ms release) dynamic low-shelf filter at 120 Hz attenuates the low end by up to -18.0 dB, removing the thump without thinning out the singer's voice.
  2. Stage 2: Split-Band Sibilance Suppressor (2.0 kHz to 16.0 kHz, default 6.5 kHz, up to -24.0 dB): Unlike wideband de-essers that duck the entire vocal whenever an S occurs (causing an unnatural "lisp"), the split-band detector isolates only the sibilant frequency band (Sibilance Freq adjustable from 2.0 kHz to 16.0 kHz with default 6.5 kHz, Max Reduction 0.0 dB to -24.0 dB with default -8.0 dB) and compresses only the high-frequency shelf while leaving the 200 Hz to 3.0 kHz vocal vowel core at 100% volume. Engaging SIDECHAIN LISTEN solos the isolated sibilance detector so you can sweep Sibilance Freq to the exact whistle pitch of the singer's S consonants.

5.3.6 Haas-Free Stereo Micro-Pitch Doubler#

A classic studio trick for widening a single mono rhythm guitar, synthesizer lead, or backing vocal is the "Haas delay" (delaying the right channel by 15 ms relative to the left). Unfortunately, summing a static Haas delay to mono (MONO M⊕) creates severe comb-filtering notches that make the instrument sound hollow and phasey on single-speaker PA systems or phones.

The Micro-Pitch Doubler generates lush stereo width that remains 100% solid when folded to mono:

  • Opposite-Polarity Dual Pitch Shifters (Detune: 1.0 to 30.0 cents, default ±9.0 cents): Pitch-shifts the Left wet voice slightly downward (-Detune cents) and the Right wet voice slightly upward (+Detune cents) using dual overlapping Hann-windowed grain buffers driven by a 0.75 Hz quadrature LFO (90° stereo phase offset).
  • Decorrelated Pre-Delay (5.0 ms to 40.0 ms, default 14.0 ms L / 19.0 ms R) & High-Cut Warmth (1.5 kHz to 16.0 kHz): Because the delayed voices are continuously pitch-decorrelated and rolled off in the extreme highs (High Cut), they fuse with the dry center channel to create a wide stereo halo without producing static comb-filter notches in MONO.

5.4 Analog VCA Compressor & Gain Reduction Meter (VCA COMPRESSOR & GR)#

The Analog VCA Compressor (3:VCA CMP) models a classic studio voltage-controlled amplifier dynamics processor (inspired by large-format British console bus compressors and fast American VCA limiters). It combines punchy transient control with a built-in Sidechain High-Pass Filter (SC HPF, shortcut H in the Channel Inspector) and New York Parallel Mix (MIX) stage.

5.4.1 VCA Compressor Parameter Reference#

Parameter / Switch UI Label Range / Presets Default Studio Function
Threshold THRESH -60.0 dB to 0.0 dB -18.0 dB Sets the input level (dBFS) above which gain reduction begins. Drag the yellow threshold node directly on the transfer graph or turn the THRESH knob.
Ratio RATIO (2:1, 4:1, 8:1, 20:1) 1.0:1 to 20.0:1 4.0:1 Determines how strongly signal excursions above THRESH are attenuated. Use the quick-ratio buttons (2:1 gentle leveling, 4:1 studio punch, 8:1 aggressive control, 20:1 peak limiting) or sweep continuously with the RATIO knob.
Attack Time ATTACK 0.1 ms to 100.0 ms 10.0 ms Controls how quickly the VCA gain cell clamps down once a transient crosses THRESH. Slow attacks (15 ms to 35 ms) let drum stick snap pass through uncompressed, while fast attacks (0.5 ms to 3 ms) tame sharp peaks.
Release Time RELEASE 10.0 ms to 1000.0 ms 100.0 ms Controls how fast gain recovers to 0.0 dB after the signal drops below THRESH. Set release so gain reduction recovers smoothly in time with the song's tempo without audible pumping.

5.4.2 Interactive Transfer Curve & Real-Time Gain Reduction (GR) Trace#

The VCA COMPRESSOR & GR graph displays input level (-48 dB to 0 dB) on the horizontal axis against output level (-24 dB to 0 dB) on the vertical axis:

  • Interactive Threshold & Knee Nodes: Drag the highlighted gold node along the diagonal line to set THRESH, and drag the upper slope handle (or click 2:1, 4:1, 8:1, 20:1) to tilt the compression ratio above threshold.
  • Scrolling Gain Reduction (GR Trace): As audio passes through the compressor, a shaded crimson trace sweeps across the graph showing instantaneous and historical gain reduction depth in decibels. Watching the GR Trace alongside the waveform makes it easy to dial ATTACK and RELEASE so the compressor breathes cleanly between snare hits or vocal phrases.

Each external sidechain route provides a selectable tap point (PRE-INS, POST-EQ, PRE-FDR, or POST-FDR), a dedicated -24.0 dB to +24.0 dB SIDECHAIN TRIM, a SIDECHAIN LISTEN audition switch (which also lights SOLO (N)·CLEAR in the Top Deck so you never leave sidechain audition stuck on), and an optional compressor Sidechain Low-Pass Filter (SIDECHAIN LPF, 200 Hz to 20.0 kHz, default 12.0 kHz) so you can duck a bass DI or fuzz guitar cleanly from the fundamental thump of the kick drum (80 Hz to 250 Hz) without false-triggering on high-frequency beater click. Cave Recorder automatically validates the routing graph to prevent feedback cycles and applies slot-level Plugin Delay Compensation across all sidechain taps.

5.4.5 Context-Aware 3-Variant Noise Gate (Expander, Drum Bleed, Amp Dynamic)#

Standard threshold noise gates are notorious for ruining live band recordings: on drums they false-trigger on loud snare hits and let bursts of harsh cymbal wash through on every tom decay, while on high-gain guitar amplifiers they either chop off quiet fingerpicked notes and intentional feedback sustain or sit wide open while fuzz pedals hum at -22 dBFS.

Cave Recorder replaces conventional gating with a Context-Aware 3-Variant Noise Gate tailored to the physics of the source instrument:

+====================================================================+
|          CONTEXT-AWARE 3-VARIANT STUDIO NOISE GATE MODES           |
+====================================================================+
  [1] EXPANDER (Vocal, Acoustic & Room Cleanup)
      * Smooth Downward Ratio (1.2:1 .. 10:1) + Dual-Threshold Hysteresis
      * Gently lowers background floor by -6..-18 dB without hard cutoffs
  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  [2] DRUM BLEED (Rack Tom, Floor Tom & Kick / Snare Isolation)
      * Differential Detector: E_key (Resonant Fundamental) - alpha * E_ref
      * One-Click [LRN] Auto-Detects Drum Fundamental Pitch (55..350 Hz)
      * 1.5 ms Lookahead + < 0.25 ms Attack preserves 100% of stick snap
      * Dynamic Decay Low-Pass Filter sweeps 20 kHz -> 250..800 Hz (380 Hz)
        so hi-hat and cymbal bleed vanish during the tom ring-out!
  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  [3] AMP DYNAMIC (Stoner, Doom, Psych & High-Gain Guitar / Bass Rigs)
      * Autocorrelation Pitch Periodicity (H in [0, 1]) + Spectral Flatness
      * Whisper Clean Lock: Pitched notes (H > 0.65) stay open at -34 dBFS
      * Feedback Bloom Lock: Harmonic sustain (H > 0.80) holds 1.5..5.0 s
      * Palm-Mute Clamp: Chug stops clamp 60 Hz hum & fuzz hiss in 15..40 ms
        along a click-free S-Curve + Split-Band [HF Tame]
+====================================================================+

Variant 1: Expander (Smooth Downward Expander)

Designed for lead vocals, horns, and acoustic instruments where a hard gate cut would sound unnatural. Below Open Threshold (with independent Close Threshold hysteresis to prevent chatter), the expander attenuates the floor smoothly according to Ratio (1.2:1 to 10.0:1) down to a musical Range / Floor ceiling (for example, -12.0 dB), tucking headphone bleed and stage shuffle down into the mix without ever dropping to dead digital silence.

Variant 2: Drum Bleed (Differential Tom/Snare Bleed Gate with [LRN] & Dynamic Decay LPF)

When a loud snare rimshot sits 40 cm from a rack tom microphone, the snare spill inside the tom mic is often nearly as loud in broad decibels as a medium tom fill. Drum Bleed separates the target drum from adjacent spill through four specialized stages:

  1. Resonant Sidechain Fundamental Filter & One-Click [LRN] Fundamental Lock: A high-Q (Q = 4.0) resonant bandpass filter focuses the detector on the specific fundamental pitch of the drum shell (55 Hz to 350 Hz, default 110 Hz). Clicking [LRN] while the drummer hits the tom (or while playing back a single tom hit on the timeline) runs a parabolic spectral peak detector that automatically locks Key Freq to that exact drum shell resonance (for example, 110 Hz on a 12" rack tom or 78 Hz on a 16" floor tom).
  2. Differential Spill Rejection (E_key - alpha * E_ref): Compares the energy inside the drum's fundamental bandpass filter against high-frequency snare wire and cymbal reference energy (> 800 Hz). Even a massive snare rimshot or crash cymbal burst has high E_ref relative to E_key, so the differential detector rejects the snare hit and keeps the tom gate shut.
  3. 1.5 ms Lookahead & Ultra-Fast < 0.25 ms Attack: Opens the gate slightly ahead of the physical stick impact so the initial 4 kHz stick transient is never dulled or clicked.
  4. Envelope-Driven Dynamic Decay Low-Pass Filter (20 kHz down to 250..800 Hz, default 380 Hz): When a tom is struck, the audio path opens at full 20 kHz bandwidth so the stick attack snaps clearly. As the tom decays over the next 40 ms to 300 ms, the drum's own high frequencies vanish quickly while its 80 Hz - 150 Hz fundamental keeps ringing. Drum Bleed automatically sweeps a smooth 12 dB/oct low-pass filter from 20 kHz down to an adjustable 250 Hz to 800 Hz cutoff (default 380 Hz) in lockstep with the tom decay envelope, filtering out 100% of the harsh hi-hat and cymbal bleed during the tom ring-out while letting the warm low-end drum resonance sustain naturally.

Variant 3: Amp Dynamic (Stoner, Doom & Psychedelic High-Gain Guitar & Bass Gate)

In stoner rock, doom, sludge, psychedelic rock, space rock, and blues-rock, guitarists and bassists rely on high-gain tube heads driven by cascaded fuzz, overdrive, and boost pedals. This creates an impossible problem for conventional amplitude-threshold noise gates:

  • The Idle Noise Floor is Loud (-22 dBFS): When the guitarist stops playing, stacked fuzz and tube stages produce loud 50/60 Hz transformer hum, rectifier buzz, and wideband thermal hiss around -26 dBFS to -22 dBFS.
  • Clean Fingerpicking is Quieter than the Fuzz Floor (-34 dBFS): When the guitarist rolls back their guitar volume knob or kicks off a fuzz pedal for a hypnotic clean psychedelic intro, the delicate fingerpicked notes sit down around -34 dBFS (12 dB below the loud fuzz noise floor). Any standard noise gate set to -20 dBFS to block fuzz hum will completely mute the clean intro!
  • Intentional Feedback Bloom vs. Tight Palm-Mute Stops: At the end of a doom riff, the guitarist may hold a chord in front of the cabinet for 5 seconds, letting it morph into singing harmonic feedback (Feedback Bloom), and then suddenly slam a tight staccato palm-mute stop (Chug Stop) where the room must drop dead silent in 18 ms to 22 ms.

Amp Dynamic solves this by analyzing signal physics rather than raw volume alone, combining an Autocorrelation Pitch Periodicity / Harmonicity Detector (H ∈ [0, 1]) across the 55 Hz to 1,200 Hz guitar/bass fundamental range with a Spectral Flatness / Entropy Measure (SFM ∈ [0, 1]):

Musical Playing State Acoustic Signature (H & SFM) Automatic Amp Dynamic Response
Quiet Clean Fingerpicking (-34 dBFS) High pitch periodicity (H > 0.65), concentrated harmonic partials Whisper Clean Lock: Lowers the effective gate threshold by up to 18 dB whenever coherent string periodicity is detected, keeping delicate -34 dBFS clean notes and long acoustic-style sustains wide open without touching a knob.
Sustained Harmonic Amp Feedback Very high periodicity (H > 0.80), near-sinusoidal low spectral flatness Feedback Bloom Lock: Recognizes intentional harmonic cabinet feedback and stretches release hold to 1.5 s .. 5.0 s (1500..5000 ms, default 2.5 s) so singing feedback tails never choke or sputter out.
Abrupt Palm-Mute Riff Stop (Chug) Rapid broadband energy drop (-12 dB in < 15 ms) + high-entropy pick/palm damping (SFM > 0.55, H < 0.25) 15 ms .. 40 ms Palm-Mute Clamp (default 18 ms .. 22 ms): Immediately overrides the slow sustain release and clamps 50/60 Hz hum and fuzz roar shut in 15 ms to 40 ms (default 18 ms to 22 ms) along a click-free S-curve.
Long Fading Chord Tail Gradually declining harmonic energy with rising > 3.5 kHz fuzz hiss Split-Band HF Tame Dynamic De-Hisser: Smoothly shelves down high-frequency white-noise fizz above 3.5 kHz as the chord fades while leaving the warm 100 Hz - 1.5 kHz tube sustain untouched.

5.4.6 Guitar & Bass Amp Rig ([CIR] Tube Circuit Models, HEAD ON/BYP & [NAM] Neural Amp Capture)#

Recording a direct instrument (DI) feed alongside (or instead of) a loud stage amplifier gives a band complete freedom to re-voice guitar and bass tones after rehearsal, track late at night on headphones, or bring their exact personal tube heads and fuzz pedals inside the console without carrying heavy cabinets to every session.

Cave Recorder's Amp Rig processor combines an input calibration stage (dBu-referenced headroom Trim, INST/LINE pad, and one-click AUTO-CAL), an overdrive/fuzz stompbox boost stage (BOOST + DRV), two selectable amplifier engines ([CIR] Physical Tube Circuit Models vs. [NAM] Native .nam Neural Amp Models), a 4-control passive tone stack (BASS, MID, TREBLE, PRESENCE), power-amp transformer SAG, an independent HEAD ON / HEAD BYP amplifier head bypass toggle, and an integrated Speaker Cabinet & Microphone stage (8 modeled speaker cabinets plus external .wav/.nam linear impulse responses, 5 studio microphone capsules, continuous POS and AIR, and a CAB BYP toggle):

  1. [CIR] Mode (8 Physical Vacuum-Tube Amplifier Topologies with 2x / 4x Anti-Aliasing Oversampling):
    • Models triode/pentode grid conduction, cathode bias shift, power-supply RC sag, and output transformer core hysteresis across 8 classic guitar and bass amplifier voicings: CLN65 (65 CLEAN 2x6L6 VIBRATO), JMP59 (59 JUMPED 4xEL34 LEAD), BRT80 (80 BRIT 3x12AX7 MASTER), CTR100 (CITRUS 4x12AX7 DIRTY), 5STG (5-STAGE 6L6 HIGH-GAIN), D-REC (MODERN OPEN-LOOP 5U4G), DM150 (73 ULTRALINEAR 4x6550), and BS300 (69 BAXANDALL 6x6550 BASS).
