  2. HEAD ON / HEAD BYP & CAB BYP (Independent Head and Cabinet Bypass):
    • Toggling HEAD BYP bypasses the preamp, overdrive boost, tone stack, and power-amp stages while keeping Amp Rig's speaker cabinet and microphone section active (ideal when tracking a physical tube head's load-box line out that only needs speaker cabinet voicing).
    • Conversely, toggling CAB BYP inside Amp Rig bypasses its internal speaker cabinet so you can insert stereo rack processors (Modulation, 3-Mode Delay, or Studio Plate Reverb) in downstream rack slots and place a standalone Cab IR (SPEAKER CABINET & IR LOADER) processor after them (Amp Rig [CAB BYP] -> Stereo Chorus/Delay -> Cab IR).
  3. [NAM] Mode (Native .nam Neural Amp Real-Time Inference & Self-Contained Library):
    • Loads open .nam (Neural Amp Modeler) files (including v0.7.0 multi-size nested/slimmable A2 capture profiles alongside A1 Standard and Feather/Lite architectures) directly into the channel strip with zero-latency real-time inference, anti-aliasing oversampling, and automatic sample-rate conversion when running sessions at 44.1 kHz, 48.0 kHz, 88.2 kHz, or 96.0 kHz.
    • Two-Tier Self-Contained .nam Storage: Imported or captured .nam profiles are indexed in your global studio library (<LibraryRoot>/.caverec/amp_captures/, along with optional return_wet.flac archives for later higher-quality re-training via RE-TRAIN HQ (WET WAV)) and are automatically copied into <SessionFolder>/models/ and <TakeFolder>/models/ whenever assigned to a strip. Every Session and Take remains 100% self-contained when synced to Google Drive or opened on a bandmate's laptop without broken external file paths.
  4. 3-Step Guided Hardware Amp & Pedal Capture Wizard (CAP) & Mastering Trainer:

    • Step 1 (Hardware Patch, Preset Selection & Loopback Level Check): Select the physical RE-AMP SEND output jack (OUT 01..18, feeding your amp/pedal input via a re-amp box) and MIC / DI RETURN input jack (IN 01..18, from your load box, attenuator line out, or cabinet microphone). Click the header preset selector button to cycle between the three training quality modes (Standard -> Mastering -> Turbo -> Standard):

    • Mastering (PRESET: MASTERING): Maximum-accuracy mode using the full 3-minute conditioning sweep, up to 1,000 training passes, automatic best-checkpoint retention, adaptive step-size refinement on plateaus, and automatic early stopping when accuracy converges.

Click TEST LOOPBACK & LEVEL to play a test burst through the hardware, verify return peak headroom (-18 to -3 dBFS) and signal-to-noise ratio (>= 36 dB), and lock sub-sample roundtrip latency and clock drift (PPM).

At any point during training, you can click STOP & KEEP BEST to finish immediately while keeping the best validated model weights and running the post-training sanity audit (or click CANCEL to abort and discard the run).

Feedback Regeneration FB 0% to 95% drag bar (98% max) 35% Controls how much delayed output is fed back into the virtual record head (0% for a single slapback repeat, 25% to 45% for natural fading trails, and up to 95%/98% for sustained dub tape repeats without runaway clipping).
Ping-Pong Width & Toggle PP (PP 60%) Off / Active (0% to 100% width) Active (60%) Alternates echo repeats between the left and right channels at the selected stereo spread width (PP 60%) while keeping AUX 2 TAPE DLY solo-safe.

5.5.3 3-Mode Delay (Capstan Tape, BBD Analog, Pristine Digital) & Dynamic Ducking#

Whether used on AUX 2 TAPE DLY or inserted directly into any channel or subgroup rack slot, Cave Recorder's delay processor offers three distinct physical delay architectures plus a built-in Dynamic Ducking envelope:

Delay Mode Physical Circuit Model Sonic & Spectral Behavior Ideal Studio Uses
Capstan Tape Multi-head magnetic tape transport with capstan wow and flutter (WOW), oxide saturation inside the feedback path, head-bump low-end warmth, and progressive high-cut (DMP). Warm, evolving repeats that never clash with the dry vocal or guitar lead, capable of self-oscillating dub swells at FB > 90% without digital clipping. Psychedelic guitar solos, dub/space-rock throws, rockabilly vocal slapback (85 ms), and horn section depth.
BBD Analog Classic 4096-stage Bucket-Brigade Device (BBD) charge-transfer delay line (Delay Time 10 ms to 600 ms physical BBD ceiling, default 300 ms) with pre-emphasis/de-emphasis compander breathe, clock-rate-linked 24 dB/oct low-pass filters (4.8 kHz at short delays down to 1.6 kHz at long delays), subtle even-order warmth, and authentic -72 dBFS clock whine at long delay times. Dark, murky, slightly gritty repeats that melt directly behind the dry instrument like a vintage analog pedalboard stompbox. Stoner/doom lead guitar ambiance, krautrock motorik synth arpeggios, and atmospheric dark vocals.
Pristine Digital Phase-accurate 32-bit floating-point stereo delay line (1 ms to 2000 ms) with adjustable Low-Cut, High-Cut, Ping-Pong Width, independent Right-channel ratio (RT) or musical subdivision (R.DV), and zero pitch drift. Crystal-clear rhythmic repeats with exact transient definition. Tight dotted-eighth rhythmic guitar patterns, 4:3 stereo bounce delays, stereo keyboard widening, and percussive echoes.
  • Built-In Dynamic Ducking (Ducking: 0.0 dB to -24.0 dB): Monitors the dry input envelope and automatically attenuates the wet delay repeats while the vocalist or guitarist is actively playing a phrase. The moment the phrase ends, the ducking releases (180 ms) and the delay tail blooms up to full volume in the spaces between lines.

Tempo-Synced Stereo Delay ([SYNC], 18 Musical Subdivisions & Smooth Capstan Glide)

Clicking SYNC next to the delay time bar on AUX 2 (or inside the Large Processor View) locks echo repeats directly to Cave Recorder's live studio tempo (driven by a hardware floor looper, 4-tap count-in in MIDI SYNC, or the native Drum Machine's STUDIO CLK, and falling back smoothly to 120.0 BPM when SYNC: FREE so toggling SYNC before capturing a loop remains musical):

  • Lossless TM / DV Switching Across 18 Musical Subdivisions: When SYNC is engaged (emerald when locked to a live tempo, gold on 120.0 BPM fallback), the delay time slider switches from milliseconds (TM) to stepped musical subdivisions (DV, defaulting to dotted eighth 1/8D): 1/64, 32T, 1/32, 16T, 32D, 1/16, 1/8T, 16D, 1/8, 1/4T, 1/8D, 1/4, 1/2T, 1/4D, 1/2, 1BAR, 2BAR, and 4BAR. Disengaging SYNC restores your exact prior free-mode millisecond setting without losing a single tweak.
  • Smooth Tempo Glide: When you tap a new tempo, close a new floor loop, or trigger 0.5x/2.0x rational scaling in MIDI SYNC, the delay target slews smoothly rather than jumping abruptly, producing an authentic analog capstan or BBD clock pitch glide in Capstan Tape and BBD Analog and a click-free transition in Pristine Digital.
  • Independent Right-Channel Polyrhythm (R.DV) in Pristine Digital: Engaging SYNC in Pristine Digital converts the Right-channel ratio slider (RT) into an independent R.DV subdivision selector (default 1/8), making classic 4:3 stereo patterns (such as 1/4 Left against 1/8D Right) effortless.
  • Physical Delay Horizon Badges & Beat-Grid Visualizer: When a slow subdivision exceeds a delay model's physical ceiling (600 ms in BBD Analog or 2000 ms in Capstan Tape and Pristine Digital), the delay clamps cleanly with no audio artifacts and displays CLAMP 600ms (or CLAMP 2.0s) in the visualizer alongside subtle quarter-note beat-grid hairlines behind the echo taps.

5.5.4 4-Pole Non-Linear Resonant Ladder Filter (with Envelope Follower & Sidechain)#

The Ladder Filter models a classic transistor ladder low-pass filter with two selectable low-pass slopes (2P 12 dB/octave 2-pole low-pass and 4P 24 dB/octave 4-pole low-pass, default 4P) and per-stage analog saturation:

  • Cutoff (20 Hz to 16,000 Hz, default 1,200 Hz) & Resonance (0% to 100% Self-Oscillation): Sweeps the resonant peak from deep sub-bass thunder to harmonic self-oscillation.
  • Class-A Input Drive (0.0 dB to +24.0 dB) & Bass Comp (0% to 100%, default 50%): Standard 4-pole ladder filters lose low-end weight when high negative feedback (Resonance) is applied. Turning up Bass Comp restores the sub-bass fundamental before the feedback summer so bass guitars and synthesizers keep their chest-thumping low end even at aggressive resonance settings.
  • Bi-Directional Envelope Follower (Env Depth -5.0 to +5.0 octaves / -60 to +60 semitones), Fast / Smooth Response Speeds & External Sidechain: Sweeps the filter cutoff upward or downward in proportion to input pluck dynamics with selectable Fast (3 ms attack / 60 ms release for snappy funk bass and guitar auto-wah) and Smooth (25 ms attack / 300 ms release for liquid psychedelic sweeps) detector ballistics, or locks onto an external kick-drum sidechain so a fuzz bass or synth drone pumps rhythmically with the drummer.

5.5.5 Algorithmic Studio Plate Reverb & 4-Mode Modulation Suite#

When you want dedicated reverb or modulation inside an individual channel or Subgroup Bus rack slot alongside AUX 1 REVERB, Cave Recorder provides two zero-latency rack processors:

  1. Algorithmic Studio Plate Reverb (4-Stage Allpass Diffuser + 8-Line Feedback Delay Network):
    • Uses four series allpass diffusers feeding an 8-channel Feedback Delay Network (FDN) with slow quadrature delay-tap modulation and independent two-band crossover damping (Bass Mult vs. High Damping).
    • Controls include Pre-Delay (0..150 ms, default 10 ms), Decay Time (0.4..8.0 s, default 2.2 s), High Damping (1.0..16.0 kHz, default 6.5 kHz), Bass Mult (0.4x..1.5x, default 0.9x), Diffusion (0%..100%, default 80%), Pre HPF (20..500 Hz, default 80 Hz), Pre LPF (2.0..20.0 kHz, default 12.0 kHz), Stereo Width (0%..150%, default 100%), and Wet/Dry Mix (0%..100%).
  2. 4-Mode Studio Modulation (Through-Zero Flanger, Dimension Chorus, Optical Phaser, Harmonic Tremolo):
    • Through-Zero Flanger (Authentic Dual-Tape Through-Zero Flanging): Delays the dry reference path by a fixed 2.5 ms offset while sweeping the modulated wet tape path from 0.05 ms to 4.95 ms with saturated feedback (-95% to +95%). As the modulated path crosses 2.5 ms, it passes straight through zero relative delay (t = 0), creating the unmistakable deep jet-whoosh null and phase inversion of two studio reel-to-reel tape machines pressed by thumb on the supply flange.
    • Dimension Chorus (Motionless 3D Stereo Widener): Models a classic 4-button studio dimension unit using dual triangle-wave BBD delay lines driven in quadrature with cross-blended anti-phase high-pass dry/wet matrixing. Expands mono guitars, keys, and vocals into a wide, motionless 3D stereo image without the seasick pitch warble of standard choruses.
    • Optical Phaser (4, 6, 8, or 12-Stage Photocell Allpass Phaser): Cascades 4, 6, 8, or 12 first-order allpass stages modulated by an asymmetric incandescent-lamp / photocell envelope (15 ms fast light-up attack vs. 120 ms logarithmic dark recovery) for liquid, swirling stoner/psych-rock guitar and electric piano movement.
    • Harmonic Tremolo (Dual-Band Linkwitz-Riley Crossover Tremolo): Splits the signal at a 400 Hz Linkwitz-Riley crossover and modulates the low band (< 400 Hz) and high band (> 400 Hz) 180° out of phase. While treble rises, bass dips (and vice versa), creating a warm, hypnotic vintage amplifier pulse that never drops the perceived volume of the track in the mix.
    • Tempo-Synced LFO Rate ([SYNC]) & Clickless Downbeat Phase-Lock ([LCK]): All four modulation modes support musical tempo sync alongside free 0.05..12.00 Hz operation:
    • Click SYNC to switch the rate control from free Hz (RATE) to musical note subdivisions (SYNC: 16T, 32D, 1/16, 1/8T, 16D, 1/8, 1/4T, 1/8D, 1/4, 1/2T, 1/4D, 1/2 [default], 1BAR, 2BAR, and 4BAR), locked to MIDI SYNC or the Drum Machine's STUDIO CLK (120.0 BPM fallback when SYNC: FREE). Turning SYNC off restores your exact free Hz rate.
    • Click LCK (available when SYNC is active) to engage clickless proportional downbeat phase-lock. Rather than hard-resetting LFO phase on Beat 1 (which would cause comb-filter or amplitude clicks in a flanger, phaser, or tremolo), LCK smoothly pulls the modulation cycle crest into exact alignment with Beat 1 within ~25 ms with zero audio discontinuities, indicated by an emerald downbeat phase-anchor tick on the modulation visualizer.

5.6 Automatic Multi-Mic Phase & Polarity Alignment (ALIGN ALL & Φ)#

When recording a drum kit, guitar cabinet, acoustic piano, or horn section with multiple microphones, physical distance differences between capsules create acoustic arrival-time offsets. Sound travels through studio air at approximately 343 meters per second (1,125 feet per second), meaning every 34.3 cm (13.5 inches) of extra distance between a close microphone and an overhead or room microphone delays the acoustic wavefront by 1.0 millisecond (1000 microseconds, or 48 samples at 48.0 kHz).

5.6.1 Why Multi-Mic Time Offsets Cause Comb Filtering & Hollow Low End#

When two microphones capture the same instrument at slightly different arrival times and are summed together on DRUM BUS or MST MASTER BUS:

  • Frequencies whose half-wavelength matches the time offset arrive 180° out of phase and cancel each other out, carving deep, hollow notches across the frequency spectrum (known as comb filtering).
  • A snare drum captured by both 02SnrTp (close dynamic mic) and 03OvrhdL (condenser mic 63 cm / 25 inches above the snare) suffers a 1.85 ms (1850 us) arrival delay at the overhead capsule. Without phase alignment, summing the overheads with the close snare mic thins out the 200 Hz snare body and smears the initial stick transient into a double flam.
  • Similarly, a snare bottom microphone pointed upward at the snare wires moves in the opposite mechanical direction from the top snare microphone, requiring a 180° polarity inversion (Ø) in addition to time alignment.

5.6.2 Running ALIGN ALL & Auditioning with PHASE: ALIGN / PHASE A/B#

Cave Recorder eliminates manual waveform sliding and guesswork through its built-in Sub-Sample Multi-Mic Phase & Polarity Alignment engine:

  1. Record a Short Pass or Play Back an Existing Take: Have the drummer play the full kit for a few bars (or load any recorded Take on the timeline).
  2. Click ALIGN ALL in the Top Deck (or Φ ALIGN ALL on the Console Bar): Cave Recorder analyzes the active Take's recorded multi-track Broadcast Wave .wav files on disk (or the live rolling capture memory if no recorded Take files exist yet) using sub-sample bandpass (150 Hz to 6 kHz) cross-correlation within a +-25 ms acoustic window, delaying closer microphones forward in time to match the furthest reference microphone. Every pass records its batch provenance so ALIGN ALL groups and aligns simultaneously recorded ACOUSTIC MIC channels independently per recording batch (for example, aligning a Base Pass drum kit together and a multi-mic Overdub acoustic guitar together without ever cross-correlating overdubs against earlier passes), while automatically skipping ISOLATED DI strips, Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments, and External MIDI tracks. The entire multi-track phase and polarity alignment operation is captured as a single undoable step so you can revert or reapply it at any time with CMD/CTRL + Z.
  3. Inspect Per-Channel Ø and Φ Readouts: Within milliseconds, each aligned channel strip updates its header telemetry and phase buttons:
    • Ø (Cyan Polarity Badge, SHIFT + P on inspected strip): Engages automatically on any channel whose acoustic waveform is inverted 180° relative to the reference microphone (such as CH02 02SnrTp or a bottom snare mic).
    • Φ (Emerald Phase Align Badge) & Microsecond Readout: Engages sub-sample time alignment (0.00 ms to +50.00 ms, displayed in microseconds from 0us to 50000us, such as 420us on CH02 and 1850us on CH03) so all wavefronts arrive at the subgroup summing bus at the exact same sub-sample instant.
  4. A/B Audition Globally (PHASE A/B): Click PHASE A/B in Top Deck Row 1 to toggle all phase and polarity corrections in and out across the entire console simultaneously. You will immediately hear the kick and snare low-end punch tighten up and the stereo center image snap into focus. Both Trigger Global Multi-Mic Phase Align and Trigger Phase Align on Inspected Track can also be bound to custom keyboard shortcuts in KEYMAP (CMD/CTRL + 8).
Individual Channel Override (Ø & Φ)

If you want to keep distant ambient room microphones unaligned to preserve natural acoustic room size while keeping close drum mics and overheads tightly phase-locked, simply click the green Φ button on the room mic channel strip to disengage phase delay on that specific track while leaving PHASE: ALIGN active on the rest of the kit.

5.6.3 Why Delay Alone Cannot Fix Ported Cabinets, Bass DI + Amp, or Dispersive Drum Kits#

Sub-sample time-of-flight delay (Φ) and 180° polarity inversion (Ø) solve pure physical distance offsets through air. However, in real rehearsal rooms and tracking studios, multi-mic sources also suffer from frequency-dependent phase dispersion (non-linear group delay):

  • Bass DI + Miked Ported Bass Cabinet: A tuned bass-reflex cabinet port acts as a high-order acoustic high-pass resonator around 45 Hz to 85 Hz, rotating the phase of the low E and A strings by 90° to 180° relative to the upper harmonics at 400 Hz. Even after you align the initial pick transient in time (Φ), the 60 Hz fundamental from the cabinet mic can sit 140° out of phase with the DI box, stealing 6 dB to 12 dB of sub-bass weight when both faders are up.
  • Multi-Mic Drum Kits & Dual-Mic Guitar Cabinets: Drum shell resonances, off-axis cardioid proximity filters, and loudspeaker crossover networks rotate low-frequency phase differently from midrange transient phase. No single time delay or 180° polarity switch can bring both 65 Hz kick chest thump and 2.5 kHz beater attack into 0° constructive alignment simultaneously.

5.6.4 Zero-Slot Top-of-Strip Phase Align Network & Mode 1 Instant Binary Polarity Maximizer (< 50 ms)#

To solve both broadband polarity conflicts and frequency-dependent phase dispersion without consuming a single slot in your 8-slot insert rack, every Input Track strip in Cave Recorder includes a dedicated, zero-slot Phase Align Network wired directly into the top of the channel strip alongside Ø and Φ:

+====================================================================+
|     TOP-OF-STRIP ZERO-SLOT PHASE & POLARITY ALIGNMENT NETWORK      |
+====================================================================+
  Channel Input (Post-Trim TRM)
         |
         v
  [1] Broadband Polarity Switch [Ø] (+1 or -1 / 180°)
         |
         v
  [2] Sub-Sample Time-of-Flight Delay [Φ] (0 .. 50,000 us)
         |
         v
  [3] Zero-Slot 5-Stage Cascaded Allpass Phase Align Network:
      * Stage 0: 1st-Order Low-Frequency Rotator (f_0 in 20..500 Hz)
      * Stages 1..4: 4x 2nd-Order Biquad Allpass (f_k in 20..12,000 Hz,
                     Q_k in 0.30..3.50, default 0.707)
      * Unified 10 ms Dual-Branch Linear Crossfader for click-free
        live auditioning between Candidates A / B / C / D and Bypass!
+====================================================================+

Cave Recorder's Polarity & Phase Maximizer operates in two distinct modes depending on whether you are in the middle of a fast rehearsal or dialing in a final studio mix:

Mode 1: Instant Binary Polarity Maximizer (< 50 ms)

When you need an immediate, zero-filter polarity check across all 18 channels right after tracking:

  1. Connected Acoustic Group Partitioning: Cave Recorder builds the 18 x 18 pairwise broadband cross-correlation matrix across active performance regions and partitions channels into independent acoustic groups (for example, grouping the 8 drum microphones into Group 1 and the bass DI + mic'd cabinet pair into Group 2 while ignoring uncorrelated synth DI tracks).
  2. Exact Global Polarity Maximizer: Within each group, the solver evaluates every possible binary polarity combination in under 50 milliseconds to maximize total constructive summed energy across four selectable studio weighting criteria:
    • Low-End Weight (30 Hz - 200 Hz Punch): Applies a band-limited 30 Hz to 200 Hz low-end punch weighting so kick, snare body, and bass fundamentals never cancel out.
    • Broadband Loudness (ITU-R BS.1770-4 K-Weighted LUFS): Maximizes full-spectrum perceived K-weighted loudness across the summed mix.
    • Transient Crest & Impact (60 Hz - 6 kHz + Top-K Transient Crest Re-Scoring): Optimizes 60 Hz to 6 kHz punch and re-scores the top-energy transient windows so drum stick crack and guitar pick attack hit with maximum crest factor.
    • Anti-Comb Spectral Smoothness: Minimizes deep phase-cancellation notches across the frequency spectrum so multi-mic sources sum smoothly without hollow comb filtering.
  3. Safe Audition Backup: Auditioning Mode 1 or Mode 2 candidates automatically backs up your complete per-channel phase state (Ø, delay Φ, and allpass settings) so canceling or closing the popover restores your exact original console state.

5.6.5 Mode 2: Deep Multicore Spectral Phase & Allpass Solver (Anytime 30 s .. 30 min)#

When you want to lock a multi-mic drum kit, a bass DI + mic'd bass cabinet rig, or a dual-mic guitar cabinet into 0° constructive phase coherence across the entire frequency spectrum, open the Polarity & Phase Maximizer and run Mode 2: Deep Multicore Spectral Phase & Allpass Solver:

  1. Compact 256-Bin Cross-Spectral Profile: Cave Recorder scans the highest-energy active performance windows of the Take once and condenses them into a compact 256-bin log-spaced cross-spectral profile (20 Hz to 20 kHz, with biquad allpass pole centers spanning 20 Hz to 12 kHz). Because all subsequent optimization runs purely against this in-memory spectral profile (< 500 KB), all CPU cores can evaluate millions of allpass filter configurations per second without touching the disk.
  2. Multicore Spectral Phase Optimization (Anytime 30 s .. 30 min Budget):
    • Theoretical Coherence Upper Bound & Efficiency Gauge: Computes the exact mathematical upper bound on the maximum energy achievable if every channel had an ideal phase rotator at every frequency bin. The UI displays your current solution as a live Coherence Efficiency % gauge against this theoretical ceiling (for example, 98.7% of theoretical maximum, +4.8 dB low-end gain recovered).
    • Global Trajectory Search & Continuous Pole Polish: Searches across log-frequency bins to find globally optimal allpass filter trajectories and refines continuous pole frequencies f_k and bandwidths Q_k to maximize summed phase coherence across all microphones.
    • Multicore Parallel Search Across Phase Barriers: Runs parallel worker threads across CPU cores to explore both broad polarity inversions, low-frequency rotators, multi-band biquad allpass stages, and microsecond time-of-flight alignment without getting trapped in local phase cancellations.
  3. Live Candidates A, B, C, D & [GAIN-MATCH AUDITION]:
    • You can choose a quick 30 s, 2 m, 5 m, or 30 m time budget (or click [STOP & KEEP BEST] at any instant). As the solver runs, it continuously populates four distinct studio candidate slots ordered from zero-dispersion polarity to full wavefront + allpass alignment that you can click to audition live with a click-free 10 ms crossfade:
    • [CANDIDATE A: PURE Ø - ZERO DISPERSION]: Optimal binary 180° polarity inversions only (0 active allpass stages, 0.0 us time shift) for zero group-delay dispersion.
    • [CANDIDATE B: TIGHT LOW-END LOCK - MINIMAL POLES]: Broadband polarity plus at most the 1st-order LF rotator and 1 low-frequency biquad allpass stage (<= 250 Hz, group delay < 2.5 ms, 0.0 us time shift) to lock kick and bass fundamentals while keeping midrange transients untouched.
    • [CANDIDATE C: DEEP MULTI-BAND ALLPASS]: Broadband polarity plus up to the full 5-stage allpass cascade (1st-order LF rotator + 4 biquads, group delay <= 6.0 ms, 0.0 us time shift) for maximum multi-band phase coherence.
    • [CANDIDATE D: FULL WAVEFRONT + ALLPASS]: Jointly optimizes causal microsecond time-of-flight alignment (0..25,000 us) on unlocked spot microphones alongside broadband polarity and the sparse 5-stage allpass cascade.
    • [GAIN-MATCH AUDITION] Toggle: Because constructive phase alignment naturally increases summed bus volume by 3 dB to 8 dB, enabling [GAIN-MATCH AUDITION] automatically normalizes the summed output loudness (clamped to ±12.0 dB) to match the unaligned bypass signal. This lets you verify that the low end is genuinely tighter, punchier, and more articulate rather than merely louder before clicking [APPLY SELECTED TO CONSOLE].

5.7 Hosting External CLAP & Audio Unit Plugins (1:PLUGIN, PDC & Low-Latency Monitoring)#

While Cave Recorder's built-in TAPE, 12B EQ, VCA CMP, DE-ESS, GATE, REPAIR, RIDER, AUX 1 REVERB, and AUX 2 TAPE DLY processors cover 95% of studio tracking and mixing tasks with zero added latency, any of the eight insert slots (Slots 1..8) on any Input Track (CH01..CH32) or Subgroup Bus (SUB 1..SUB 16) can host third-party CLAP (Clever Audio Plug-in, .clap) effects across macOS, Windows, and Linux as well as native macOS Audio Unit (AUv3 and AUv2) audio effects ('aufx' and 'aumf'). In addition, any Input Track's Zone-2 Input Stage ([INST]) can host Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments, including CLAP instruments (cross-platform), macOS Audio Unit Music Devices ('aumu'), and Cave Recorder's native Virtual Analog Drum Machine, printing live synth and keyboard performances straight into standard 32-bit float .wav Pass stems (rec/*.wav) and true stereo 30-minute RETRO memory.

5.7.1 Scanning & Loading .clap & Audio Unit Plugins into the 8-Slot Rack#

Cave Recorder maintains a persistent, machine-local plugin index (clap_plugin_index.json inside your user configuration directory) covering two studio plugin architectures:

Plugin Format Supported Platforms Standard System Discovery Locations & Identifiers
CLAP (.clap) macOS, Windows, Linux macOS: /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/CLAP and ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/CLAP
Windows: C:\Program Files\Common Files\CLAP and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Common\CLAP
Linux: ~/.clap and /usr/lib/clap
Custom: Any folder added via + ADD SEARCH FOLDER..., any file added via + ADD .CLAP FILE..., or directories listed in the CLAP_PATH environment variable. Indexed by canonical reverse-URI identifier (such as org.surge-synth-team.surge-xt-fx).
Audio Unit (AUv3 & AUv2) macOS ('aufx' Audio Effects, 'aumf' Music Effects, and 'aumu' Music Device Instruments) Synchronized automatically at macOS startup via the Audio Component registry across /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components, ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components, and registered macOS AUv3 application extensions. Indexed with canonical identifiers (au.<type>.<subtype>.<manufacturer>, such as au.aufx.dely.appl for AUDelay, or au.aumu.<subt>.<manu> for Audio Unit instruments) and virtual audiounit://<type>/<subtype>/<manufacturer> bundle paths.

Fast Startup Validation & Isolated Out-of-Process Audio Unit Hosting on macOS

  • Zero-Delay Startup Validation & Auto-Discovery: On application startup, Cave Recorder verifies the file modification timestamps of indexed .clap bundles on disk (in direct downloads) and automatically synchronizes all registered macOS Audio Unit ('aufx', 'aumf', and 'aumu') components via the system Audio Component registry without loading third-party dynamic libraries into memory. If a .clap bundle was moved or uninstalled while Cave Recorder was closed, its catalog entry is marked ! MISSING rather than deleted, preserving its metadata for non-destructive session recovery.
  • Isolated Out-of-Process Audio Unit Sandbox Protection (macOS & Mac App Store): On macOS, Cave Recorder instantiates both modern AUv3 extensions and AUv2 components ('aufx', 'aumf', and 'aumu') in isolated out-of-process system host processes by default so a faulty third-party plugin can never crash your active recording session (falling back cleanly to the generic parameter view if a custom graphical editor view cannot initialize). In the Mac App Store Edition, PLUGINS hosts macOS Audio Units exclusively and hides .clap filter pills and .clap disk import buttons to comply with macOS App Sandbox security rules. Direct downloads from caverec.app continue to host both .clap and Audio Unit plugins.

5.7.2 Indexing & Managing Plugins in the PLUGINS Workspace View (CMD/CTRL + 7)#

Pressing CMD + 7 on macOS (CTRL + 7 on Windows and Linux) or clicking PLUGINS in Row 2 of the Top Transport Deck opens the dedicated PLUGIN MANAGER & INDEXED CATALOG workspace view.

  1. Header Telemetry, KIND Filter (ALL | EFFECTS | INSTRUMENTS) & Guided Discovery Actions:
    • Live Status Telemetry Pill: Reports INDEXED: N | READY: N | MISSING: N | ERRORS: N | IN USE: N at the top of the panel (illuminated emerald when all indexed plugins are ready, or amber when any entry is missing or failed to probe).
    • 3-Way Kind Filter (KIND: ALL | EFFECTS | INSTRUMENTS): Isolates rack insert effects (EFFECTS), Pre-Tape Virtual Instruments (INSTRUMENTS, showing both CLAP instruments and macOS Audio Unit 'aumu' Music Devices), or the full catalog (ALL), alongside live counts (INSTRUMENTS: N | EFFECTS: N).
    • RESCAN DIRECTORIES (Non-Blocking Out-of-Process Scanning): Walks all standard OS .clap directories and configured custom search folders using an incremental modification-time check and probes newly added or updated .clap bundles and macOS 'aufx', 'aumf', and 'aumu' Audio Unit components asynchronously in an isolated background worker process. Faulty or incompatible third-party plugin bundles can never freeze the 60 Hz user interface or crash your active console session, and plugin reloads automatically guard against mid-operation session switches so stale results never overwrite a newly opened Session. Upon completion, an inline status banner summarizes SCAN COMPLETE: N DIR(S) WALKED | N BUNDLE(S) DISCOVERED (N PROBED, N CACHED) | N READY, N MISSING, N ERROR(S).
    • + ADD SEARCH FOLDER...: Opens a folder selection dialog (with an inline text-path fallback modal on headless systems) to register an additional .clap directory. Each custom folder appears in the search paths strip below the header as a recessed pill with an X button to remove the folder and prune its unreferenced entries.
    • + ADD .CLAP FILE...: Prompts you to select and probe an individual .clap bundle file asynchronously in the isolated background scanner without adding its entire parent directory.
  2. Searching, Filtering & Sorting the 8-Column Catalog Table:
    • Live Search (Search plugins...): Filters the catalog in real time across plugin name, vendor, reverse-URI or au. plugin ID, version, description, primary category (EQ, Compressor, Limiter, Gate / Expander, De-Esser, Transient, Reverb, Delay, Chorus, Flanger, Phaser, Saturation, Filter, Mastering, Analyzer, Restoration, Utility, Music Effect), feature tags, bundle path, status (ready, missing, error), and Audio Unit format tags (audio unit, audio-unit, auv2, auv3).
    • Quick-Filter Pills: Isolate ALL, AVAILABLE ([READY] plugins only), CLAP (.clap bundles only), AUDIO UNIT (macOS AUv2/AUv3 effects only), MISSING / NEEDS RESOLUTION (! MISSING and X ERROR rows), or IN USE IN SESSION (plugins currently assigned to one or more rack slots in the loaded session).
    • Sortable Columns & Hover Expansion: Click any of the seven sortable column headers (STATUS, NAME, VENDOR, CATEGORY, VERSION, PLUGIN ID, PATH) to sort ascending or descending. Dwelling the mouse pointer over any truncated cell or folder pill for 180 ms expands the full identifier, path, or error reason in place.
  3. Per-Row Status Badges & Recovery Actions (ACTIONS Column):
    • [READY] (Emerald): The .clap bundle or macOS Audio Unit is verified and ready to load into any rack slot. Plugins active in the current session display an emerald [IN USE xN] badge next to their name showing how many rack slots reference that plugin.
    • ! MISSING (Amber) & X ERROR (Crimson): Indicates a .clap bundle that was moved or renamed on disk (Missing on disk (click LOCATE)), a macOS Audio Unit that is not currently registered (Missing Audio Unit (click RESCAN)), or a bundle that failed factory validation (with the diagnostic reason shown beneath the plugin name).
    • LOCATE..., RESCAN & REMOVE: Click LOCATE... to point Cave Recorder to a moved .clap bundle on disk (verifying that the selected bundle exports the expected plugin_id and immediately relinking any Ghost Slots in the active session), click RESCAN to re-probe that specific plugin entry, or click REMOVE to delete the entry from clap_plugin_index.json.

5.7.3 Selecting, Loading & Opening Plugins in the 8-Slot Rack (SLOT N PROCESSOR & PLUGIN GUI)#

To load a built-in processor, third-party .clap plugin, or macOS Audio Unit effect into any channel or Subgroup Bus insert slot:

  1. Open the SLOT N PROCESSOR Selector Overlay: Select the target Input Track (CH01..CH18) or click SEL on the target Subgroup Bus (SUB 1..SUB 16), then click any slot pill (Slots 1..8) in Upper Well 1 (MIX CONSOLE, CMD/CTRL + 1) or in the left column of CHANNEL INSPECTOR (CMD/CTRL + 3).
  2. Choose Between Built-In Studio Processors or Plugin (External Plugin):
    • Clicking any of the built-in studio processor rows (12-Band Dynamic EQ, VCA Compressor, Tape Saturation, Vocal De-Esser, Context-Aware Gate, Signal Repair, Guitar/Bass Amp Rig, 2P/4P Ladder LPF, Vocal Rider, Transient Shaper, Micro-Pitch Doubler, Gain & Polarity Utility, Studio Modulation, or Aux Send Tap) assigns that zero-latency native module to the slot, while Empty Slot clears the slot (---).
    • Clicking Plugin (or clicking a 1:PLUGIN slot pill that already hosts an external plugin) expands the floating card to 348 px and reveals the INDEXED PLUGIN CATALOG subpanel at the bottom of the selector menu.
  3. Search & Assign from the Indexed Catalog Subpanel:
    • Type into the Search indexed plugins... filter box (or click CLR to clear) to narrow the list by plugin name, vendor, category, or format badge ([CLAP] / [AU]).
    • If you have not indexed your plugins yet, click MANAGE... beside the search box to jump directly to the PLUGINS workspace tab (CMD/CTRL + 7).
    • Click any [ ] [AU] Name (Vendor) [Category] or [ ] [CLAP] Name (Vendor) [Category] row in the scrollable list ([x] indicates the plugin currently loaded in that slot). Cave Recorder instantiates the .clap or macOS Audio Unit effect, negotiates stereo 32-bit floating-point audio buses at the active hardware sample rate, and swaps the processor into the rack slot without interrupting transport playback.
  4. Open & Close Floating Native Plugin Editor Windows (PLUGIN GUI):
    • Whenever a slot has an available .clap or Audio Unit plugin assigned, the header of the SLOT N PROCESSOR overlay displays a PLUGIN GUI toggle button (illuminated emerald when the editor window is open on screen).
    • Cross-Platform CLAP Floating Windows: For .clap plugins that implement the native plugin editor extension, clicking PLUGIN GUI opens a native floating desktop window on macOS, Windows, or Linux with live bidirectional parameter synchronization and plugin-initiated resize support.
    • Three-Tier Native Floating GUI Hosting on macOS (Audio Units): For hosted macOS Audio Units (AUv3 and AUv2), clicking PLUGIN GUI resolves the plugin's native editor view on the macOS main thread using a three-tier fallback chain and embeds it in a resizable native floating desktop window:
    • Tier 1 (Modern AUv3 Custom Editor View): Opens the modern AUv3 custom editor view, including sandboxed remote plugin views and bridged AUv2 view controllers.
    • Tier 2 (Legacy AUv2 Custom Editor View): Instantiates the custom AUv2 graphical editor view provided by legacy .component bundles.
    • Tier 3 (Generic Parameter Editor Fallback): If an Audio Unit does not provide a custom graphical view, Cave Recorder automatically constructs a macOS generic Audio Unit parameter editor so every Audio Unit parameter remains accessible.
  5. External Side-Chain Key Routing (SIDE-CHAIN KEY SOURCE): When a hosted plugin declares a secondary side-chain input port (or dynamics/side-chain feature tags), you can open the SIDE-CHAIN KEY SOURCE dropdown to route either INTERNAL (Self) or any Input Track, Subgroup Bus, or Aux Return strip into the plugin's key input with selectable PRE, POST-EQ, or POST-FDR tap point and -24.0 dB to +24.0 dB side-chain gain trim.

5.7.4 Preset State Persistence & Non-Destructive Ghost Slot Recovery (! MISSING)#

When you save a Session (*_session.json) or capture a Console Snapshot (SNAPS, CMD/CTRL + S), Cave Recorder serializes each populated plugin slot's complete state directly inside the session manifest:

  • The canonical plugin_id (org.vendor.plugin or au.aufx.subt.manu), display label, vendor, version, and last-known bundle path hint.
  • The slot's complete saved plugin preset state alongside the slot's parallel wet/dry mix ratio and bypass setting.

If you open a shared session on a second rehearsal or studio computer where a referenced .clap bundle or macOS Audio Unit is not yet installed (or was moved to a different disk folder), Cave Recorder never strips the plugin or discards its preset settings. Instead, it preserves the slot as a non-destructive Ghost Slot:

  1. Top-Level Missing Plugin Warning Banner: A high-contrast crimson-and-amber warning banner appears at the top of the workspace (! MISSING PLUGIN(S) | N PLUGIN(S) ACROSS M GHOST SLOT(S) BYPASSED (STATE PRESERVED)), identifying the first missing plugin, vendor, plugin_id, strip name, and slot number, paired with three action buttons:
    • LOCATE...: Opens a file picker to locate the missing .clap bundle on disk and immediately relinks and activates every Ghost Slot referencing that plugin_id.
    • OPEN PLUGINS: Switches directly to the PLUGINS workspace view (CMD/CTRL + 7) pre-filtered to MISSING / NEEDS RESOLUTION.
    • X (Dismiss): Hides the top warning banner for the remainder of the session while keeping the Ghost Slots safely bypassed in the rack.
  2. In-Slot Ghost Banner & Safe Audio Bypass: Opening SLOT N PROCESSOR on a Ghost Slot displays an amber diagnostic banner (! MISSING: <Name> (<Vendor>) and ID: <Plugin ID> | BYPASSED (STATE SAVED)) with a header LOCATE... button. Audio passes cleanly through the bypassed Ghost Slot during playback and recording, and the saved preset state is written back untouched whenever the session or a new Snapshot is saved.
  3. One-Click Live Restoration: The moment you relink the .clap bundle via LOCATE... or install the missing plugin and click RESCAN DIRECTORIES in the PLUGINS view, Cave Recorder instantiates the plugin, restores its saved preset state and original user bypass setting, and resumes live processing across all matching slots in the session.

5.7.5 Automatic Plugin Delay Compensation (PDC) & Transparency Breakdown#

All built-in Cave Recorder processors (TAPE, 12B EQ, VCA CMP, DE-ESS, GATE, REPAIR, RIDER, AUX 1 REVERB, AUX 2 TAPE DLY) operate with zero internal sample latency (0 smp / 0.00 ms). However, when you insert a third-party .clap plugin or macOS Audio Unit (AUv3 / AUv2) effect that uses internal lookahead buffering (such as linear-phase equalizers, spectral processors, or lookahead limiters), that plugin communicates its reported plugin latency in samples to Cave Recorder.

To prevent phase cancellation or timing drift between parallel tracks and subgroups, Cave Recorder performs Automatic Plugin Delay Compensation (PDC) across the entire mixing graph:

  • Row 2 of the Top Deck displays a live LATENCY 0.0 ms status pill at all times.
  • Clicking the LATENCY pill in the Top Deck opens the Latency & PDC Transparency Breakdown popover (shown in Figure 5.4 above), which reports every latency stage in your studio system in both Samples (smp) and Milliseconds (ms):
    • Audio I/O: Current hardware buffer size (256 frames @ 48000 Hz), input buffer latency (In: 64 smp / 1.33 ms), output buffer latency (Out: 64 smp / 1.33 ms), and calibrated hardware Roundtrip I/O (640 smp / 13.33 ms).
    • Total Graph PDC & Effective Playback PDC: Total delay compensation applied across parallel tracks and buses (Max Safe Ceiling: 96,000 smp / 2000.00 ms).
    • Playhead Lag & Overdub Record-Offset: Exact negative sample offset (-640 smp / 13.33 ms) applied automatically when writing new Overdub Passes (Rec002-OD) to disk so that everything a musician plays against playback lands sample-accurately on the timeline.
    • Filterable Per-Channel Table (ALL, ARMED, COMPENSATED, BYPASSED): Lists every Input Track (Track 1 [ARMED]..Track 18), Subgroup 1..2, Aux 1 (Reverb), Aux 2 (Delay), and Master Bus with its individual sample and millisecond compensation state.

5.7.6 LOW-LATENCY Monitoring & Live Monitoring Latency Warning Persistence#

When you are late in a mix and have inserted a high-latency lookahead mastering plugin or linear-phase EQ (.clap or macOS Audio Unit) on a track or Subgroup Bus, recording a last-minute vocal or guitar overdub through that high-latency plugin would introduce a distracting echo in the musician's headphones.

Clicking LOW-LATENCY in Row 2 of the Top Deck solves this immediately:

  • Cave Recorder temporarily bypasses high-latency CLAP and Audio Unit effect plugins only on record-armed (R) live monitoring paths and their downstream buses, dropping the musician's headphone monitoring latency back down to pure zero-latency built-in console processing (0 smp graph PDC). If an armed Pre-Tape Virtual Instrument itself reports high internal lookahead latency (> 256 samples at 48.0 kHz), LOW-LATENCY keeps the sound-generating instrument active while bypassing downstream high-latency rack effects and surfaces a high-latency instrument advisory.
  • All unarmed playback tracks continue playing with full Plugin Delay Compensation.
  • As soon as you finish recording the Overdub Pass and disarm the track (or toggle LOW-LATENCY off in the Top Deck), the high-latency plugins re-engage automatically without losing a single plugin parameter setting.

Whenever one or more record-armed tracks exceed the 10.0 ms live software monitoring threshold, Cave Recorder displays the Live Monitoring Latency Warning banner (Live Monitoring Latency Warning (<N> record-armed track(s)) | <total> ms total (<pdc> ms PDC + <io> ms I/O)) with three persistent choices:

  1. Enable Low-Latency Monitoring: Activates LOW-LATENCY immediately and bypasses high-latency plugins on armed monitoring paths, suppressing the banner once effective latency falls within threshold (or recording a high-water mark for residual unbypassable latency).
  2. Dismiss: Silences the warning banner for the remainder of the current Session unless effective live-monitoring latency strictly increases above the dismissed high-water mark (for example, if you later insert an even heavier lookahead plugin). Switching sessions or disabling LOW-LATENCY or HW DIRECT MON resets the dismissal watermark.
  3. Enable Hardware Direct Monitoring: For studios where musicians monitor live inputs through an audio interface or stagebox's zero-latency hardware mixer rather than software foldback, clicking Enable Hardware Direct Monitoring saves hardware_direct_monitoring globally inside device_settings.json so the preference persists automatically across session switches and application restarts. To toggle or reset Hardware Direct Monitoring later, open the Top Deck LATENCY popover and click HW DIRECT MON (displaying Monitoring: Hardware Direct (interface zero-latency mix) when active, or Monitoring: Software DAW (live inputs monitored through mixer) when off).

5.8 Built-In Non-Destructive Audio Restoration (ADC De-Clipper & 12-Harmonic Hum Canceller)#

In a high-energy rehearsal or live tracking session, a drummer will occasionally hit a rimshot 6 dB harder than during soundcheck and flat-top the hardware preamp's analog-to-digital converter (0.0 dBFS), or a vintage tube combo amp will pick up 50 Hz or 60 Hz power-line buzz in an older basement venue.

Instead of forcing you to export stems to an external audio restoration editor, Cave Recorder includes two non-destructive studio restoration tools built directly into the console and timeline:

  1. [REPAIR CLIPPING] (Two-Tier Smooth Spline & Spectral Waveform De-Clipper):
    • Automatically detects contiguous flat-topped digital saturation bursts where the waveform hits the converter ceiling (default -0.1 dBFS threshold, user-adjustable from -12.0 dBFS to 0.0 dBFS for hard-clipped external preamps).
    • Short Clips (1 to 8 samples): Reconstructs the missing transient peak using smooth spline interpolation anchored to the unclipped amplitude, velocity, and curvature immediately preceding and following the clip burst.
    • Medium & Long Clips (9 to 256 samples): Fits a forward/backward harmonic waveform prediction model to the 512 clean context samples surrounding the clipped plateau, predicts the natural harmonic waveform trajectory forward and backward across the gap with raised-cosine crossfade blending, and restores the lost 3 dB to 6 dB transient dome cleanly.
  2. 50 Hz / 60 Hz 12-Harmonic Comb Hum Canceller (Hum Canceller):
    • Power-line ground loops and neon/dimmer transformer buzz never sit solely at 50 Hz or 60 Hz. They generate a sharp comb of odd and even harmonics (60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360, 420, 480, 540, 600, 660, 720 Hz) that sounds like an angry hornet nest inside guitar and bass tracks. Trying to cut all 12 harmonics with regular EQ bands wastes your entire parametric equalizer and hollows out the low-mid tone of the instrument.
    • The dedicated Hum Canceller cascades 12 ultra-narrow constant-Q biquad notch filters (Q = 20.0 to 100.0, default Q = 60.0, bandwidth < 1.0 Hz at the fundamental) locked to f_0, 2f_0, ..., 12f_0 (50.0 Hz European or 60.0 Hz North American mains, with fundamental fine-tuning from 45.0 Hz to 65.0 Hz and selectable Odd Harmonics Only vs. Odd + Even Harmonics). Because each notch is less than a couple of Hertz wide, 50/60 Hz buzz vanishes completely while 99% of the surrounding bass and guitar note warmth passes through untouched.

For step-by-step instructions on applying [REPAIR CLIPPING], range-bounded Pass comping, [PATCH FROM SOURCE...], and [SMOOTH OVER ARTIFACT] spectral spot-healing directly on the Waveform Timeline, see Section 6.5 in Chapter 6.

5.9 Native Virtual Analog Groovebox, Melodic Sequencer & Studio Sampler (GROOVEBOX)#

Pressing CMD + 6 on macOS (CTRL + 6 on Windows and Linux), clicking GROOVEBOX in Row 2 of the Top Transport Deck, or clicking [GUI] on any channel strip hosting [NATIVE] CAVE DRUM MACHINE opens Cave Recorder's built-in Virtual Analog Groovebox, Melodic Sequencer & Studio Sampler across four sub-views: SEQUENCER, SYNTH & SCOPE, SAMPLER, and ARRANGER.

Built directly into the Pre-Tape Track Input Stage, the Groovebox gives rehearsal bands, electronic/krautrock trios, and live jammers a tactile 16-voice drum, bass, and sampling groovebox (combining four coupled percussion voice archetypes, the monophonic ANALOG BASS synthesizer, and the STUDIO SAMPLER voice) that locks cleanly to ● MIDI, feeds the 30-minute stereo ● RETRO memory, prints directly into standard 32-bit float audio Pass stems (rec/*.wav), breaks individual drum, bass, or sampled voices out to separate console channels, and pairs wirelessly with the Cave Companion tablet and phone GROOVEBOX (WAVE / SLICES / MANGLE) remotes.

5.9.1 Pre-Tape Stem Breakouts, Bidirectional Tempo & Non-Destructive Factory Kits#

  1. 16-Voice Kit Pool & Individual Voice Console Stem Breakouts (OUT: BUS vs. STEM):
    • Each Drum Machine instance provides a 16-voice kit pool (12 voices active by default, expandable up to 16 via + INSERT VOICE / + VOICE), letting you place one or more monophonic ANALOG BASS lanes right alongside percussion voices in any kit.
    • By default, all voices sum into the Drum Machine's internal stereo Glue Bus (OUT: BUS) and record through the hosting channel strip.
    • Assigning any voice's OUT control to a STEM breakout removes that voice from the internal Drum Master Bus by default (preventing comb filtering, with an explicit parallel option if desired) and routes its stereo output directly into a dedicated Mix Console channel strip at zero added latency. That broken-out drum or bass voice then gets its own 8-slot console rack, Aux 1..8 Reverb/Delay sends, fader, raw .wav Pass stem, and 30-minute RETRO capture.
  2. Bidirectional Studio Tempo (STUDIO CLK) & 4-Mode Master Transport Coupling (FOLLOW TRN):
    • Tempo Follower & Master (STUDIO CLK): When MIDI SYNC is locked (SYNC: LOCK) from a floor looper or 4-tap count-in, the Drum Machine locks automatically as a sample-accurate follower. When MIDI SYNC is free (SYNC: FREE) and STUDIO CLK is lit (default), adjusting BPM (30.0 to 300.0 BPM) inside the Drum Machine drives the entire studio clock, automatically locking outbound 24 PPQN MIDI Clock, AUX 2 Stereo Delay, 4-Mode Modulation, and sibling virtual instruments to the Drum Machine's tempo and downbeat.
    • 4-Mode Master Transport Coupling (FOLLOW TRN) & Immediate Coupled STOP / |< Response:
    • Rehearsal Jam Mode (Master Transport Stopped): Clicking SEQ PLAY rolls the sequencer live (continuously feeding stereo 30-minute RETRO memory) without advancing a Take timeline.
    • Standstill Master Play / Record: Pressing Master Play or Record while idle starts the active Scene at Bar 1 / Step 01 locked cleanly to 00:00:00.000 (holding cleanly through any <= 25 ms external MIDI pre-roll so Beat 1's kick transient is never truncated).
    • Mid-Jam Record Punch & Coupled Stop/RTZ: Punching Master Record while SEQ PLAY is rolling preserves unbroken live groove phase in the room (or waits for the next Beat 1 when AUTO-REC ON BEAT 1 is latched in MIDI SYNC). Pressing Master Stop halts step triggering while allowing cymbal, membrane, and bass tails to decay naturally. During coupled Master DAW Playback (when not recording a Take), clicking SEQ PLAY (Stop) or |< (Return-to-Zero) on Desktop or Cave Companion responds immediately and stays synchronized with the Master Transport without interrupting active Take recordings.
    • Recorded Take Pass Isolation: On a disarmed, unmonitored Drum Track (R off, I off) with a recorded audio Pass (Rec001.wav), pressing Master Play streams the recorded .wav stem (preserving every live CTRL ALL, Scene jump, melodic bass performance, and Slip Beat-Repeat move) and silences the live sequencer so drums and bass never double-play.
  3. Pinned Woody Studio METRONOME Kit & Symmetric 13-Kit [POCKET | CLUB] Factory Suite (21 Grooves, Non-Destructive +GROOVE Opt-In):
    • The FACTORY KITS: bar across Desktop and Cave Companion (DRUMS) pins METRONOME permanently on the far left followed by a symmetric, zero-scroll two-bank [POCKET | CLUB] selector covering 13 built-in kits and 21 starter grooves:
    • Pinned Leftmost METRONOME Kit (4-Track Woody Studio Click & 7 Meter Grooves): Collapses the matrix cleanly to four phase-reset modal wood-block voices (01 BAR ACCENT, 02 GROUP BEAT, 03 BEAT CLICK, 04 SUBDIV TICK) with the Glue Bus bypassed so clicks stay crisp and uncolored. Selecting METRONOME automatically seeds its default FREE (unaccented 4/4 live pulse) groove whenever the active pattern is completely empty (while preserving any non-empty pattern when +GROOVE is OFF), and contextually displays seven meter buttons in GROOVES:: FREE, 4/4, 3/4, 5/4, 6/4, 7/4, and Jazz 2 & 4.
    • POCKET Bank (6 Kits / 8 Grooves): STUDIO ANALOG (SHUFFLE BRK, featuring pre-voiced slot 12 ANALOG BASS), DESERT ROCK (DESERT SLOUCH and TRIBAL TOMS heavy open-drum stoner rock grooves with parallel room-crush bus), SOUL POCKET (DRUNK POCKET unquantized micro-nudged groove, also featuring slot 12 ANALOG BASS), BOOM BAP (EAST COAST 90 swung-pickup punch groove), MOTORIK DRY (MOTORIK 4/4), MODAL METAL (POLY MODAL), plus the syncopated ladder-bass showcase groove FUNK POCKET (octave bassline slides and tied holds on slot 12 ANALOG BASS).
    • CLUB Bank (6 Kits / 6 Grooves): TECHNO PUNCH (MINIMAL TECH), DEEP SUB ELECTRO (ELECTRO SUB), BREAKS 174 (DNB 2-STEP), HALFTIME SUB (HALFTIME 140), PSY MATRIX (PSY ROLLER phase-locked kick/bass on Choke Group 3), and ACID & FUNK (122.0 BPM, pairing punchy electro-funk drums with dual pre-voiced ANALOG BASS slots 11 LADDER FUNK and 12 ACID SQUELCH, plus the 16th-note resonant ACID SQUELCH starter groove showcasing melodic notes, ties, pitch slides, and accents).
    • Strictly Non-Destructive Kit Switching: Clicking any Factory Kit swaps only the synthesized drum and bass voices, Glue Bus, and Morph presets (preserving your console STEM breakouts, all 64 Patterns, all 16 Scenes, and your active Scene). Enable +GROOVE (default OFF) if you also want kit selection to load a starter groove into the single currently selected active pattern (fully undoable via CMD/CTRL + Z, leaving all other 63 patterns untouched), or click any contextual groove button in GROOVES: or CLEAR PAT.

5.9.2 The Six Voice Archetypes (4 Drum Voices + ANALOG BASS + STUDIO SAMPLER), Storage-CRT Scope & Glue Bus (SYNTH & SCOPE)#

Every voice slot in the 16-voice kit pool can be switched between six voice archetypes (four coupled virtual analog percussion voices, the monophonic ANALOG BASS synthesizer, and the STUDIO SAMPLER voice), each exposing a standardized 2 x 4 (8-macro) rotary bay that maps 1:1 across the desktop faceplate, the Studio Pad Surface, and the Cave Companion tablet and phone touch encoders. Analog oscillator phases, filter integrators, and envelope capacitors retain natural analog charge memory across rapid hits and notes, while STUDIO SAMPLER applies an automatic 2.0 ms click-free de-click tail on retriggers and slice jumps:

Whenever a STUDIO SAMPLER voice is focused in SYNTH & SCOPE, a contextual STUDIO SAMPLER: banner offers a 1-click OPEN IN SAMPLER jump. Chopped rehearsal breakbeats, resampled guitar/horn stabs, pitched vocal textures, micro-grain drones, and chromatic melodic one-shots.
  • Contextual Bass Voice Setup Strip (ANALOG BASS Voices Only): Whenever the selected voice is set to ANALOG BASS (Analog Violet badge BAS in the Voice Rail, BASS keycap in CIRCUIT ARCHETYPE:), a compact setup strip appears directly below the voice header in both the SEQUENCER Quick Synth bay and the SYNTH & SCOPE view (omitted on percussion voices so drum layouts never shift):
    • ROOT (C1..C4, default C2): Sets the voice's fallback root pitch for unpitched steps and [AUDITION] clicks (double-click or OPT/ALT + Click resets to C2). Clicking [AUDITION] on an ANALOG BASS voice plays a punchy 220 ms note at ROOT.
    • FINE (-100..+100 ct, default 0 ct): Bipolar micro-tuning offset in cents to match slightly sharp or flat live studio instruments.
    • GLIDE (0..500 ms, default 35 ms) & G-MODE (G: SLIDE / G: ALWAYS): Controls 1V/oct log-Hz exponential portamento speed. In G: SLIDE (default), pitch glides occur on sequencer steps with SLIDE enabled and during overlapping live legato MIDI notes. In G: ALWAYS, every pitch change glides smoothly at the configured GLIDE time.
    • ENV (ENV: RETRG / ENV: LEGTO / ENV: GATE): Selects between three analog envelope behaviors: ENV: RETRG (default, re-excites filter and amp capacitors on every non-tied note while holding uninterrupted across tied steps), ENV: LEGTO (suppresses envelope retriggering on any overlapping live MIDI phrase, tie, or full-step gate overlap), and ENV: GATE (organ/pedal sustain holding the VCA at a steady plateau across the entire note gate while the filter decays toward a warm sustain floor).
    • MIDI (MIDI: CHRM / MIDI: PAD): When MIDI: CHRM is active (automatically enabled when creating or switching to an ANALOG BASS voice), inbound external MIDI keyboard notes (0..127) route exclusively into the focused ANALOG BASS voice through an 8-note monophonic last-note-priority key stack (supporting held-gate sustain, overlapping legato glides, and clean previous-note return on key release) while suppressing drum-pad note triggers so playing C2, D2, or F#2 basslines never fires Kick, Snare, or Hi-Hat. Toggle to MIDI: PAD whenever you want the bass slot to trigger as a single-note drum pad alongside the rest of the kit.
  • Triggered Log-Time Storage-CRT Oscilloscope (0..500 ms) & 2D XY Reticles: Captures each hit or bass note on a logarithmically warped time axis (0..500 ms) with 3-hit phosphor persistence trails and archetype-specific overlays (pitch sweep curve, clap discharge bursts, 6-oscillator alloy spectrum bars, dual modal formants, or resonant ladder/OTA bass harmonic contour). Drag the two interactive reticle nodes (P1 and P2) directly over the waveform to sculpt paired macros in 2D (hold SHIFT for fine gear, OPT/ALT + Click to reset). On ANALOG BASS voices, P1 maps to CUTOFF × RESONANCE and P2 maps to ENV MOD × DRIVE.
  • Asymmetric SWING-VCA CURVE Visualizer: Displays the voice's equal-loudness asymmetric transistor VCA transfer curve in real time as you adjust drive and bias.
  • Shared Drum Master GLUE BUS: Sums all BUS voices through a parallel VCA Glue Compressor (THRESH, SC HPF 20..150 Hz, ATTACK 0.1..30 ms, AUTO/REL 50..400 ms, RATIO 2:1 | 4:1 | SLAM, MAKEUP, MIX 0..100% blended pre-clipper for zero phase cancellation, and a top-down amber GR meter) feeding a 4x Oversampled Asymmetric Soft Clipper (DRIVE 0..+12 dB, CEIL -6.0..0.0 dBFS).

5.9.3 Polymetric & Melodic Step Sequencer ([2D | NOTE | VEL]), Parameter Locks & Live Performance Deck (SEQUENCER)#

  1. 64 Patterns (A01..D16), Per-Voice Polymeter & Pattern Swing:
    • Each Pattern spans 1 to 64 steps across four page selectors (1-16, 17-32, 33-48, 49-64) with selectable base step division (DIV: 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/16T, 1/32), COPY / PASTE, and one-click EUCLID Euclidean rhythm generation.
    • Pattern SWING (50.0% to 75.0% in 0.1% increments): Paired with a selectable swing division (SWG: 1/8 default, 1/16, 1/4, or 1/32) delaying off-beat sub-pulses smoothly.
    • Per-Voice Polymeter (LEN 1..64), Polyrhythm (CLK) & Dynamic Choke Groups (CHK C1..C4): Give any drum or bass voice an independent step length (LEN) and clock ratio (CLK: x1, 1/2, 1/4, 3/2, 4/3, 5/4, 2/1) with zero cumulative drift. Voices sharing a choke group (C1..C4, such as Closed and Open Hi-Hat, or Kick choking Bass for tight club ducking) damp each other smoothly over 3..12 ms with zero clicks.
  2. Always-Visible Thin-Line Playhead & Return-to-Zero ([|<]):
    • One continuous 1.5 px fractional-phase vertical playhead hairline glides smoothly from the step ruler across active voice rows (luminous phosphor green while rolling, calm slate/cyan when parked). Polymetric rows whose wrapped position differs from row 1 draw a subtle row-local hairline.
    • Click |< (or double-stop) to return the playhead to Step 01, or click anywhere along the step ruler while stopped to park and scrub the playhead.
  3. Contextual Step Inspector, Non-Destructive Selection & Parameter Locks (P-LOCK):
    • On percussion rows, click any empty step cell to activate HIT and drag vertically in one motion to set velocity. Clicking an active step with < 4 px movement toggles it off while preserving stored notes, parameter locks, and articulations for quick re-enable.
    • Non-Destructive Step Selection: To inspect or edit an active step without turning it off, enable SELECT mode, arm P-LOCK mode (which automatically switches clicks to select-only), or use OPT/ALT + Click, CMD + Click, or Middle-Click anywhere on the matrix. Use SHIFT + Click to toggle ACC (Accent) and Right-Click to toggle LOCK (Triggerless Parameter Lock ◇).
    • Per-Step Articulations: Shape VEL (1..127), GATE (5..1600%, where 100% is a natural one-shot on percussion voices and a crisp 55% analog sequencer gate duty on ANALOG BASS voices, reaching full-step overlap at 182%), NUDGE (-50..+49% micro-timing), SINGLE / FLAM (4..30 ms) / RETRIG (2..8 sub-hits with crescendo/decrescendo slope), SLIDE (smoothly slews P-locked macros on percussion voices, and executes a slurred 1V/oct log-Hz pitch slide with continuous gate bridge into the next active note on ANALOG BASS voices), and step COND (Always, probability %, cycle k:n 1:2..8:8, FILL, or !FILL).
    • Parameter Locks (P-LOCK): Hold any step cell (>= 180 ms with < 4 px travel) and turn any of the 8 voice macros (or arm P-LOCK and select steps) to record per-step parameter overrides. Click CLR LOCKS to clear locks on the selected step, or ? STEP GLYPHS for an inline legend of step symbols.
  4. Melodic ANALOG BASS Step Rows, Tie Bridges & [2D | NOTE | VEL] Step-Drag Modes:
    • High-Contrast Note Labels & Violet Tie Bridge Bars: Active steps on ANALOG BASS rows display their centered chromatic 12-TET note name (C2, Eb2, F#1, etc.) and a left-edge octave-register pip alongside velocity shading, amber Accent bars, cyan / slide glyphs, and P-lock diamonds. Whenever an active step has TIE enabled (or SLIDE into the following active step), an Analog Violet Tie Bridge Bar connects across the cell or beat-group gap, and the scheduler holds the gate across exact swung and micro-nudged beat positions so the envelopes stay uninterrupted without false retriggers.
    • Contextual Bass Step Inspector (TIE, NOTE & [2D | NOTE | VEL]): Selecting an ANALOG BASS voice expands the Step Inspector with TIE (toggles continuous legato bridging into the next step), NOTE (C0..C8 vertical drag slider with Double-Click / OPT/ALT + Click reset to ROOT, plus Right-Click keyboard entry accepting both note names such as Eb2 or F#1 and MIDI note numbers such as 36), and the three-way [2D | NOTE | VEL] step-drag mode selector:
    • 2D (Default, Axis-Locked Pitch + Tie Chains): After crossing the 4 px deadzone, dragging vertically locks to chromatic pitch (8 px per semitone, with a short preview audition when transport is stopped, and holding SHIFT mid-drag steps in whole octaves ±12 st for fast funk leaps). Dragging horizontally paints a sustained Tie chain rightward across steps (retracting cleanly if you drag back left). Hold OPT/ALT or CMD and drag vertically on an active step to sculpt velocity without leaving 2D mode.
    • NOTE (Pure Vertical Pitch): Uses the same vertical chromatic pitch drag (SHIFT = octave steps, OPT/ALT or CMD = velocity) with horizontal Tie-chain painting locked off so rapid diagonal sweeps never add unintended ties.
    • VEL (Pure Vertical Velocity): Matches percussion rows (Click + Vertical Drag edits velocity 1..127, SHIFT for fine gear) for fast ghost-note bass dynamics, while OPT/ALT or CMD + vertical drag edits chromatic note pitch.
  5. Live Performance Deck (STASH KIT, CTRL ALL, MORPH, Humanizer & SLIP BEAT-REPEAT):
    • STASH KIT / UNDO ST / RELOAD (Q:INST | Q:BAR): Bookmarks your active Kit, Pattern, and Morph state into RAM. Overwriting a dirty stash (STASH KIT*) requires a 400 ms press-and-hold (or SHIFT + Click) with 1-deep UNDO ST protection. RELOAD snaps the kit back instantly (Q:INST) or on the next bar downbeat (Q:BAR) with smooth 5 ms macro slewing.
    • CTRL ALL: Momentary while held (double-click to latch), fanning relative macro knob moves across all unmuted voices simultaneously.
    • MORPH Crossfader (M1..M4 + CAP): Interpolates stored per-voice macro scenes (A <-> B) smoothly across the kit.
    • Seeded Humanizer (HUM T 0.0..15.0 ms, HUM V 0..25%): Adds organic micro-timing and velocity variation while keeping Beat 1 downbeats tightly anchored.
    • Momentary HOLD FILL & Phase-Locked SLIP BEAT-REPEAT: Hold HOLD FILL to trigger FILL conditional steps, or hold any SLIP BEAT-REPEAT division (1/4, 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/32, 1/64) to retrigger the real analog drum and bass voices rhythmically while true song phase keeps advancing underneath ("Slip Mode"), landing cleanly back on the beat when released (automatically clamping repeated ANALOG BASS gates so rapid 1/32 and 1/64 bass rolls articulate crisply instead of fusing into a static drone). REV GRAIN reverses the most recent transient slice and TAPE STOP decelerates the drum bus smoothly over 450 ms.

5.9.4 16-Scene Pattern-Chain Arranger (ARRANGER)#

Switch to ARRANGER to chain Patterns (A01..D16) into up to 16 playable Scenes (S01..S16):

  • Scene Chain Blocks (+ ADD BLOCK, 1x.., DEL, RESET CHAIN): Stack up to 32 ordered blocks per Scene, assigning any Pattern slot from the 64-Slot Pattern Bank (A01..D16), setting per-block bar repeats (1x, 2x, ...), and toggling Per-Block Voice Mute Overrides to build automated intros, drops, and drum breakdowns without duplicating patterns.
  • Phase-Locked Scene Jumping (JUMP: DIRECT | NEXT BEAT | NEXT BAR): In DIRECT mode (default), jumping between Scenes mid-bar preserves exact running beat phase so the groove never restarts from zero or drops a downbeat. Switch to NEXT BEAT or NEXT BAR to queue Scene transitions to the next musical boundary.

5.9.5 Studio Sampler Workspace (SAMPLER): SuperFlux Slicing, Live Resampling, Creative Shaping & SAMPLE HISTORY#

Switch to SAMPLER inside GROOVEBOX (CMD/CTRL + 6), click OPEN IN SAMPLER from SYNTH & SCOPE, or click -> SAMPLER on any selected Range in TIMELINE to open the dedicated Studio Sampler workstation. The Studio Sampler lets bands capture spontaneous live rehearsal grooves, guitar chords, or full console submixes directly into playable pads without cluttering song Take timelines.

The desktop SAMPLER view is organized into four fixed-height zones with zero layout jitter:

  1. Top Source, Asset & SAMPLE HISTORY Bar (IMPORT RANGE, RESAMPLE, LOAD WAV, Sample History (N)…):
    • Step through Groovebox voices (< V01..V16 >) and session sample assets (< Smp001 <label> v01 >), zoom the sample viewport (Z-, Z+, 1:1, or scroll wheel around the cursor), or bring audio into the focused slot via three sources:
    • IMPORT RANGE (DRY PASS | POST-FX): Imports the active Timeline Range (K..L or R001..R016) directly into <SessionFolder>/samples/. DRY PASS extracts the selected track's active Pass Lane in under 20 ms (honoring overdub record offsets and range comp crossfades), while POST-FX runs an offline faster-than-real-time bounce of the selected Track (1..32), Subgroup (1..16), Aux Return (1..8), or Master Bus with pre-roll warmup.
    • RESAMPLE: Jumps straight to live direct-from-mixer recording in the RECORD deck below.
    • LOAD WAV: Imports any external .wav file from disk asynchronously off the 60 Hz interface thread, replicating it into <SessionFolder>/samples/ (with Broadcast Wave provenance metadata) so the session folder remains completely self-contained for archiving or Google Drive sync. Sample bank loading enforces active session-switch safety guards and retires replaced sample voice memory off the real-time audio path so live Groovebox playback stays glitch-free.
    • Versioned SAMPLE HISTORY Drawer & Alert Banner (Sample History (N)…): Every destructive bounce creates a new v<VV+1> file in <SessionFolder>/samples/ and archives v<VV> into <SessionFolder>/samples/_history/ so UNDO (CMD/CTRL + Z) and REDO restore prior versions and pre-bounce macro settings losslessly. Prior generations are never silently auto-deleted. Click Sample History (N)… (or use the fixed-height alert strip that appears automatically whenever archived history reaches 10 files or 256 MB) to access Keep Latest 3 (keeps the latest 3 prior versions per active sample and purges older generations), Empty Trash… (purges all archived sample files), and HIDE.
  2. Center Waveform & 180 px Split Zero-Crossing Zoom Lens:
    • Displays the sample waveform with live playhead hairline, Start/End markers, S01..S64 slice flags, and the live transient novelty/threshold trace when SLICE is in TRANSIENT mode. Drag markers horizontally (hold SHIFT for 0.20x fine precision), click to audition slices, or click directly on the waveform in LIVE PAD mode to drop zero-crossed slice markers.
    • The right-hand 180 px Split Zero-Crossing Zoom Lens magnifies ±96 sample frames around the active Start/End boundary or focused slice (S01..S64) so you can verify exact zero-crossings visually before committing a crop or loop.
  3. 4-Mode Sampler Deck (RECORD | EDIT & COMMIT | SLICE | ZONE & LFO):
    • RECORD (Direct-to-Sampler Live Resampling, Zero Take Clutter): Select SRC: (TRACK TRK 01..32, SUBGROUP SUB 01..16, AUX BUS AUX 01..08, MASTER MST PRE unaffected by Control Room DIM/MONO, or ADC IN IN 01-02..17-18), TAP: (PRE-FX, POST-FX default pre-fader so fader rides do not disturb sample gain, or POST-FDR), and TRIG::
    • THRESHOLD (-60.0 to 0.0 dB, default -36.0 dB): Maintains a continuous 10 ms pre-roll capture so the moment input crosses threshold, recording captures 10 ms prior to the transient with zero clipped attacks.
    • BAR SYNC (1B, 2B, 4B, 8B, 16B, default 4B): Arms for the next downbeat of the Studio Tempo clock and captures an exact bar-quantized loop automatically.
    • MANUAL: Captures immediately from ARM / REC until STOP (up to a 5:00 safety ceiling) with zero extra Take entries in the Session Reel.
    • EDIT & COMMIT (Offline Processing with Reversible Versioned Undo):
    • CROP (FADE IN 0..2000 ms, FADE OUT 0..2000 ms, DC OFF DC-offset removal, ZC SNAP zero-crossing snap), NORM (PEAK -12.0 to -0.1 dB, default -0.3 dB), REVERSE (reversing audio and rebasing slice markers cleanly), and COMMIT FX BOUNCE (renders active Pitch, Filter / Comb, Reso / Fdbk, Grit / Crush, and envelope shaping into v<VV+1> and resets the live macros back to neutral unity in a single undoable step).
    • BPM FIT (1B, 2B, 4B, 8B, TGT BPM 30.0..300.0, PITCH -24.0..+24.0 st, TRANSIENTS, COMMIT STRETCH): Fits a live band snippet (SRC <est> BPM auto-estimated from bar count) to your target Sequencer BPM (0.50x..2.00x) and/or pitch shift independently using a transient-preserving hybrid stretcher that splices ~12 ms attack windows cleanly while phase-locking harmonic sustain.
    • SLICE (Noise-Robust Transient Auto-Slicer, Grid & Live Pad Chop):
    • TRANSIENT: Tuned specifically for unisolated rehearsal rooms, bleeding drum mics, and humming guitar amps. Uses adaptive spectral whitening and moving-median noise floor tracking with live SENSITIVITY (0..100%, default 50%) and MIN SLICE (30..500 ms, default 80 ms) plus onset-foot backtracking and zero-crossing snap (1..64 slices).
    • GRID: Divides the sample into 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, or 64 equal slices.
    • LIVE PAD: Tap unlit pads (or click SLICE HERE / DEL SLICE) while auditioning to drop manual zero-crossed chops on the fly.
    • Dual Apply Targets (Single Undoable Action): Choose CHOKE (OFF, G1..G4), AD-HOC (replaces kit slots 0..K with sliced STUDIO SAMPLER voices) vs. FILL EMPTY (fills only inactive slots), and opt-in +SEQUENCE (default OFF unless the active pattern is empty, laying down micro-nudged linear slice steps in the active pattern only without touching the other 63 patterns). Click APPLY TO KIT to spread up to 16 slices across pads, or APPLY TO TRACK to bind all 1..64 slices to the focused slot in SLICE-LOCK mode (with 1-click LINEAR LOCKS and RANDOM LOCKS pattern P-lock generators).
    • ZONE & LFO (Playback Machines, Bipolar DJ / Comb Filter & Assignable LFO):
    • PLAY: ONE-SHOT (default, obeying percussion gate choke < 100%), GATE HOLD (sustains while held, releasing via Decay / Rel), LOOP FWD (equal-power loop crossfade XFADE 0..50 ms, shrinking Length down to 0.5% turns any transient into a pitched micro-grain oscillator), PING-PONG (alternating forward/reverse loop with turnaround crossfade), and SLICE-LOCK (Start / Slice selects S01..S64 per step).
    • FLT: DJ FILTER (0..48% 2-pole LP, 48..52% flat bypass, 52..100% 2-pole HP) or COMB RES (tuned feedback delay resonator 30 Hz..4,000 Hz with bipolar negative hollow-pipe to positive metallic-string feedback on Reso / Fdbk). Toggle REV for slot-level reverse (overridable per step via step reverse lock), CHRM for chromatic MIDI keyboard playback (ROOT C0..C8 default C4, FINE -50..+50 ct), and configure the per-voice LFO (SINE, TRI, EXP, SAW, S&H, SYNC 4 BAR..1/64 or FREE 0.05..30.0 Hz, RETRIG phase reset, TGT: OFF, PIT, STR, LEN, FLT, RES, GRT, PAN, and bipolar DEPTH -100..+100%).
  4. Bottom 2 x 4 Rotary Macro Deck & 4 x 4 Audition / Chop Pad Bank:
    • All 8 standardized macros (Pitch, Start / Slice, Length, Attack, Decay / Rel, Filter / Tune, Reso / Fdbk, Grit / Crush, where Grit / Crush sweeps warm analog preamp drive across 0..45% and progressive 16 -> 5-bit / sample-rate crush across 45..100%) support CTRL ALL, M1..M4 MORPH, P-locks, Double-Click / OPT/ALT + Click reset, and right-click numeric entry, alongside AUDITION and the bottom-up 4 x 4 SLICE / AUDITION PADS (LIVE CHOP PADS in LIVE PAD mode) banked across A, B, C, D (S01..S64).

5.10 Controlling Built-In Processors, Hosted Plugins & the Drum Machine from a Studio Pad Surface#

Your Dual-Screen Pad Controller gives direct tactile control over both the focused channel strip's processing chain (in [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE]) and all 16 Drum Machine / ANALOG BASS voices (in [DRUM STUDIO]).

5.10.1 Strip PROCESSORs & Hosted PLUGIN [CLAP] / PLUGIN [AU] (PLUG-IN View)#

In [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE], press PLUG-IN to open STRIP PROCESSORS & PLUGINS for the currently inspected Input Track, Subgroup Bus, Aux Return, or Master Bus. Soft keys F1..F8 (or Page < / >) select across the strip's built-in Processors and third-party Plugins (strictly labeled PROCESSOR for built-in studio DSP and PLUGIN [CLAP] or PLUGIN [AU] for external hosted plugins):

  1. 12-Band Dynamic EQ (PROCESSOR):
    • Left Screen plots the live analytical EQ magnitude curve across 20 Hz..20 kHz with highlighted active band marker (E1..E4 dock below Left Screen, E5..E8 dock below Right Screen). Page 1 maps Freq Hz, Gain dB, Q, Filter Shape, Dyn Range, Dyn Thresh, Enable, and Dyn Enable across E1..E8 (press F6: DYN ENV for Page 2 dynamic envelope controls). Soft keys F1..F4 select the 4 bands in the active bank and F5 cycles band banks (1..4, 5..8, 9..12).
  2. VCA / FET / Opto Compressor & Noise Gate (PROCESSOR):
    • Left Screen renders the live 2D input-to-output transfer curve alongside an animated Gain Reduction bar. Encoders E1..E8 span both screens to control Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release, Knee, Sidechain HPF, Makeup, and Mix.
  3. Rack Slot PROCESSORs (Tape Saturation, Vocal De-Esser, Guitar/Bass Amp Rig, Cab IR, 4-Mode Modulation, 3-Mode Delay, Plate Reverb, Ladder Filter, Transient Shaper, Vocal Rider, Micro-Pitch Doubler, Gain Utility):
    • Left Screen displays real-time slot context and calibrated telemetry (including saturation transfer curves and wet/dry readouts), while E1..E8 map clean 8-encoder parameter pages with physical units (dB, Hz, ms, %). Holding CLEAR and touching any encoder resets that parameter immediately to its unity default.
  4. Hosted External PLUGIN [CLAP] & PLUGIN [AU]:
    • Reads live parameter names and formatted values directly from the hosted plugin across paginated 8-encoder banks (< / > switches parameter pages, with Mix on the final bank slot). Capacitive touch on E1..E8 brackets every tweak into a single coalesced Undo gesture. Press F8: OPEN GUI (or CLOSE GUI) to toggle the desktop floating plugin window. Missing plugins render a clear crimson MISSING GHOST (GHOST) slot state without altering saved preset data.

5.10.2 Tactile [DRUM STUDIO] Synthesis, SAMPLING Workspace, Step Sequencing & Live Performance#

In [DRUM STUDIO], the dual displays and 16 pads act as a dedicated physical drum, bass, and sampling instrument:

  • PLUG-IN (VOICE SYNTH & SCOPE): Left Screen draws the live triggered Storage-CRT oscilloscope trace for the focused voice alongside its archetype badge (MEMBRANE, SNARE, METALLIC, MODAL, ANALOG BASS, or STUDIO SAMPLER). Encoders E1..E4 (Left Screen) and E5..E8 (Right Screen) map all 8 voice synthesis or sampler macros (SHIFT + Turn for 10x fine resolution, CLEAR + Touch to reset to archetype default). Top soft keys map F1..F4 to ARCHETYPE, PHASE MOD, VOICE/BASS, and GLUE BUS, and F5..F8 to STASH KIT, RELOAD KT (SHIFT + F6 quantized to next bar), MORPH PAD, and FILL.
  • SAMPLING (STUDIO SAMPLER Workspace) vs. SHIFT + SAMPLING (STEM & SYNC):
    • Pressing bare SAMPLING opens the dual-screen STUDIO SAMPLER with four top tabs (F1: RECORD, F2: EDIT, F3: SLICE, F4: ZONE), context actions on F5/F6 (TRIM HIST / COMMIT), F7: +SEQ, and F8: APPLY (Kit vs. Track chosen on E8). Left Screen plots the full-sample waveform overview, amber slice flags, cyan active slice, emerald playhead, and E1..E4 (Mode/Source, Sensitivity/Thresh, Choke/Tap, Slices/Bars). Right Screen displays the Split Zero-Crossing Zoom lens around active slice/region Start (E5) and End (E6) plus E7 (PlayMode / BPM Stretch) and E8 (Apply Target / Commit). In SLICE mode, tapping unlit pads drops live zero-crossed chop markers on the fly while lit pads audition slices 1..16 (banked A..D via GROUPS when > 16 slices exist in SLICE-LOCK mode).
    • Pressing SHIFT + SAMPLING (or opening CHANNEL -> F3: STEM PATCH) opens STEM & SYNC (16-voice Pre-Tape Stem Breakout patchbay and Looper Sync controls).
  • STEP MODE (64-Step Polymetric Sequencer): Pads 1..16 follow bottom-to-top hardware row order (1..4 bottom row to 13..16 top row). Left Screen shows a paginated 8-voice labeled matrix (toggleable via F3 to a 16-voice Full-Kit Radar), while Right Screen exposes focused voice step parameters. Turn bare E1..E8 to edit Velocity, Gate %, Micro-Nudge %, Note, Tie/Slide, Flam/Ratchet, Step Condition, and Subdivision, or hold any Step Pad and turn E1..E8 to write per-step macro Parameter Locks (ERASE + Touch clears individual locks). Manual < / > page navigation automatically suspends F8: FOLLOW.
  • KEYBOARD (SHIFT + PAD MODE), NOTE REPEAT, ARP & ALL + NOTE REPEAT: Play ANALOG BASS, chromatic STUDIO SAMPLER voices, or pitched Modal Impact across 16 contiguous semitones or folded musical scales (E1: SCALE, E2 / F5 layout mode, E3: OCTAVE), ride aftertouch-sensitive NOTE REPEAT (> 85% pressure = Accent) or melodic ARP, hold ALL ([CTRL ALL], or ALL + F1 to pin) to fan relative macro sweeps across all unmuted voices, or hold ALL + NOTE REPEAT to play phase-locked Slip Beat-Repeat performance pads (1/4..1/32, REV GRAIN, TAPE STOP).
  • GROUPS A..H & Edit Cluster: PATTERN + A..D selects Pattern Banks A..D (64 patterns, while PATTERN + F4 doubles pattern length 16 -> 32 -> 64), and E..H recall Live Morph Slots M1..M4 (SHIFT + E..H captures). UNDO/REDO, COPY/PASTE, QUANTIZE (SHIFT = 50%), NOTE + Jog (transpose), NUDGE + Jog, CLEAR, ERASE + Hold Pad (real-time step wipe), and SHIFT + MUTE (Choke All Voices) all operate directly on the focused Pattern and Kit.
Part III · Chapter 6

Waveform Timeline, Pass Lanes, Markers & Ranges

2D waveform scrub-zooming, AUTO ZOOM stepwise recording expansion and Full-Take auto-fit, active-surface 1:1 ZOOM (256.0 smp/px), LOCK PLAYHEAD, expandable Pass Lanes, non-destructive live-take mistake surgery, ADC clip repair, 50/60 Hz hum cancellation, range-bounded pass comping, clip gain, spectral spot-heal, markers, Ranges, direct Range-to-Sampler import (-> SAMPLER), Take splitting, and the Multi-Camera Video Monitor with multi-lane time-anchored frame-accurate Camera Filmstrips, 35 mm sprocket tick rails, and 16:9 Frame Loupe skimming.

Every multitrack recording in Cave Recorder is a self-contained Take with its own timeline starting at 00:00:00.000 (t = 0).
