Rather than stringing an entire evening of rehearsals along a multi-hour horizontal scroll bar or stacking separate songs on top of one another, the timeline always focuses on one active Take at a time. Within that active Take, you can scrub and zoom sample-accurate waveforms, expand Pass Lanes to comp track-level overdubs, drop timestamped cue markers on the fly, loop rehearsal sections, and split long jams into individual song Takes.

6.1 Navigating the TIMELINE View & Upper Mini-Timeline Well#

Cave Recorder provides two synchronized timeline viewports for the currently active Take:

  1. Upper Mini-Timeline Well (TIMELINE & WAVEFORM on MIXER): Located in the right-hand well of the Upper Inspector Row on the MIXER view (CMD/CTRL + 2). It displays the waveform of the currently inspected track alongside quick-access transport and zoom keys so you can scrub, zoom, and switch Passes without leaving the faders.
  2. Full-Screen TIMELINE Workspace (CMD/CTRL + 1): Displays all active tracks simultaneously with dedicated Marker ([MARKERS]) and Range ([RANGES]) lanes, per-track headers, expandable Pass Lanes, and a two-row editing toolbar.

6.1.1 Multi-Resolution Waveform Detail & Viewport Readouts#

Both the Upper Mini-Timeline Well and the full-screen TIMELINE view render audio using multi-resolution waveform detail, covering full-song overview envelopes, medium phrase zoom, and individual sample-level waveform display. As you zoom from a 30-minute rehearsal jam down to a single snare transient, the display transitions across pre-computed resolution tiers so transient peaks remain sharp at every scale without frame drops.

The upper-left readout of the TIMELINE toolbar displays the current horizontal resolution in samples per pixel (Zoom: 48.0 smp/px, with 1:1 anchored to 256.0 smp/px) and the visual waveform gain offset (Gain: +0.0 dB), while the right-hand status readout confirms the active Take number, cursor timestamp, and total Take duration (TAKE 001 | CUR: 00:00:00.853 | LEN: 00:00:01.000). Resizing the desktop window dynamically preserves your visible sample span across lane geometry updates so your framing never jumps unexpectedly.

6.1.2 Upper Mini-Timeline Well Controls#

At the bottom of the Upper Mini-Timeline well on MIXER (Chapter 4: Mix Console, Stagebox Mixer, Signal Flow & Channel Strips), six dedicated hardware buttons control the inspected track's timeline:

Control Keyboard Shortcut Function
PASSES E Expands or collapses the Pass Lanes for the currently inspected channel so you can switch or mute individual overdub passes directly from the console.
LOCK PLAYHEAD Configurable in KEYMAP Toggles locking the Playhead (PH, green triangle) and the Position Cursor (CUR, amber diamond) together. When locked, clicking to place the cursor moves the playback start position simultaneously. When unlocked, the Position Cursor can be placed independently as an edit or zoom anchor while playback continues.
→ PLAYHEAD . Snaps the transport Playhead immediately to the current Position Cursor location.
ZOOM + = Zooms horizontally into the waveform by one octave (halving the smp/px span).
ZOOM - - Zooms horizontally out of the waveform by one octave (doubling the smp/px span).
1:1 0 Sets the active timeline surface (MIXER mini-timeline, CHANNEL STRIP mini-timeline, or full-screen TIMELINE) to the exact 256.0 smp/px reference zoom scale.

6.1.3 Full-Screen TIMELINE Toolbar & Track Headers#

Pressing CMD/CTRL + 1 (or clicking TIMELINE in the navigation bar) opens the multi-track timeline workspace. Above the waveform canvas, two toolbar rows provide direct access to zoom, lane visibility, marker placement, and Take splitting:

  • Row 1 (Viewport & Lane Controls):
    • ZOOM + / ZOOM - / 1:1: Step horizontal zoom in (=), step out (-), or set the active timeline surface (TIMELINE, CHANNEL STRIP mini-timeline, or MIXER mini-timeline) to the exact 256.0 smp/px reference scale (0).
    • AUTO ZOOM (Stepwise Recording Zoom & Full-Take Auto-Fit): New-Take recordings open on a crisp 10.0 s window with AUTO ZOOM latched. Whenever the advancing recording playhead reaches 80% of the visible span, Cave Recorder automatically steps the viewport out by one octave so the playhead sits comfortably at 40% and the entire Take stays in view from 00:00:00.000. Manual zooming or panning unlatches AUTO ZOOM, and clicking AUTO ZOOM re-latches it at any time. Stopping and committing a recording, rescuing a SAVE RETRO Take, switching Takes, or opening a Session automatically performs Full-Take Auto Zoom-to-Fit, framing the complete Take edge-to-edge and selecting the R001 Full Take range.
    • H- / H+ (Track Lane Height): Steps the vertical height of all track waveform lanes between 56 px (compact 18-channel overview) and 220 px (tall surgical transient inspection). Track header heights on the left stay locked 1:1 with their waveform lanes.
    • LOCK PLAYHEAD & → PLAYHEAD: Identical to the Mini-Timeline well controls, allowing coupled or decoupled Playhead and Position Cursor operation.
    • MARKERS & RANGES: Toggle visibility of the dedicated MARKERS and RANGES ruler lanes above the audio tracks.
    • EXPAND ALL PASSES & COLLAPSE ALL PASSES: Unrolls (E) or collapses (SHIFT + E) the overdub Pass Lanes across every track in the active Take simultaneously.
  • Row 2 (Markers, Ranges, Sampler Import & Take Split Bar):
    • + MARKER (M) / RANGE START (K) / RANGE END (L): Drops a cue marker at the Playhead (M) or defines the start (K) and end (L) boundaries of a loop or song range.
    • NEW TAKE, SPLIT TAKE & -> SAMPLER: Extracts the active range as a new self-contained Take (NEW TAKE), divides the active Take into two consecutive Takes at the current Playhead/Cursor position (SPLIT TAKE), or sends the active Range directly into the Studio Sampler (-> SAMPLER, paired with DRY PASS or POST-FX mode inside GROOVEBOX -> SAMPLER, see Section 5.9.5 in Chapter 5).
    • |< FIRST / < PREV / NEXT > / LAST >|: Jumps the Playhead to the first marker (SHIFT + [ or HOME), previous marker ([), next marker (]), or final marker (SHIFT + ] or END) in the active Take.

Each row in the left-hand TRACK LANES & OVERDUB PASSES column displays the track number and scribble-strip name (01 Kick In), the Pass Lane disclosure button (▶ (1) or ▶ (2) showing the number of recorded Passes on that track in the current Take), Mute (M), Solo (S), Record Arm (R), and Input Monitor (I) switches (in universal [M][S][R] Solo Gold order), the active Pass badge (PASS 01 or OD 02), the output bus assignment (OUT: SUB 1 or OUT: MST), the channel fader readout (-2.4 dB), and the sample span summary (Span: 0..48000 smp (1.00s) | 2 pass(es)).

6.1.4 Complete Reference of Timeline Navigation & Zoom Gestures#

Cave Recorder supports fast one-handed 2D Scrub-Zooming directly on the timeline ruler and waveform canvas, alongside standard mouse wheel, trackpad, and keyboard navigation:

Gesture / Action Input / Shortcut Behavior
Reposition Playhead / Cursor Single-Click (< 4 px travel) on ruler or waveform canvas Places the crisp 1 px Playhead or Position Cursor at the clicked timestamp. Automatically snaps to Take start (00:00:00.000) and Take end boundaries within 8 px.
Bypass Boundary Snapping Hold SHIFT or CMD/CTRL + Click Places the Playhead or Position Cursor at the exact sub-sample mouse coordinate without snapping to Take boundaries.
2D Ruler / Canvas Scrub-Zoom Click + Drag Vertically (up/down) on ruler or canvas Continuously zooms the timeline exponentially in or out anchored directly to the sample beneath the cursor (or around the Playhead when LOCK PLAYHEAD is active).
2D Ruler Scrub / Canvas Pan Click + Drag Horizontally (left/right) on ruler or canvas Dragging horizontally on the ruler scrubs the Playhead across the Take. Dragging horizontally on the waveform canvas pans the visible time window left or right.
Nudge Timeline Cursor LEFT / RIGHT (hold SHIFT for 10x step) Nudges the Position Cursor (and the Playhead when LOCK PLAYHEAD is active) backward or forward by a fine or coarse sample step.
Horizontal Scroll Pan Two-Finger Horizontal Trackpad Scroll or SHIFT + Mouse Wheel Smoothly pans the visible viewport backward or forward across the active Take.
Modifier Scroll Zoom CMD/CTRL + Mouse Wheel Zooms horizontally in or out anchored at the current mouse pointer position.
Step Zoom In / Out ZOOM + (=) / ZOOM - (-) Zooms horizontally in or out by one octave per press.
Reset Zoom (1:1) 1:1 (0) Sets the active timeline surface (TIMELINE, CHANNEL STRIP mini-timeline, or MIXER mini-timeline) to exact 256.0 smp/px.
Toggle Timeline Auto-Scroll SCROLL in Top Deck (configurable in KEYMAP) Follows the advancing Playhead automatically during playback and live recording, paging the viewport forward whenever the Playhead reaches the right edge. Manually panning during playback temporarily suspends following until re-engaged.
Snap Playhead to Cursor → PLAYHEAD (.) Moves the green transport Playhead to the amber Position Cursor immediately.
Zooming Around the Playhead vs. Mouse Cursor (LOCK PLAYHEAD)

Enable LOCK PLAYHEAD when you want keyboard zoom keys (= / -) and vertical scrub-zoom drags to stay centered on the rolling Playhead during playback. Disable LOCK PLAYHEAD when editing stationary waveforms so zooming stays pinned to the exact transient under your mouse cursor or Position Cursor.

6.2 Recording Overdubs (OVERDUB) & Comping in Expandable Pass Lanes (PASSES)#

In Cave Recorder, session-level songs and track-level overdubs are strictly separated so your timeline never becomes cluttered:

  • Base Pass (Rec001, labeled PASS 01): When OVERDUB is off (the default), pressing Record (R) creates a brand-new session Take starting at 00:00:00.000. Every armed channel strip records its initial multitrack stem as Rec001 (PASS 01).
  • Overdub Pass (Rec002-OD, Rec003-OD, ..., labeled OD 02, OD 03, ...): When you want to layer a second guitar solo, punch in a vocal fix, or try three alternate bass lines inside the currently active Take, latch the crimson OVERDUB button in the Top Deck transport bar (O) and arm only the target track(s). Pressing Record (R) plays back the existing tracks of the active Take from 00:00:00.000 while recording a new Overdub Pass (OD 02, OD 03, ...) into the active Take's rec/ folder and appending a new Pass Lane under each armed track.

6.2.1 Step-by-Step: Recording Multi-Pass Overdubs on a Track#

  1. Load the Target Take: Use the < / > buttons beside TAKE 001 in the Top Deck (ALT + [ / ALT + ]) or click Load in TAKES (CMD/CTRL + 5) to load the Take you want to overdub onto.
  2. Disarm Backing Tracks & Arm the Overdub Track: On MIXER or in the left track header column of TIMELINE, disarm (R off) the backing band tracks (drums, rhythm section) so they stream from disk, and arm (R lit crimson) only the channel(s) you are overdubbing. Enable input monitoring (I / MON) if you are monitoring through Cave Recorder's console EQ and compression.
  3. Latch Overdub Mode (OVERDUB): Click OVERDUB in the Top Deck transport bar (or press O) so the indicator illuminates crimson and the timecode badge confirms OVERDUB.
  4. Optional Pre-Roll or Cycle Range: Position the Playhead a few bars before the section you want to overdub, or enable Cycle Loop (⇄, C) across a defined range (Section 6.3).
  5. Record the Overdub Pass: Press Record (R) to begin playback and capture OD 02. Press Stop (SPACE or SHIFT + SPACE) when finished. Cave Recorder automatically promotes the newly recorded Overdub Pass (★ OD 02) as the active playback Pass on that track and captures a post-recording Snapshot.
Automatic Overdub Latency Compensation

When you record an Overdub Pass (OD 02), Cave Recorder automatically compensates the recorded Pass Lane using your calibrated hardware loopback offset and live monitoring latency (displayed in the Pass Lane header as -640 smp (-13.3ms)). Backing tracks stream from disk with negative read-ahead compensation so your new overdub lands phase-aligned with the original PASS 01 drum and rhythm stems. See Chapter 2: Hardware Setup, Audio Connections & First Session for loopback calibration details.

6.2.2 Expanding Pass Lanes, Auditioning Passes & Comping Phrases#

When a track within the active Take has more than one recorded Pass, the disclosure badge in the track header displays the total Pass count (for example, ▶ (2) on 02 Snare Top and 03 Overhead L).

  • Expand or Collapse a Single Track's Pass Lanes:
    • Click the ▶ (N) / ▼ (N) badge in the track header on the WAVEFORM TIMELINE view.
    • Or select the track and click PASSES in the Upper Mini-Timeline Well (or press E while in the CHANNEL INSPECTOR view).
  • Expand or Collapse All Tracks' Pass Lanes:
    • Click EXPAND ALL PASSES (E) or COLLAPSE ALL PASSES (SHIFT + E) in the upper-right WAVEFORM TIMELINE toolbar.

When expanded, each track unrolls its vertical stack of Pass Lanes in chronological order (BASE PASS PASS 01 at the top, followed by OVERDUB OD 02, OD 03, and so on):

  • Visual Active vs. Standby Distinction: The currently active Pass Lane (labeled ACTIVE COMP LANE with a green ★ PASS 01 or ★ OD 02 badge) renders its waveform in bright amber-copper. Inactive Pass Lanes (labeled STANDBY COMP LANE with a Use PASS 01 or Use OD 02 button) render in muted slate-grey so you can immediately see which Pass is feeding the Mix Console channel strip.
  • Auditioning & Promoting Passes:
    • Promoting a Pass on the WAVEFORM TIMELINE View: Click Use PASS 01 (or Use OD 02, Use OD 03) in any standby Pass Lane header to promote that Pass as the active playback lane (ACTIVE COMP LANE) immediately. Because playback readers pre-buffer ahead of the Playhead, switching Passes during playback crossfades cleanly without clicks.
    • Promoting a Pass from the MIX CONSOLE or CHANNEL INSPECTOR View: Click PASSES in the Upper Mini-Timeline Well (or press E in the CHANNEL INSPECTOR view) to expand the inspected channel's Pass Lanes, and click Use PASS <NN> or Use OD <NN> on the Pass you want to hear.
  • Per-Pass Mute (M) & Soft Delete (Del):
    • Click M on a Pass Lane to silence that Pass without changing your channel strip Mute state.
    • Click Del on a flawed Pass Lane to mark that Pass as deleted in the session history. Because deletion is non-destructive, pressing CMD/CTRL + Z restores the Pass immediately.
  • Comping Phrases Across Multiple Passes:
    • When an overdub was punched in over a specific chorus or solo section (for example, Span: 240000..480000 smp), promoting that Overdub Pass plays your new performance across its recorded span while allowing you to compare it directly against the underlying PASS 01 Base Pass or alternate OD 03 passes. Every Pass promotion is recorded in the Undo history and stored in Console Snapshots (Chapter 7: Session Reel, Mixdowns, Snapshots, Disk Layout & Cloud Sync) so you can save and compare multiple comp combinations across the session.

6.3 Dropping Cue Markers & Defining Cycle Loop Ranges (MARKERS)#

During a live rehearsal jam or playback review, you can drop timestamped Markers and define bounded Ranges without stopping the transport. Markers and Ranges appear both as interactive flags in the MARKERS and RANGES lanes of TIMELINE and as sortable, searchable rows in the dedicated MARKERS workspace (CMD/CTRL + 4).

6.3.1 Dropping & Navigating Cue Markers on the Fly (M)#

Every Take automatically initializes with two boundary markers (M001 Take Start at 00:00:00.000 and M002 Take End at the end of the longest recorded stem, forming the default R001 Full Take range). To mark song transitions, solo entrances, or mix notes:

  1. Drop a Marker (M): Press M at any time during live recording or playback (or click + MARKER (M) in the TIMELINE toolbar or ADD MARKER (M) in the MARKERS toolbar). Cave Recorder places a cyan standalone marker flag (M005 Marker 05, M006 Marker 06) at the exact sample position of the rolling Playhead (or at the Position Cursor when transport is stopped).
  2. Reposition a Marker by Dragging: In the MARKERS lane of TIMELINE, hover over any cyan marker flag to inspect its metadata, or click and drag the marker handle left or right to fine-tune its sample timestamp.
  3. Jump Between Markers: Use the toolbar buttons or keyboard shortcuts to navigate between cue points instantly:
    • Previous Marker (< PREV / < PREV MKR): Press [.
    • Next Marker (NEXT > / NEXT MKR >): Press ].
    • First Marker in Take (|< FIRST / |< FIRST MKR): Press SHIFT + [ or HOME.
    • Last Marker in Take (LAST >| / LAST MKR >|): Press SHIFT + ] or END.

6.3.2 Defining Ranges (K / L) & Cycle Loop Playback (⇄)#

A Range (R001, R003, ...) is a named time span bounded by a RANGE START marker and a RANGE END marker. Ranges are used for Cycle Loop playback, overdub punch/loop rehearsal, zooming to a song section, and extracting a song section as a new Take.

  1. Mark Range Start (RANGE START (K)): Move the Playhead or Position Cursor to the beginning of the phrase (or press it live as the band hits the downbeat) and press K (or click RANGE START (K) / SET RANGE START (K)). An amber status pill (RNG T01: START @ 00:00:00.853) appears in the toolbar indicating that a range start boundary is pending.
  2. Mark Range End (RANGE END (L)): When playback reaches the end of the section, press L (or click RANGE END (L) / SET RANGE END (L)). Cave Recorder pairs the start and end boundaries, creates a new numbered Range span (such as R003 Range 03) in the amber RANGES lane, and selects it as the active loop range.
  3. Cancel a Pending Boundary (ESC): If you pressed K by mistake, press ESC or click CANCEL PENDING RANGE to discard the uncompleted boundary.
  4. Select, Drag, or Cycle Overlapping Ranges: In the RANGES lane above the waveforms, click any amber range bar to make it the active range (clicking repeatedly on overlapping spans cycles through them). Drag the left [ or right ] handle of any range bar in the RANGES lane to adjust its start or end sample directly on the timeline.
  5. Toggle Cycle Loop Playback (⇄): Click the Cycle Loop button ⇄ in the Top Deck transport bar (or press C). When ⇄ is illuminated amber, playback loops continuously between the start and end boundaries of the active Range (or across R001 Full Take if no sub-range is selected).
  6. Send a Range Directly to the Studio Sampler (-> SAMPLER): With any Range or loop region active, click -> SAMPLER in the timeline toolbar to load that exact [start, end) span into the focused Studio Sampler voice in GROOVEBOX -> SAMPLER (DRY PASS extracts the selected track's active Pass Lane in under 20 ms, honoring overdub record offsets and range comp crossfades, while POST-FX renders a post-insert bounce of the selected Track, Subgroup, Aux Return, or Master Bus into <SessionFolder>/samples/). On a Studio Pad Surface in [CONSOLE DAW REMOTE], hold any lit Range pad in SCENE mode and press F5: -> SAMPLER or F6: POST-FX -> SMP.

6.3.3 Managing, Renaming & Filtering in the MARKERS View#

Pressing CMD/CTRL + 4 (or clicking MARKERS in the workspace navigation bar) opens the MARKERS management workspace, divided into two synchronized tables: MARKERS (top) and RANGES (bottom).

  • Session-Wide vs. Per-Take Filtering: Use the top filter bar (ALL TAKES (SESSION), FILTER TAKE 001, FILTER TAKE 002) to view cue points across every Take in the evening's Session at once, or isolate markers belonging to a single Take. Clicking VIEW TAKE 001 TIMELINE jumps directly to TIMELINE with that Take loaded.
  • Marker Type Filtering & Automatic Color Badges: Filter the upper table by ALL, STANDALONE (crimson STANDALONE badges, such as M005), or BOUNDARY (slate RANGE START and RANGE END badges paired to a Range, such as RANGE START (R003)), or type into Search markers... to filter by marker name or description note.
  • Per-Marker Actions (GO TO, Rename, -> RNG START, -> RNG END, DEL):
    • GO TO: Loads the owning Take (if not already active) and snaps the transport Playhead directly to that marker's exact sample position.
    • Rename (or inline click on Marker Name): Opens inline editing fields to update the marker's Name (for example, Verse 2 Harmonies) and free-form Description note (ENTER saves, ESC cancels), or click PRESET MARKER HIGHLIGHT M<NNN> to emphasize key cue points.
    • -> RNG START / -> RNG END: Promotes an existing standalone cue marker into the start or end boundary of a Range so you can drop single-key M markers during a live jam and turn them into bounded song ranges afterward.
    • DEL: Deletes the marker (reversible via Undo CMD/CTRL + Z).
  • Range Filtering (ALL / FROM STANDALONE) & Per-Range Actions (ZOOM RANGE, NEW TAKE, Rename, DEL):
    • FROM STANDALONE Filter Pill: Filters the RANGES table (alongside ALL) to show only Ranges whose start or end boundaries were promoted from standalone cue markers via -> RNG START / -> RNG END.
    • ZOOM RANGE: Switches to TIMELINE and zooms the horizontal viewport to frame that exact Range from edge to edge.
    • Rename (or inline click on Range Name): Opens inline fields to rename the Range (for example, R003 Chorus Loop or Song 2 - Midnight Drive) and update its description.

6.4 Non-Destructive Take Splitting (Split Take at Playhead / Split by Markers)#

During a band rehearsal, musicians often hit Record once and play a continuous 25-minute block containing warm-up banter, three separate songs, and an improvised jam. Cave Recorder lets you carve that long continuous capture into independent, self-contained t = 0 Takes (Take 002, Take 003, Take 004) so each song gets its own 00:00:00.000 timeline, its own song tag, and its own stereo mixdown.

6.4.1 Three Ways to Split or Extract Independent Takes#

Cave Recorder provides three non-destructive workflows depending on whether you want to divide a Take in two or extract a specific marker/range span:

Split / Extract Method Where to Trigger How It Works
1. Split Take at Playhead / Cursor (SPLIT TAKE) Click SPLIT TAKE in the TIMELINE toolbar Divides the active Take at the current Playhead/Cursor timestamp into two consecutive segments: the first part (00:00:00.000 to the split point) remains in the current Take, and the second part (from the split point to the end) becomes a brand-new t = 0 Take (Take<NNN>).
2. Extract from Marker to End (NEW TAKE -> END) Click NEW TAKE -> END on any standalone marker row in MARKERS (CMD/CTRL + 4) Extracts everything from that marker's sample timestamp through the end of the Take into a brand-new t = 0 Take (Take<NNN>), leaving the source Take's full duration untouched.
3. Extract Bounded Range as New Take (NEW TAKE) Click NEW TAKE in the TIMELINE toolbar (with a Range selected) or click NEW TAKE on any row in the RANGES table (CMD/CTRL + 4) Copies the exact sample span between the Range's START and END boundaries (R003) into a brand-new t = 0 Take (Take<NNN>) whose 00:00:00.000 origin corresponds to the start of that Range, leaving the source Take's span untouched.

6.4.2 How Non-Destructive Splitting Preserves Stems, Passes & Phase Offsets#

When you divide a Take with SPLIT TAKE or extract a span with NEW TAKE:

  1. Zero Destructive File Overwrites & Full Undo: None of your original .wav files on disk are ever overwritten or deleted. Both SPLIT TAKE and NEW TAKE are tracked in the Session's Undo history, so pressing CMD/CTRL + Z reverses the split or extraction immediately.
  2. Sample-Zero (t = 0) Alignment: Every multitrack stem in the newly created Take (Take<NNN>) starts at its own 00:00:00.000 timeline zero aligned to the split or range start point, with Broadcast Wave (bext) timecode metadata preserved.
  3. Pass Structure & Console Routing Preserved: All recorded Base Passes (Rec001) and Overdub Passes (Rec002-OD) that overlap the extracted span are preserved in their respective Pass Lanes, along with per-track phase alignment offsets, latency compensation metadata, and internal markers shifted relative to the new 00:00:00.000 origin.
  4. Immediate Session Reel Registration: The newly created Take appears immediately in the SESSION REEL catalog (Chapter 7: Session Reel, Mixdowns, Snapshots, Disk Layout & Cloud Sync) ready for tagging, live Print conversion, or offline Mixdown rendering.
  5. Non-Blocking Background Execution & Transactional Rollback: Both SPLIT TAKE and NEW TAKE run asynchronously off the 60 Hz timeline thread so waveform scrubbing and console metering stay responsive. If you switch Sessions while a split is running, Cave Recorder discards stale completion state automatically, and if disk space runs out before completion, staged files roll back cleanly so your source Take stays untouched.

6.5 Non-Destructive Live-Take Salvage & Timeline Mistake Surgery#

When a full band plays live in one room and captures a magic Take where the groove, tempo push, and collective energy are unrepeatable, you should never have to throw away that performance because of a minor technical or musical blemish: a snare rimshot that clipped the preamp converter for 14 samples, a vintage guitar combo that buzzed at 60 Hz, a lead vocal phrase that jumped out 6 dB too loud in the bridge, a flubbed chord in bar 38, or a vocalist bumping the microphone stand during an acoustic intro.

Cave Recorder provides six 100% non-destructive Live-Take Salvage and Mistake Surgery tools directly inside TIMELINE (CMD/CTRL + 1) and CHANNEL STRIP (CMD/CTRL + 3). Every operation preserves your original 32-bit floating-point .wav files untouched on disk and is tracked in the Session's Undo/Redo history (CMD/CTRL + Z):

Non-Blocking Audio Surgery & Transactional Protection

Heavy timeline surgery ([REPAIR CLIPPING], 50/60 Hz hum cancellation, [PATCH FROM SOURCE...], and [SMOOTH OVER ARTIFACT]) executes asynchronously off the 60 Hz interface thread with live progress in the Top Deck Async Job pill. Automatic session-switch safety guards ensure background repairs never apply to the wrong Take or Session, and transactional file writes roll back cleanly if disk space runs out mid-repair so your source recordings stay intact.

+====================================================================+
|     NON-DESTRUCTIVE LIVE-TAKE SALVAGE & MISTAKE SURGERY SUITE      |
+====================================================================+
  [1] [REPAIR CLIPPING] (Two-Tier Smooth Spline & Spectral De-Clipper)
      * Reconstructs flat-topped ADC converter clips (1..256 samples)
  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  [2] 50/60 Hz 12-HARMONIC COMB HUM CANCELLER (Q = 20..100 Notch)
      * Strips f_0 .. 12*f_0 mains & dimmer buzz without dulling tone
  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  [3] RANGE-BOUNDED PASS COMPING ([USE OD 02 IN RANGE])
      * Punches an Overdub Pass into a selected Range with 5..50 ms
        equal-power sin/cos crossfades (zero clicks, zero file edits)
  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  [4] PRE-INSERT CLIP GAIN ENVELOPE (-24.0 dB to +24.0 dB)
      * Normalizes a single loud phrase or quiet intro BEFORE the
        8-slot rack so compressors & tape saturators hit evenly
  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  [5] [PATCH FROM SOURCE...] (Same-Take or Cross-Take Bar Graft)
      * Copies a clean chord or drum fill from another bar (or another
        Take) into the selected Range with phase-locked crossfades
  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  [6] [SMOOTH OVER ARTIFACT] (5..150 ms Spectral Spot-Heal)
      * Erases a mic stand bump, cable pop, lip smack, or stick click
        using bidirectional waveform & spectral synthesis
+====================================================================+

6.5.1 [REPAIR CLIPPING]: Reconstructing Clipped Preamp Transients#

If an enthusiastic snare hit or vocal shout overloaded the hardware audio interface's analog-to-digital converter (0.0 dBFS) during tracking, red clip markers appear along the top edge of the waveform in WAVEFORM TIMELINE:

  1. Select the Clipped Region (or Full Track): Frame the clipped transient using a Range (K and L) or leave no sub-range selected to scan the entire active Pass on the selected track.
  2. Click [REPAIR CLIPPING]: Cave Recorder locates every contiguous flat-topped sample plateau where |x[n]| >= Clip Threshold (default -0.1 dBFS, adjustable from -12.0 dBFS to 0.0 dBFS if an external analog preamp or pedal clipped below digital full scale).
  3. Two-Tier Waveform Reconstruction:
    • Short Clips (1 to 8 samples): Rebuilds the rounded peak using smooth spline interpolation matched to the entry and exit slopes of the waveform.
    • Medium & Long Clips (9 to 256 samples): Fits a forward/backward harmonic waveform prediction model to the 512 clean context samples before and after the clip, predicts the harmonic waveform forward and backward across the clipped gap with a raised-cosine blend, and writes the repaired region to a companion repair layer while keeping the original Rec001.wav stem intact.

6.5.2 50 Hz / 60 Hz 12-Harmonic Comb Hum Canceller#

When a single-coil guitar pickup, vintage bass amplifier, or unshielded stage cable injects 50 Hz or 60 Hz power-line buzz into a great live Take, enable the Hum Canceller on that track (50 Hz or 60 Hz fundamental selector, 45.0..65.0 Hz fine tune, 12 Harmonics, Q = 20.0..100.0, default Q = 60.0). Twelve ultra-narrow constant-Q notch filters remove the fundamental and its first 11 overtones (60 Hz through 720 Hz) without carving a wide hole out of your bass or guitar low-mids.

6.5.3 Range-Bounded Pass Comping ([USE OD 02 IN RANGE])#

In Section 6.2, clicking Use OD 02 switches the entire track from start to finish to Overdub Pass OD 02. Frequently, however, the original live PASS 01 (Rec001) is magical for 95% of the song and you only recorded a quick Overdub Pass (OD 02) to fix a single missed lyric or guitar clam in Verse 2:

  1. Expand the track's Pass Lanes with E in WAVEFORM TIMELINE (CMD/CTRL + 2).
  2. Mark the start and end of the phrase to replace using K (RANGE START) and L (RANGE END).
  3. Click [USE OD 02 IN RANGE] (or the desired standby Pass row inside the bounded Range).
  4. Cave Recorder keeps PASS 01 active across the rest of the song and cleanly splices OD 02 into that exact Range using a phase-accurate 5 ms to 50 ms equal-power (sin/cos) crossfade at both boundaries.

6.5.4 Pre-Insert Clip Gain Envelope (-24.0 dB to +24.0 dB)#

If a guitarist kicked on a solo boost pedal that jumped out +7 dB too loud in the bridge, lowering the channel fader after the 8-slot rack will not stop the channel's TAPE saturator and VCA CMP compressor from being slammed into heavy distortion during that bridge.

Instead, select the Range (K .. L) on the waveform and drag the Pre-Insert Clip Gain Handle (-24.0 dB to +24.0 dB, with smooth 5 ms entry/exit ramps). Because Clip Gain is applied directly to the disk playback reader before the 8-slot processor rack, pulling the loud bridge down by -6.0 dB on the waveform ensures the track hits your channel EQ, tape drive, and compressor at the exact same sweet-spot level as the rest of the song.

6.5.5 [PATCH FROM SOURCE...]: Grafting a Clean Bar or Chord Across Bars or Takes#

What if the bass player or rhythm guitarist hit one wrong chord in the second chorus of a live Take, and nobody noticed until mixing day when the band has already packed up their gear?

Because the band played the exact same chord progression cleanly in Chorus 1 (or in another Take from the same rehearsal session), you can repair the mistake using [PATCH FROM SOURCE...]:

  1. Select the Flawed Target Range: In WAVEFORM TIMELINE, mark the 1-bar or 1-chord mistake span using K and L on the target track.
  2. Click [PATCH FROM SOURCE...] and Choose the Clean Source Bar: Select an earlier or later timestamp from the same Take (for example, Chorus 1) or from another Take in the Session.
  3. Automatic Transient & Phase-Correlation Micro-Alignment (±50 ms): Even when a band plays without a click track, Cave Recorder automatically slides the source audio snippet within a ±50 ms window to maximize waveform cross-correlation and zero-crossing phase alignment at both the entry and exit boundaries, welding the clean chord into place with adjustable 10 ms to 100 ms equal-power crossfades.

6.5.6 [SMOOTH OVER ARTIFACT]: Spectral & Waveform Spot-Heal (5 ms to 150 ms)#

During an intimate acoustic intro or quiet vocal breakdown, a stray mechanical noise (a vocalist bumping the mic stand, a guitar cable pop, a loud lip smack, or an accidental drumstick click on a rim) can momentarily distract from the performance. Simple muting leaves an unnatural hole in the room ambience.

To erase a short transient blemish (5 ms to 150 ms) without leaving a gap:

  1. Zoom in (ZOOM + or vertical drag) and bracket the 5 ms to 150 ms artifact with RANGE START (K) and RANGE END (L).
  2. Click [SMOOTH OVER ARTIFACT] in the timeline toolbar.
  3. Cave Recorder analyzes the 250 ms of clean room tone and sustained note harmonics immediately before and after the artifact:
    • For short clicks and pops (5 ms to 25 ms), it performs bidirectional harmonic waveform interpolation across the gap.
    • For longer thumps or stand bumps (25 ms to 150 ms), it performs Windowed Spectral Magnitude & Phase Coherence Interpolation, replacing only the transient anomaly with continuous harmonic sustain and natural room ambience while leaving the rest of the track untouched.

6.6 Multi-Camera Video Monitor & Timeline Filmstrip (video/*.mp4 & .vididx)#

When one or more studio cameras or wireless Cave Companion mobile camera nodes are armed during a Take, Cave Recorder displays each camera angle as its own stacked Video Timeline Strip lane inside WAVEFORM TIMELINE (CMD/CTRL + 2) paired with a real-time Multi-Camera Video Monitor.

6.6.1 48.0 kHz Audio-Clock Synchronization & the .vididx Frame Index#

To prevent audio/video drift across 30-minute rehearsal jams and ensure instant frame-accurate scrubbing without scanning multi-gigabyte .mp4 container files, every recorded camera file (<TakeFolder>/video/<SessionID>_Take<NNN>_Cam<CC>-<Name>_<Stamp>.mp4) is accompanied by a deterministic frame index file (.vididx):

  • Exact Integer 48.0 kHz Audio-Clock Timestamps: Rather than trusting the operating system wall clock or USB bus arrival jitter, Cave Recorder stamps every captured video frame against the hardware audio interface's monotonic sample counter (960 samples per frame at 50 FPS, 1,920 samples at 25 FPS, 1,600 samples at 30 FPS, or 800 samples at 60 FPS).
  • .vididx Frame Index Structure: Each .vididx file stores the camera's nominal frame rate, 48.0 kHz sample rate, calibrated optical latency offset, user camera trim offset, and a per-frame index of t = 0 audio sample positions and keyframe offsets.
  • Instant Keyframe Lookup & Scrubbing: During timeline playback or rapid ruler scrubbing, Cave Recorder looks up the target video frame directly from the .vididx index, jumps to the nearest preceding 0.5 s (25-frame) keyframe, and decodes only the minimal forward frames required to display the exact target image.

6.6.2 BT.709 Video Monitor & Sample-Locked Playback#

The Video Monitor renders camera frames in BT.709 studio color space. While transport playback is rolling, Cave Recorder continuously keeps all active camera angles locked to the 48.0 kHz audio playhead:

Sync State Audio-to-Video Offset (|Δt|) Playback Synchronizer Action
Locked Cadence |Δt| <= 0.5 frame (<= 10.0 ms @ 50 FPS) Presents every decoded CFR frame in natural 1:1 cadence with zero frame drops or repeats.
Smooth Catch-Up 0.5 frame < |Δt| <= 2.5 frames (10..50 ms) Advances or holds a single frame step within the current 0.5 s GOP so visual sync converges smoothly without decoder reset.
Keyframe Seek |Δt| > 2.5 frames (> 50.0 ms, or after a timeline scrub jump) Dispatches an immediate .vididx keyframe seek to the target GOP and pre-rolls to the exact playhead sample.

6.6.3 Operating the Video Timeline Filmstrip & Camera Trim Offset Slider#

Each simultaneous camera angle renders in its own stacked lane in WAVEFORM TIMELINE (CMD/CTRL + 2) as a time-anchored, frame-accurate thumbnail filmstrip aligned 1:1 with the horizontal audio sample ruler:

  1. Camera Angle Selection & Split-Screen Preview: Click any camera lane header (Cam01-Drums, Cam02-GtrMobile, Cam03-RoomMobile) to focus that angle in the Video Monitor, or switch the monitor to Multi-Camera Split-Screen mode (Side-by-Side Crop, Side-by-Side 16:9, 3-Cam Band, or Quad 2x2) to inspect all angles simultaneously.
  2. Time-Anchored Filmstrip Span & 35 mm Sprocket Tick Rails: Every recorded video clip spans its exact start-to-end sample range on the timeline (incorporating its recorded start time and Camera Trim Offset) with frame-accurate thumbnail decoding and top/bottom 35 mm filmstrip sprocket tick rails marking exact frame boundaries when zoomed in.
  3. Interactive Pointer Skimming & Floating 16:9 Frame Loupe Popover: Moving your pointer across any camera filmstrip lane reveals a cyan skimmer hairline, a floating high-resolution 16:9 BT.709 Frame Loupe Popover displaying the exact frame number and timestamp (#F<frame> · <MM:SS.mmm>), and a vertical transient alignment guide extending down across the audio tracks so you can visually line up drumstick impact or pick attack against the audio waveform.
  4. Per-Clip Fine Trim Nudge (Camera Trim Offset): Although the 3-Second Camera Latency Calibration modal (Section 2.5.2) automatically compensates for hardware sensor and capture-card delay, you can fine-tune any individual video clip's alignment on the timeline using its Camera Trim Offset slider (adjustable in exact audio samples and milliseconds, with Double-Click / Alt+Click reset to 0 smp). Adjusting the camera trim offset updates the .vididx and take.json metadata non-destructively and propagates automatically into offline split-screen .mp4 mixdowns and .fcpxml v1.9 multicam exports.
Part III · Chapter 7

Takes Dashboard, Mixdowns, Snapshots, Companion Mobile & Cloud Sync

Managing Takes with streamlined 4-button rows ([Load], [Rename], [Export...], [...]) and ARCHIVE / Restore governance, converting live Prints to FLAC and MP3, rendering offline Mixdowns, Stem Bounces, and Multi-Camera Split-Screen .mp4 Video Mixdowns, exporting Takes to external workstation project formats (.rpp, .als, Session XML, .dawproject, .fcpxml multicam and stacked split-screen timelines, and BWF/iXML bundles), comparing Snapshots with persistent Live Mix A/B banners, disk naming rules including Studio Sampler samples/ and stagebox_scene.json storage, resumable Google Drive video and mix sync, and the Cave Companion Mobile ecosystem (Android API 36 / 16 KB .apk and iOS .ipa) featuring zero-configuration Bonjour Wi-Fi discovery, the bundled Sample Studio Session (UNPAIRED SAMPLE), responsive 6-tab Phone and 8-tab Tablet navigation, wireless MIXER, STAGEBOX (MY MONITOR and PIN-lockable FULL MIXER), and GROOVEBOX + SAMPLER remotes.

A typical three-hour band rehearsal or studio tracking night produces anywhere from five to twenty recorded Takes alongside evolving console mixes, overdub passes, and stereo mixes for the band group chat. Cave Recorder centralizes all session management inside the TAKES workspace (CMD/CTRL + 5), combining a searchable Takes Catalog with streamlined 4-button rows ([Load], [Rename], [Export…], [⋯]), one-click Print-to-FLAC and Print-to-MP3 conversion, offline Master Mixdowns, Stem Bounces, and External Workstation Project & Bundle Exports, non-destructive Console Snapshots with Live Mix protection, a self-documenting disk layout, built-in two-way Google Drive Cloud Sync, and the Cave Companion wireless mobile and tablet ecosystem.

7.1 Managing Takes in the TAKES View#

Pressing CMD/CTRL + 5 (or clicking TAKES in the workspace navigation bar) opens the Takes Dashboard ledger for the currently open Session.

7.1.1 The Session Header & Undo/Redo History Bar#

At the top of the TAKES view, two horizontal control bars summarize the active Session and its edit history:

  • Session Metadata & Global Actions Bar:
    • Displays the parent Project badge (PROJ: TEST), the permanent Session ID (TEST_20261020-2), the human-readable Session display title (Birthday Studio Session), the optional folder tag (TAG:BirthdayMix), the hardware sample rate (48000 Hz), and the count of active and archived Takes.
    • Rename (Inline Session Title) & Clear Session Tag: Rename the Session's display title inline (or from the Top Deck Session pill) or edit/clear its <SessionTag>. Editing a Session tag cleanly renames the Session folder on disk and updates all relative links in <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/ without renaming any audio files inside.
    • ARCHIVED Filter & Empty Trash…: Toggle visibility of archived Takes in the catalog (paired with the ALL + ARCHIVED filter pill below) or click the crimson Empty Trash… button when archived Takes or archived Studio Sampler generations (samples/_history/) are present to inspect and permanently remove their audio files from disk.
    • FLAC ALL PRINTS, MP3 ALL PRINTS, AUTO-FLAC ON UPLOAD & AUTO-MP3 ON UPLOAD: Batch-convert all uncompressed live stereo Prints across the Session to lossless 24-bit .flac or 320 kbps CBR .mp3 files, or automatically convert Prints to .flac and/or .mp3 whenever uploading to cloud storage.
    • Upload Session Full / Upload Session Mixes / CLOSE SESSION: Trigger a full or mixes-only cloud sync for the entire Session, or close the Session and return to the PROJECT browser modal (CMD/CTRL + O).
  • HISTORY Bar (Reversible Undo/Redo & Manual Snapshot Capture):
    • Every fader drag, EQ node move, phase alignment, marker edit, Pass promotion, and Take archive action is tracked as a reversible step in the Session's command history (Rev:13 | Undo:13 | Redo:0). Continuous knob or fader gestures automatically group into a single undo step when you release the mouse button.
    • Click UNDO (CMD/CTRL + Z) or REDO (CMD/CTRL + SHIFT + Z) to step backward or forward through your session adjustments.
    • Click SNAP MANUAL (CMD/CTRL + S) to capture an immediate point-in-time Console Snapshot (Section 7.3).

7.1.2 Switching, Starring, Renaming & Archiving Takes in the TAKES CATALOG#

The TAKES CATALOG table lists every Take recorded or split during the Session. You can filter the catalog using the search box (Search takes, tags...) or the filter pills: ACTIVE (default, showing non-archived Takes), ALL + ARCHIVED (showing both active Takes and archived Takes), OVERDUBS (showing only Takes that contain Rec002-OD overdub passes), and UNSYNCED (showing Takes with local changes not yet uploaded to Google Drive).

Every row in TAKES CATALOG uses a clean, predictable 4-button action cluster ([Load], [Rename], [Export…], [⋯]):

Column / Action Operation
Favorite Star (★) Click the star icon on the far left of any row to mark a keeper Take. Starring a Take lets bandmates and engineers spot the best performance of a song at a glance.
Active Take Badge (ACT Take 001) & [Load] Highlights the Take currently loaded into MIXER and TIMELINE. Click Load on any row (or use < / > beside TAKE 001 in the Top Deck, ALT + [ / ALT + ]) to switch the active Take.
FOLDER / STAMP / TAG Shows the on-disk Take folder name (Take001_1430), capture timestamp (Stamp:1430), and optional song tag (Tag:none or Tag:SongA).
COUNTS Summarizes the audio assets inside the Take: multitrack stems (Stems:4), recording passes (Rec:2), rendered offline mixdowns (Mix:0), live stereo prints (Prt:0), and stem bounces (Bnc:0), plus total disk footprint.
RECORD OFFSET & RE-APPLY MEASURED OFFSET Displays the roundtrip latency offset applied to overdub passes in that Take (Offset: -640 smp (-13.33 ms)). If you recalibrate hardware loopback latency in AUDIO SETTINGS (CMD/CTRL + ,), clicking RE-APPLY MEASURED OFFSET in the catalog header updates the alignment offset on the active Take.
[Rename] (or inline click on Take Title) Renames the Take's song title inline, updates its alphanumeric <TakeTag> (for example, changing Take001_1947 to Take001_1947_MidnightDrive), and records rehearsal or mix notes.
[Export…] Menu Consolidates all outbound Take workflows in one place: Convert Print to FLAC / MP3, external workstation project formats (.rpp, .als, Session XML, .dawproject, .fcpxml, BWF Bundle), Stem Bounces, and Split-Screen Video Mixdown (.mp4) rendering.
[⋯] Overflow Menu (Upload, Convert Retro Take, Archive… / Restore) Houses per-Take Upload Full, Upload Mixes, Convert Retro Take (for Takes captured via SAVE RETRO, SHIFT + R), and crimson Archive… (marks an unwanted false-start Take as ARCHIVED, hiding it from ACTIVE without re-downloading it during cloud sync, and reversible via Undo or Restore in ALL + ARCHIVED).
Empty Trash… (CONFIRM EMPTY TRASH) When one or more Takes have been archived (or archived Studio Sampler bounce generations exist in samples/_history/), a crimson Empty Trash… button appears in the header showing the exact byte count to be reclaimed. Clicking Empty Trash… opens a confirmation banner listing the exact Take folders and archived sample files to be removed from disk. Click CONFIRM EMPTY TRASH to permanently delete those audio files from your drive, or CANCEL EMPTY TRASH to keep them.

7.2 Live Stereo Prints vs. Offline Mixdowns & Stem Bounces#

Cave Recorder provides four distinct stereo, multitrack, and external project interchange workflows so you can share rough rehearsal recordings with the band in seconds, export studio-grade stems for external mastering, or hand off complete multitrack project files to an external mixing or video editing suite.

7.2.1 Comparison of Export & Bounce Outputs#

Output Type Capture Mode Signal Path & Destination Studio Use Case
1. Live Stereo Print (Print<NNN>) Real-time during every Take. Convert to .flac or .mp3 via FLAC PRINT <NNN>, MP3 PRINT <NNN>, FLAC ALL PRINTS, or MP3 ALL PRINTS. Live post-Master-Bus stereo mix saved to <TakeFolder>/mix/ and linked into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/. Instant post-rehearsal listening on phones, web browsers, or band group chats without waiting for an offline render.
2. Offline Stereo Mixdown (Mix<NNN>) Faster-than-realtime offline render (triggered via the Master Bus FLAC, MP3, and BOUNCE controls). Full Mix Console signal path (trims, phase delays, active Pass Lanes, 8-slot inserts, EQ, VCA compression, Subgroup/Aux buses, Master limiter) saved to <TakeFolder>/mix/ and linked into _Mixes/. Sharing polished stereo mixes in 24-bit FLAC or 320 kbps CBR MP3 after refining faders, EQ, dynamics, or overdub comps.
3. Offline Stem Bounce (Bounce<NNN>) Faster-than-realtime offline multi-stem render. Individual post-DSP Track channels (<CC>-<TrackName>) and/or Subgroup Buses (Bus<BB>-<BusName>) rendered from 00:00:00.000 into <TakeFolder>/bounce/. Delivering phase-aligned, delay-compensated instrument or bus stems (WAV or FLAC) for external remixing or mastering.
4. Multi-Camera Split-Screen Video Mixdown (VideoMix<NNN>.mp4) Offline hardware-accelerated multi-camera video + console audio render. Multi-camera split-screen compositor (Single, Side-by-Side Crop, Side-by-Side 16:9, 3-Cam Band, Quad 2x2) paired with console-mixed 48.0 kHz stereo AAC-LC audio saved to <TakeFolder>/mix/ and linked into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/. Sharing complete multi-angle band performance videos with studio-mixed console audio immediately after rehearsal.
5. External Project, .fcpxml v1.9 Multicam & Bundle Export (EXPORT TAKE) Instant project interchange, multicam video timeline, or stem bundle export from the SESSION REEL or Export modal. Generates .rpp project files, .als Live Set project archives, <Session version="7003"> XML session folders, .dawproject open interchange archives, .fcpxml v1.9 Final Cut XML timelines (both stacked split-screen and native <mc-clip> multicam), or universal BWF/iXML/MIDI/IR stem bundles in <TakeFolder>/export/ (linked into <ProjectTag>/_Exports/). Handing off a Take (with faders, pans, polarity, phase delays, Pass Lanes, markers, calibrated multi-camera video angles, and optional .nam neural amp models) to an external mixing or video post-production workstation.

7.2.2 Converting Live Stereo Prints to Lossless FLAC (FLAC PRINT) & 320 kbps MP3 (MP3 PRINT)#

While you are tracking a Take, Cave Recorder writes the live 2-track Master Bus print as an uncompressed .wav file (Print001_<Stamp>.wav) with automatic Plugin Delay Compensation (PDC) latency trimming so the audio engine expends zero processor time on compression during live recording. Once the transport stops:

  1. Convert a Single Take's Print: In the SESSION REEL view (CMD/CTRL + 4), click FLAC PRINT 001 (for a lossless 24-bit .flac file) or MP3 PRINT 001 (for a 320 kbps CBR .mp3 file with a Xing/Info seek header for instant web-player scrubbing) in the ACTIONS column of that Take row.
  2. Convert All Prints in the Session: Click FLAC ALL PRINTS or MP3 ALL PRINTS in the Session Reel header bar to convert every unconverted .wav Print across all active Takes in one batch.
  3. Safe Write & Project _Mixes/ Linking: Cave Recorder encodes the 24-bit .flac counterpart (50-60% smaller than the source .wav file) or 320 kbps CBR .mp3 counterpart in the background before finalizing the file on disk. If local disk space ever runs out during encoding, any incomplete file is removed immediately so corrupt files never appear on disk. Once converted, the FLAC PRINT 001 or MP3 PRINT 001 button illuminates in its active state and Cave Recorder automatically places a relative link to the converted file inside the top-level <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/ folder.

7.2.3 Rendering Offline Stereo Mixdowns & Stem Bounces#

After you refine channel EQ, VCA compression, multi-mic phase alignment (Chapter 5: Built-In Processors, Phase Alignment & External Plugins (CLAP & AU)), or overdub Pass selections (Chapter 6: Waveform Timeline, Pass Lanes, Markers & Ranges), you can render an updated stereo Mixdown (Mix<NNN>) or multitrack Stem Bounce (Bounce<NNN>) faster than real time:

  1. Load and Verify the Take: Load the target Take into the console (LOAD TAKE <NNN>) and verify your mute, solo, active Pass Lane, and Master Bus limiter settings.
  2. Render an Offline Stereo Mixdown (Mix<NNN>): On the Master Bus strip (Chapter 4: Mix Console, Signal Flow & Channel Strips), toggle FLAC (24-bit lossless .flac), MP3 (320 kbps CBR .mp3 with a Xing/Info seek header), or both simultaneously, and click BOUNCE. Cave Recorder processes the entire Take from 00:00:00.000 through the full console signal path, increments the sequential mix number (Mix001, Mix002, ...), writes the rendered file(s) into <TakeFolder>/mix/, and links them into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/. When both FLAC and MP3 are selected, a single BOUNCE click renders both files under the same Mix<MMM> number.
  3. Render Processed Track or Subgroup Stems (Bounce<NNN>): When exporting stems for an external mix or mastering session, Cave Recorder renders Individual Track Stems (01-Kick-In, 02-Snare-Top, ...) and/or Stereo Subgroup Bus Stems (Bus01-Drum-Bus, Bus02-Guitar-Bus, ...) into <TakeFolder>/bounce/ in WAV or FLAC. Every bounced stem starts at exact sample 0 (00:00:00.000) with full Plugin Delay Compensation applied so all stems line up sample-accurately when dragged into any external workstation.

7.2.4 Exporting Takes to External Workstation Project Formats (EXPORT TAKE)#

When an outside mixing engineer or video editor wants to open a recorded Take in an external digital audio workstation or non-linear video editor without rebuilding track names, fader balances, subgroup routing, or marker flags by hand, click EXPORT TAKE on any Take row in the SESSION REEL view (CMD/CTRL + 4).

Cave Recorder writes the selected interchange package into <TakeFolder>/export/ and automatically maintains a flat relative link inside the project-level <ProjectTag>/_Exports/ directory:

  • .rpp Project File (EXPORT TAKE -> .rpp): Writes a plain-text .rpp project file referencing the Take's audio stems with sample-accurate microsecond phase offsets, active and muted Pass Lanes, channel faders, stereo pans, polarity switches (Ø), Subgroup Bus folder routing, and timeline markers and loop ranges.
  • .als Live Set Project (EXPORT TAKE -> .als): Writes a gzip-compressed XML .als project file with AudioTrack lanes, sample-zero AudioClip entries (IsWarped=false so natural band tempo fluctuations remain untouched), linear mixer volume and pan values, Subgroup GroupTrack routing, and Timeline locators.
  • Open-Source Workstation Session XML (EXPORT TAKE -> Session XML 7003): Generates a complete <Session version="7003"> XML directory structure with Sources, Regions, Playlists, Route strips, GainControl faders, Pannable stereo positions, Subgroup Buses, and Locations markers.
  • .dawproject Open Interchange Archive (EXPORT TAKE -> .dawproject): Packages a standard ZIP container (project.xml + metadata.xml + optional audio stems) preserving tracks, channel gains, pans, Subgroup Bus routing, Pass clips, and timeline markers for any workstation supporting the open .dawproject specification.
  • .fcpxml v1.9 Video Timeline XML (EXPORT TAKE -> .fcpxml): Writes a Final Cut XML v1.9 timeline (<fcpxml version="1.9">) with <asset-clip> audio lanes tagged by track role (dialogue.<TrackName>), rational frame-aligned sample timing, decibel volume adjustments, and chapter markers for immediate sync with multi-camera rehearsal or live-session video footage.
  • Universal BWF / iXML / MIDI / IR Stem Bundle (EXPORT TAKE -> BWF Bundle): Exports Broadcast Wave (bext + <BWFXML> iXML track and pass metadata) audio stems paired with a Type 1 Standard MIDI File (_markers.mid carrying marker cues and tempo map metadata), a README_SESSION_NOTES.txt console sheet, and 24-bit 48 kHz minimum-phase impulse response .wav files capturing each channel's 5-stage Phase Alignment Network + 12-Band static EQ curve so any workstation can reproduce Cave Recorder's exact phase and tonal alignment via a standard convolution loader.

When exporting a Take, you can choose Zero-Copy Relative References (which links directly to your existing rec/*.wav stems on disk in milliseconds with zero duplicated audio data) or Self-Contained Copy / Render (which copies or renders stems alongside any active .nam neural amplifier models into the export package for portable delivery on an external drive).

7.2.5 Rendering Multi-Camera Split-Screen .mp4 Video Mixdowns & .fcpxml v1.9 Multicam Timelines#

When a Take contains one or more recorded studio or wireless Cave Companion camera angles in <TakeFolder>/video/, open the Export Video Mixdown & Multicam FCPXML modal from any of four convenient entry points: per-Take EXPORT TAKE or VIDEO MIXDOWN (.MP4) in the TAKES CATALOG, the Session Reel header EXPORT VIDEO & MULTICAM button (CMD/CTRL + 4), or VIDEO MIXDOWN / FCP inside CAM SYNC:

  1. Choose a Split-Screen Compositor Layout: Cave Recorder composites up to four camera angles directly in BT.709 color space at 1080p50 (1920×1080 @ 50 FPS) or 1080p25 (25 FPS) with 2 px dark studio dividers:
    • Single (Full-Frame 16:9): Renders a single selected camera angle across the full 1920×1080 frame.
    • Side-by-Side Crop (2-Camera Vertical 8:9 Split with Horizontal Pan): Places Camera 1 on the left half (960×1080) and Camera 2 on the right half (960×1080), with independent Horizontal Camera Pan (-100% to +100%) sliders so you can center each musician cleanly within their vertical half-frame.
    • Side-by-Side 16:9 (2-Camera Letterboxed 16:9 Split): Displays two full-width 16:9 camera frames side by side (960×540 each) with zero cropping.
    • 3-Cam Band (3-Camera Triptych / Band Layout): Combines a wide or featured upper/left hero angle with two companion bandmate panes and per-pane crop/pan framing.
    • Quad 2x2 (4-Camera 2×2 Studio Grid): Displays four synchronized 960×540 16:9 quadrants (Cam 1 Top-Left, Cam 2 Top-Right, Cam 3 Bottom-Left, Cam 4 Bottom-Right).
  2. Offline Split-Screen .mp4 Mixdown Engine (960/1920-Sample Video Cadence to 1024-Sample AAC-LC Bridge):
    • Clicking RENDER VIDEO MIXDOWN (.MP4) runs asynchronously in the background without blocking console playback or editing, processing the Take from 00:00:00.000 through the full Mix Console audio engine while decoding and compositing every calibrated camera stream using its .vididx calibrated latency and clip trim offset.
    • Because 50 FPS (960 samples/frame), 25 FPS (1,920 samples/frame), 30 FPS (1,600 samples/frame), and 60 FPS (800 samples/frame) video cadences differ from the 1024-sample frame size required by hardware AAC-LC audio encoders, Cave Recorder bridges the 48.0 kHz stereo console bus through an exact sample-accurate accumulator into the hardware H.264 + AAC-LC (320 kbps) .mp4 muxer alongside gapless 48.0 kHz .flac and .mp3 post-take audio prints.
    • Once rendered, clicking COMMIT EXPORT reuses the finished render instantaneously with zero re-encoding, saving it to <TakeFolder>/mix/<SessionID>_Take<NNN>_VideoMix<MMM>_<Stamp>.mp4 and linking it into <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/ for instant local playback, LAN companion streaming, or Google Drive sharing.
  3. Dual-Mode .fcpxml v1.9 Video Timeline Export (Stacked Split-Screen & Native <mc-clip> Multicam):
    • Clicking EXPORT MULTICAM FCPXML (.FCPXML) generates a Final Cut XML v1.9 package in <TakeFolder>/export/ supporting two non-linear editing workflows:
    • Stacked Split-Screen Spine (<adjust-crop> & <adjust-transform>): Translates your selected Cave Recorder split-screen layout (Side-by-Side Crop, 3-Cam Band, Quad 2x2) directly into stacked <asset-clip> video lanes with exact rational <adjust-crop>, <adjust-transform> pan/scale coordinates, and <timeMap> clock-drift tables derived from each camera's .vididx index.
    • Native <mc-clip> Multi-Camera Switching Angle Assembly: Builds a standard Final Cut <mc-clip> multicam resource combining all calibrated camera angles (<mc-angle>) and post-trim audio stems so a video editor can cut live between camera angles on the timeline with zero manual clap-syncing.

7.3 Non-Destructive Console Snapshots & Live Mix (SNAPS)#

A Console Snapshot (Snap 001, Snap 002, ...) is a complete, point-in-time capture of your entire mixing console and timeline comp state stored as a compact JSON file inside <SessionFolder>/snapshots/. Because Snapshots reference your existing audio stems rather than duplicating .wav files on disk, you can save dozens of mix variations per Session with near-zero disk footprint.

7.3.1 What a Snapshot Captures & Automatic Snapshot Policies#

Every Snapshot records:

  • All input channel strip parameters (input trim, 180-degree polarity invert, microsecond acoustic phase delay, reorderable 8-slot processing rack order, 12-band Parametric EQ nodes, VCA Compressor settings, Tape Saturation, CLAP plugin states, Aux send levels and tap points, pan, fader gain, mute, solo, and output bus routing).
  • All stereo Subgroup Bus (SUB 1..16), Aux Return (AUX 1 Convolution Reverb, AUX 2 Stereo Tape Delay), and Master Bus parameters.
  • Active Pass Lane selections (PASS 01, OD 02, ...) and per-pass mute states across every Take in the Session.
  • The complete compact Undo/Redo history stack at that moment in time, so restoring a Snapshot also restores its undo timeline.

Snapshots are created in three ways and can be filtered in the SNAPSHOTS table at the bottom of the SESSION REEL view using the ALL, MANUAL, and AUTO pills:

  1. Manual Snapshot ([MANUAL]): Click SNAP MANUAL in the Session Reel history bar or press CMD/CTRL + S from any view to save a named milestone (for example, Manual Snapshot 04 or Pre-Vocal-Overdub Balance).
  2. Post-Recording Auto-Save ([POST-REC]): Automatically captured immediately after every normal recording stop (Auto-Save (Post-Recording)), preserving the exact monitor mix and Pass state that was active when the band finished the Take. (If you abort a false start using the clean-restart discard stop command, the post-recording auto-save is suppressed.)
  3. Periodic 20-Minute Auto-Save ([AUTO]): Automatically captured every 20 minutes while a Session is open, provided at least one console or timeline action has occurred since the last saved Snapshot.

7.3.2 Auditioning Historical Snapshots with Live Mix Protection#

In traditional mixing consoles, loading an old scene or snapshot overwrites your current unsaved fader moves unless you remember to save a temporary file first. Cave Recorder eliminates this hazard by automatically preserving your Live Mix:

  1. Click AUDITION SNAP <NNN> to Enter Audition Mode: The moment you click AUDITION SNAP 001 on any row in the SNAPSHOTS table while working on a live mix, Cave Recorder automatically saves your current unsaved working console state as your Live Mix in memory and illuminates the burgundy AUDITION MODE: SNAP 001 | VIEWING: HISTORICAL SNAPSHOT banner (see Figure 7.2).
  2. Click Through Multiple Historical Snapshots Freely: While in Audition Mode, you can click AUDITION SNAP 002, AUDITION SNAP 003, AUDITION SNAP 004, and so on across five or more historical Snapshots to compare balances. Your original working Live Mix remains safely preserved in memory the entire time.
  3. Instant Zero-Latency Comparison (A/B LIVE MIX): Click A/B LIVE MIX in the Audition Mode banner to toggle directly between the historical Snapshot and your preserved Live Mix while audio is playing. All fader, EQ, and dynamics changes transition via sample-accurate smoothing ramps (5 to 10 ms) without audio clicks.
  4. Restore Your Working Mix (RETURN TO LIVE MIX or BACKSPACE): Click RETURN TO LIVE MIX in the Audition Mode banner (or press BACKSPACE while in the SESSION REEL view) to exit Audition Mode and restore your exact working console state with zero lost fader or EQ moves.
  5. Adopt the Historical Snapshot (LOAD SNAPSHOT): If you decide you prefer the historical Snapshot over your previous working state, click LOAD SNAPSHOT to promote that Snapshot as your active live session mix.
Zero Lost Fader Moves During Snapshot Comparison

You never need to manually save a throwaway snapshot before checking how the mix sounded an hour ago. Live Mix protection engages automatically on the first AUDITION SNAP click and guards your working console balance until you explicitly click RETURN TO LIVE MIX (BACKSPACE) or LOAD SNAPSHOT.

7.4 Self-Documenting Disk Folder Structure & File Naming Rules#

Cave Recorder stores all Projects, Sessions, Takes, Passes, Prints, Mixdowns, Stem Bounces, and Snapshots in an open, human-readable directory hierarchy on your drive (defaulting to ~/Music/caverec/ on macOS and Linux, and %USERPROFILE%\Music\caverec\ on Windows). Every folder and audio filename states which Project, Session, Take, Channel, and Pass it belongs to, so any engineer can open the folder in macOS Finder, Windows Explorer, Linux file managers, or any external audio editor ten years from now with zero proprietary database lock-in.

7.4.1 Complete Project & Session Directory Tree on Disk#

Conceptual studio hierarchy (Project -> Session -> Take -> Pass / Prints / Mixdowns / Snapshots):

ProjectName/
└── SessionName/
    ├── session.json
    ├── Snapshots/
    ├── Mixdowns/
    ├── Prints/
    │   └── Take001_LiveMix.flac
    └── Takes/
        └── Take001_SongName/
            ├── Pass001_Base/
            │   └── Ch01_Kick.wav
            └── Pass002_Overdub/
                └── Ch09_LeadGtr.wav

On disk inside your Cave Recorder Library Root (~/Music/caverec/), this hierarchy is organized on disk using self-identifying prefixed filenames and a project-wide _Mixes/ index folder:

~/Music/caverec/                         # Library Root folder
├── .caverec/
│   ├── projects.json                    # Local Project registry
│   ├── drive_sync_state.json            # Cloud sync state ledger
│   ├── sampler_library/                 # Deduplicated external WAV imports
│   └── templates/
│       ├── MicAndGuitar001.json         # Default 2-ch session template
│       ├── GuitarBassDrumTrio001.json   # 11-ch band session template
│       ├── XR18Base001.json             # 17-track stagebox flat template
│       └── Empty.json                   # Blank 0-track starter template
├── GF/                                  # Project ("Grottfolk")
│   ├── .caverec_project.json            # Cloud Project index
│   ├── _Mixes/                          # Flat links to Mix* & Print*
│   │   ├── GF_20261015-2_Take001_Print001_1947.flac
│   │   ├── GF_20261015-2_Take001_Print001_1947.mp3
│   │   ├── GF_20261015-2_Take001_Mix001_2315.flac
│   │   └── GF_20261015-2_Take001_Mix001_2315.mp3
│   ├── _Exports/                        # Flat links to EXPORT TAKE packages
│   └── GF_20261015-2_Jam/               # Session folder (tag "Jam")
│       ├── GF_20261015-2_session.json   # Console & marker manifest
│       ├── stagebox_scene.json          # Portable Stagebox hardware scene
│       ├── models/                      # Self-contained .nam neural models
│       ├── samples/                     # Active latest v<VV> Studio Sampler WAVs
│       │   ├── GF_20261015-2_Smp001_Take001-Guitar1_v02_2145.wav
│       │   └── _history/                # Prior bounce versions & soft-deleted WAVs
│       │       └── GF_20261015-2_Smp001_Take001-Guitar1_v01_2140.wav
│       ├── snapshots/                   # Saved Console Snapshots
│       │   └── GF_20261015-2_001_2026-10-15_19-34-12.json
│       ├── Take001_1947_Improv/         # Take 001 folder
│       └── Take002_0015_SongB/          # Late-night Take (same day)
└── MISC/                                # Built-in default project
    └── _Mixes/
