7.4.2 Canonical File & Folder Naming Reference#

Every file created by Cave Recorder follows consistent, predictable naming rules so files sort chronologically and never collide when dragged into an external folder or shared across operating systems:

Item Naming Pattern Concrete Example
Project Tag & Folder 1 to 8 uppercase letters or digits (A-Z, 0-9) GF, INSOF, MISC
Project _Mixes/ Folder <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/ (relative links to active Mix*, Print*, and VideoMix* .flac/.mp3/.wav/.mp4 files) GF/_Mixes/GF_20261015-2_Take001_Print001_1947.flac
Project _Exports/ Folder <ProjectTag>/_Exports/ (relative links to exported external workstation packages) GF/_Exports/GF_20261015-2_Take001.rpp
Session ID (Permanent) <PROJECT_TAG>_<YYYYMMDD> (plus -2, -3, ... for additional sessions on the same session day) GF_20261015, GF_20261015-2
Session Folder <ProjectTag>/<SessionID>[_<SessionTag>] GF/GF_20261015-2_Jam
Take Folder Take<NNN>_<Stamp>[_<TakeTag>] Take001_1947_Improv
Base Pass Stem (rec/) <SessionID>_Take<NNN>_<CC>-<TrackName>_Rec001_<Stamp>.wav GF_20261015-2_Take001_01-Kick-In_Rec001_1947.wav
Overdub Pass Stem (rec/) <SessionID>_Take<NNN>_<CC>-<TrackName>_Rec<MMM>-OD_<Stamp>.wav GF_20261015-2_Take001_09-LeadGtr_Rec002-OD_2210.wav
Camera Video & Index (video/) <SessionID>_Take<NNN>_Cam<CC>-<CamName>_<Stamp>.<mp4|vididx> GF_20261015-2_Take001_Cam01-Drums_1947.mp4
Live Stereo Print (mix/) <SessionID>_Take<NNN>_Print<NNN>_<Stamp>.wav / .flac / .mp3 GF_20261015-2_Take001_Print001_1947.flac
Offline Mixdown (mix/) <SessionID>_Take<NNN>_Mix<NNN>_<Stamp>.flac / .mp3 / .wav GF_20261015-2_Take001_Mix001_2315.flac
Split-Screen Video Mix (mix/) <SessionID>_Take<NNN>_VideoMix<NNN>_<Stamp>.mp4 GF_20261015-2_Take001_VideoMix001_2320.mp4
Track Stem Bounce (bounce/) <SessionID>_Take<NNN>_<CC>-<TrackName>_Bounce<NNN>_<Stamp>.wav / .flac GF_20261015-2_Take001_09-LeadGtr_Bounce001_2315.wav
Subgroup Stem Bounce (bounce/) <SessionID>_Take<NNN>_Bus<BB>-<BusName>_Bounce<NNN>_<Stamp>.wav / .flac GF_20261015-2_Take001_Bus01-Drum-Bus_Bounce001_2315.wav
External Take Export (export/) <TakeFolder>/export/<SessionID>_Take<NNN>.<rpp|als|dawproject|fcpxml> Take001_1947_Improv/export/GF_20261015-2_Take001.rpp
Neural Amp Model (models/) <SessionFolder>/models/<ModelName>_<ShortHash>.nam GF_20261015-2_Jam/models/StudioCrunch_a1b2c3d4.nam
Studio Sampler WAV (samples/) <SessionID>_Smp<NNN>_<Label>_v<VV>_<Stamp>.wav (archived prior generations in samples/_history/) GF_20261015-2_Smp001_Take001-Guitar1_v02_2145.wav
Stagebox Scene (stagebox_scene.json) <SessionFolder>/stagebox_scene.json GF_20261015-2_Jam/stagebox_scene.json
Console Snapshot (snapshots/) <SessionID>_<NNN>_<YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS>.json GF_20261015-2_001_2026-10-15_19-34-12.json

Key studio rules governing disk files:

  • 08:00 Local Time Session-Day Rollover: A studio session day runs from 08:00 to 07:59 local time the following morning. If your band starts rehearsing on October 15 at 21:00 and records a Take after midnight at 01:30 on October 16, that late-night recording still belongs to session date 20261015 and receives a four-digit <Stamp> (0130). If you open the same Session four days later on October 19 to record a guitar overdub, <Stamp> automatically expands to include the calendar date (20261019-1922).
  • Permanent File IDs vs. Editable Folder Tags: The <SessionID>, Take numbers (Take001, Take002), Pass numbers (Rec001, Rec002-OD), and timestamps are assigned once at creation and never change, and numbers are never reused after a deletion. Editable tags (<SessionTag> like Jam and <TakeTag> like Improv) appear only in folder names, never inside .wav or .flac filenames. As a result, you can rename song tags and display titles freely at any time without breaking file references or re-uploading gigabytes of audio to the cloud.
  • Broadcast Wave (bext) Headers & Sample-Zero Alignment: Every .wav stem is written with standard Broadcast Wave (bext) metadata embedding the wall-clock origin timecode while aligning the start of the Take to sample 0 (00:00:00.000).

7.5 Band Collaboration & Google Drive Cloud Sync (CLOUD)#

Cave Recorder includes built-in two-way Google Drive Cloud Sync designed specifically for bands and production teams. Bandmates can pull lightweight stereo .flac and .mp3 Prints, Mixdowns, and Console Snapshots to their laptops or stream .mp3 files directly in the Google Drive web player immediately after rehearsal, while selectively downloading multi-gigabyte raw multitrack stems only for the Takes they want to remix or overdub at home.

7.5.1 Connecting a Project to Google Drive & Reading the CLOUD Badge#

  1. Authenticate with Google Drive: Click PROJECT in the Top Deck (CMD/CTRL + O) to open the Project & Session Browser modal (or click the CLOUD: IDLE status badge in the Top Deck). In the top Cloud Folder row, click Check / Connect Drive. When a Google OAuth Client ID is configured, Cave Recorder launches your default web browser for the Google account sign-in flow and stores your refresh credentials inside your operating system's user configuration folder. If no OAuth Client ID is configured yet on your workstation, Cave Recorder displays DRIVE: OAUTH NOT CONFIGURED with inline setup guidance for placing gdrive_oauth_client.json in your Cave Recorder configuration directory (~/Library/Application Support/caverec/ on macOS, ~/.config/caverec/ on Linux, or %APPDATA%\caverec\ on Windows) or setting the CAVEREC_GDRIVE_CLIENT_ID environment variable.
  2. Monitor the Top Deck CLOUD Status Pill:
    • CLOUD: IDLE: Connected and ready, with no transfer currently running.
    • CLOUD: SYNCING: Actively uploading or downloading session manifests, mixes, or stems in the background.
    • CLOUD: SYNCED: All local Session changes match the remote Google Drive project index.
  3. Automatic Real-Time Recording Guard: If a background cloud upload or download is running when you press Record (R) on the transport bar, Cave Recorder automatically pauses and terminates the background transfer immediately so disk and network activity never compete with live multitrack audio capture.

7.5.2 Selective Sync Tiers: MIXES vs. FULL, AUTO-FLAC ON UPLOAD & AUTO-MP3 ON UPLOAD#

Because an evening of 18-channel 48 kHz / 24-bit multitrack stems can total 10 to 30 GB while stereo .flac and .mp3 Prints and Console Snapshots take only a few megabytes, Cave Recorder supports two explicit transfer modes for both uploading and downloading:

Sync Tier Upload / Download Buttons What Is Transferred When to Use
Mixes & Metadata Only (MIXES) UPLOAD SES MIXES, UPLOAD MIXES <NNN>, Sync Library (Mixes), DOWNLOAD MIXES Session & Take JSON manifests, Markers & Ranges, Console Snapshots (snapshots/), .flac/.mp3/.wav Live Prints and Mixdowns (mix/), Stem Bounces (bounce/), and <ProjectTag>/_Mixes/. Skips raw rec/ multitrack WAV stems. Right after rehearsal over studio Wi-Fi or mobile hotspot so bandmates can listen to every Take, stream .mp3 mixes in Google Drive, inspect markers, and audition mixes within seconds.
Full Multitrack Backup (FULL) UPLOAD SES FULL, UPLOAD FULL <NNN>, Sync Library (Full), DOWNLOAD FULL Everything in MIXES plus all raw multitrack Base Pass (Rec001) and Overdub Pass (Rec002-OD) .wav stems in rec/. Backing up the complete multitrack session to cloud storage, or pulling raw stems of a keeper Take (UPLOAD FULL 001 / DOWNLOAD FULL) to overdub or remix on another computer.
Automatic Print Conversion on Upload (AUTO-FLAC ON UPLOAD & AUTO-MP3 ON UPLOAD)

Both the SESSION REEL header bar and the Top Deck CLOUD popover provide independent AUTO-FLAC ON UPLOAD and AUTO-MP3 ON UPLOAD toggles (AUTO-FLAC ON UPLOAD is enabled by default). When enabled, clicking UPLOAD SES MIXES or UPLOAD MIXES <NNN> automatically converts any uncompressed Print<NNN>.wav files to 24-bit .flac and/or 320 kbps CBR .mp3 before uploading so bandmates get compact lossless files and browser-streamable MP3s without uploading huge uncompressed stereo WAV prints. If your local drive ever runs completely out of free space during pre-conversion, Cave Recorder presents a three-choice recovery banner (PROCEED WITHOUT FLAC PRINTS, UPLOAD PRINT.WAV INSTEAD, or CANCEL) so you can still back up your session safely.

7.5.3 Sharing a Project with Bandmates (+ Link Remote Project...)#

Each Project in Cave Recorder is an independent sync root, allowing you to keep personal projects in your own Google Drive while linking band projects hosted in a bandmate's Google Drive:

  1. Share the Project Folder: The bandmate who created the Project shares its <ProjectTag> folder in Google Drive with the band's Google accounts (or clicks COPY SHARE LINK in the PROJECT modal to copy a caverec:// project link to the clipboard).
  2. Link the Remote Project: On each bandmate's computer, open the PROJECT modal (CMD/CTRL + O) and click + Link Remote Project....
  3. Auto-Discovery or Link Paste: Cave Recorder automatically lists all Cave Recorder projects found in your Google Drive "Shared with me" view for one-click linking, or lets you paste a Google Drive folder URL or caverec:// share URI directly.
  4. Automatic Tag Collision Resolution: Because every Project in your local library must have a unique <ProjectTag>, if a linked remote project uses a tag (such as GF) that already exists on your machine, Cave Recorder prompts you with three clear choices:
    • RENAME LOCAL PROJECT TAG...: Re-tags your existing local project (for example, GF to GF2) to free GF for the shared band project.
    • MERGE SAME PROJECT (ADOPT REMOTE): Used when two bandmates independently created the GF project before linking, adopting the shared cloud project identity cleanly.
    • CANCEL: Aborts linking without changing local files.

7.5.4 Exclusive Session Write-Locking (Read-Only Preview) & Zero-Loss Conflict Merging#

When multiple bandmates collaborate on the same Session across different computers, Cave Recorder prevents accidental overwrites using Exclusive Session Write-Locking paired with Snapshot-Backed Conflict Merging:

  • Automatic Write Lock on Open & Release on Close:
    • When you open a Session while online, Cave Recorder acquires an exclusive edit lock for your computer and automatically pulls any newer cloud metadata if your local copy has no unsaved edits.
    • When you close the Session (CLOSE SESSION) or quit Cave Recorder while online, the edit lock is released automatically so another bandmate can open the Session for editing.
  • Opening a Session Locked by a Bandmate (Read-Only Preview Mode):
    • If a bandmate currently has the Session open on another computer, Cave Recorder alerts you and offers OPEN READ-ONLY PREVIEW (recommended), BREAK LOCK & TAKE WRITE ACCESS, or CANCEL.
    • In Read-Only Preview mode, an amber READ-ONLY (LOCKED BY <MACHINE>) badge appears in the header. You have full playback, timeline scrubbing, and live in-memory console mixing (faders, solos, 12-band EQ, VCA compression, and Snapshot auditioning), while transport Record / Overdub and background disk writes are disabled so you never conflict with your bandmate's live recording session.
    • If you dial in a great mix while in Read-Only Preview mode, click SAVE AS LOCAL SNAPSHOT in the header bar to preserve your mix settings locally, or click TAKE LOCK once your bandmate finishes.
  • Zero-Loss Merging of Offline Edits, Takes & Deletions:
    • Audio files in rec/, mix/, and bounce/ are never overwritten, and new recordings and bounces are always saved as new numbered files. Pulling a MIXES update onto the studio computer that holds the raw rec/ multitrack WAV stems adds new mixes and snapshots without ever deleting local multitrack stems.
    • Takes or Passes that were marked as deleted in the session history on one machine remain marked as deleted across syncs so purged false starts are never re-downloaded.
    • If two bandmates both edit a Session's mix while offline and later sync to Google Drive, Cave Recorder detects that both computers edited the Session while offline, combines all newly recorded Takes, Passes, Mixdowns, and Snapshots from both machines, and prompts you to choose either KEEP LOCAL MIX & SAVE CLOUD MIX AS SNAPSHOT or ADOPT CLOUD MIX & SAVE LOCAL MIX AS SNAPSHOT. The alternate mix is automatically saved into snapshots/ so zero fader or EQ work is ever lost, and you can immediately compare both bandmates' mixes side by side using Live Mix (Section 7.3.2).

7.5.5 Unified Google Drive Resumable Video/Print Sync & Cross-Device Deduplication#

When a Session includes multi-camera .mp4 + .vididx recordings alongside .flac and .mp3 audio prints, Cave Recorder coordinates desktop and Cave Companion mobile transfers through a unified Google Drive Resumable Sync pipeline:

  1. Automatic Cross-Device Deduplication: Every uploaded .mp4, .vididx, .flac, .mp3, and .wav asset is tagged in Google Drive metadata with its content fingerprint. If a mobile camera node has already transferred a 1080p50 .mp4 angle to the desktop workstation over studio Wi-Fi (or uploaded it directly from the phone), Google Drive confirms the matching file fingerprint so the second device never re-uploads the same multi-hundred-megabyte video file.
  2. Chunked Resumable Uploads: Large .mp4 video angles, split-screen VideoMix<NNN>.mp4 renders, and .wav/.flac stems upload via resumable upload sessions in 8 MB chunks. If a rehearsal basement Wi-Fi connection drops mid-upload, Cave Recorder automatically resumes from the last committed byte offset when connectivity returns.
  3. Verified Downloads, Non-Blocking Sync & Transactional Rollback: Downloads stream into a temporary .part staging file and finalize into place only after the integrity check passes. Project catalog loads, cloud manifest merges, and background transfers execute asynchronously off the 60 Hz interface thread on both Desktop and Cave Companion mobile, guarded against mid-sync session switches and backed by automatic transactional rollback if a network link or storage drive drops mid-transfer. When you pair a Cave Companion phone via the desktop pairing QR code, the project's Google Drive root folder link propagates automatically to the phone so mobile sign-in connects directly to the shared band project folder.

7.6 Cave Companion Mobile Ecosystem (Android .apk & iOS .ipa)#

The Cave Companion mobile application for Android (API 36 / 16 KB page-size compliant caverec-v0.7.1-android-arm64.apk) and iOS (caverec-v0.7.1-ios-arm64.ipa) turns every bandmate's phone or tablet into a low-latency Wireless TRANSPORT & 16-Channel Meter Bridge, a full Realtime Wireless Studio MIXER Console, a dedicated STAGEBOX (MY MONITOR personal IEM & PIN-lockable FULL MIXER) controller, a tactile wireless GROOVEBOX & SAMPLER remote, a sample-locked Wireless 1080p50 CFR Studio Camera Node, and an offline-capable Multi-Angle & Multi-Print Take PLAYER unified in Plain Studio Language and the universal [M] (Mute Amber) -> [S] (Solo Gold) -> [R] (Record Crimson) strip order across all viewports.

  • Responsive 8-Tab Tablet vs. 6-Tab Phone Navigation:
    • Tablets (>= 840 dp/pt): Bottom navigation displays all 8 root tabs: PAIR | TRANSPORT | MIXER | STAGEBOX | GROOVEBOX | CAMERA | TAKES | PLAYER (giving MIXER, STAGEBOX, and GROOVEBOX dedicated top-level buttons with zero redundant inner tab rows).
    • Phones (< 600 dp/pt min-dimension): Bottom navigation locks cleanly to 6 root tabs: PAIR | TRANSPORT | CONSOLE | CAMERA | TAKES | PLAYER, grouping [MIXER | GROOVEBOX | STAGEBOX] under CONSOLE with a single 48 dp top switcher so every target remains wide and thumb-reachable.

7.6.1 Desktop REMOTE Workspace (CMD/CTRL + 0), Bonjour Auto-Discovery, SAMPLE STUDIO SESSION & One-Tap Approval#

Click the ● REMOTE live status pill in Row 2 of the Top Deck (immediately right of ● STAGEBOX), or press CMD/CTRL + 0, to toggle the full-workspace Cave Companion view (clicking ● REMOTE, <- RETURN, or ESC returns immediately to your previous workspace tab).

  • Zero-Configuration Bonjour Wi-Fi Discovery (_caverec._udp): Desktop macOS automatically advertises _caverec._udp over local Wi-Fi alongside UDP LAN studio discovery. Both iOS and Android Cave Companion apps discover studio workstations automatically on the PAIR screen with zero manual IP entry (auto-filling single-host studios) and offer 1-tap PAIR ON WI-FI with a 6-digit MATCH CODE verified on the desktop global approval banner (PAIR REQUEST: "<Device>" (<IP>) MATCH CODE: NNN NNN).
  • Bundled SAMPLE STUDIO SESSION (UNPAIRED SAMPLE) for First-Launch Exploration (Including Full Offline STAGEBOX): Before pairing with a desktop studio, tapping SAMPLE STUDIO SESSION on the mobile PAIR screen loads genuine pre-rendered 48.0 kHz studio media (Take001 "Live Room Check" with .flac FullMix + .mp3 RhythmDry + 2-angle 50 FPS H.264 video, Take002 "Late Jam Groove", and a sliceable Sampler loop) through the real studio audio/video engine alongside a hydrated sample hardware mixer state. Musicians and evaluators can explore TRANSPORT, MIXER (32-channel band patch), STAGEBOX (fully populated MY MONITOR personal IEM bus sends and FULL MIXER FOH channel strips, PEQ, RTA, GEQ, and FX rack controls without live mixer hardware connected), GROOVEBOX + SAMPLER, CAMERA (25/50 FPS viewfinder), TAKES (tappable 1..5 stars and Rename…), and PLAYER (multi-angle playback and print switching). While active, an amber/copper UNPAIRED SAMPLE pill stays visible in the top bar. Tapping UNPAIRED SAMPLE, tapping EXIT SAMPLE SESSION on PAIR, or completing a live Wi-Fi pairing exits and purges the staged sample files cleanly.
  • Crisp Studio QR Code, Live QR Auto-Zoom, ENLARGE QR Lightbox & 6-Digit Studio PIN: Desktop displays a large integer-aligned QR code (ENLARGE QR opens a centered 456 x 456 studio-distance lightbox), a one-click COPY PAIRING URL button, REFRESH LAN IP, and the 6-digit numeric fallback PIN (ON COMPANION: <IP> | PIN <NNN NNN>). Every installation creates a unique persistent device identity, and ROTATE KEY / PIN rotates credentials cleanly.
  • Live Companion Table & Access Roles (FULL, CAM, VIEW, REVOKE): Lists every paired companion with live ONLINE (<rtt>) / OFFLINE / REVOKED telemetry and access role controls (Full Control + Camera, Camera + Player, Player & Meters Only, and Stagebox MY MONITOR vs. FULL MIXER permissions managed in STAGEBOX -> 4. SCENES & SETUP). Paired companions with camera capability register automatically inside ● CAMERA.

7.6.2 Wireless Studio Link & Zero-Scroll TRANSPORT Tab#

Cave Companion separates sub-millisecond studio telemetry and transport control from bulk .mp4 / .flac media transfers across two dedicated local Wi-Fi channels, anchored by the zero-scroll TRANSPORT root tab (REC, PLAY/PAUSE, STOP, ⏮ START, NEW TAKE, 16-channel 40-segment LED meter bridge, 60 Hz interactive scrub ruler, and a guarded two-step Discard Recording? modal so a stray tap never wipes a Take):

Studio Channel Capability Cadence & Protection Studio Function
Real-Time Studio Control Link Sub-Millisecond Clock Lock Continuous drift-compensated clock synchronization (Locking Clock… -> CLOCK LOCKED) Maps the companion device's camera and player clock directly onto the desktop audio interface's 48.0 kHz sample timeline (< 0.5 ms lock).
Real-Time Studio Control Link Remote Transport Commands Authenticated studio session commands Triggers Play/Pause, Stop, START, Record, Overdub, SAVE RETRO, NEW TAKE, Take switching, safe two-step Discard Recording?, and live Marker drops (M) from behind the drum kit or amp stack.
Real-Time Studio Control Link Remote Timeline Scrubbing 60 Hz smooth playhead scrubbing Lets a musician scrub the desktop Timeline smoothly by dragging across the mobile timeline ruler.
Real-Time Studio Control Link Live Console Telemetry & Meters 25 Hz / 50 Hz broadcast from desktop to paired companions Streams active Take timecode, transport state (PLAY, REC, OVERDUB), and 16-channel Peak/RMS + 40-segment Master Bus LED meter levels.
High-Speed Media Transfer Link Manifest, Video & Audio Sync Authenticated transfer with automatic .part resume and file integrity verification Transfers session/take manifests, sends wireless 1080p50 .mp4 + .vididx camera recordings to <TakeFolder>/video/, and downloads .mp3, .flac, and VideoMix<NNN>.mp4 files to paired companions at full Wi-Fi speed.

7.6.3 Wireless 1080p50 CFR Mobile CAMERA Node & Direct Wireless-Clock Rear Torch Calibration#

Switching to the CAMERA tab inside the Cave Companion app configures the companion device's hardware camera and H.264/HEVC encoder as a sample-locked wireless studio camera (Standby -> CAMERA ARMED • AUTO-REC WITH DAW):

  1. Lens & Constant Frame Rate (CFR) Selector Pills: Pick your preferred physical lens (ULTRA-WIDE, WIDE, TELEPHOTO, or FRONT) and exact frame rate (24, 25, 30, 50, or 60 FPS). Default 1080p50 CFR locks sensor exposure duration and frame delivery to an exact 50 FPS (20.000 ms / 960 audio samples per frame at 48.0 kHz) with zero B-frames and 0.5 s closed GOP keyframes, stamping every frame's presentation timestamp into a local .vididx sidecar locked to the desktop audio clock.
  2. DAW-Coupled Arming & Live Studio HUD: Arming the mobile camera illuminates CAMERA ARMED • AUTO-REC WITH DAW so the phone or tablet starts and stops recording automatically in lockstep with the desktop transport (with AUTO-PUSH ON STOP enabled for hands-free upload). Devices with Full Control can also tap RECORD DAW TAKE and STOP TAKE & SYNC directly from the Camera HUD alongside the green CLOCK LOCKED (±0.2 ms) badge, 16-channel mini-meters, and crimson Recording Tally Border.
  3. Collapsible FLASH SYNC ▾ (OPTICAL FLASH SYNC CALIBRATION) Drawer: Expanding FLASH SYNC ▾ and tapping TRIGGER 4-PULSE REAR TORCH CALIBRATION fires the companion device's rear LED Torch in a 4-pulse optical sequence and measures the camera sensor's rolling-shutter and encoder latency directly against wireless studio-clock timestamps with no phone speaker or microphone audio loop, combining automatically with the desktop studio calibration offset.
  4. Automatic Wi-Fi Camera Transfer & Desktop Timeline Auto-Ingest: The instant recording stops, the companion finalizes its .mp4 and .vididx files and automatically transfers both over studio Wi-Fi into the desktop workstation's <TakeFolder>/video/ folder. As soon as the verified transfer completes, the desktop workstation automatically attaches the mobile camera angle to the active Take and renders its stacked Video Timeline Strip time-anchored thumbnail filmstrip on TIMELINE (CMD/CTRL + 1).

7.6.4 Split TAKES & PLAYER Root Tabs, Multi-Angle Playback & Mobile Storage Quota Tiering#

Cave Companion separates Take browsing (TAKES tab, with tappable 1..5 favorite stars, Rename…, Download, and Remove Local Video controls) from dedicated playback (PLAYER tab, featuring a 2-pane landscape layout on tablets with the video monitor and transport alongside the angle/print list) so bandmates can review every recorded Take either in the studio over local Wi-Fi or on the road via Google Drive Cloud Sync:

  • Instant Multi-Angle & Multi-Print Switching: While a Take is playing in PLAYER, tap any camera angle pill (Cam01-Drums, Cam02-GtrMobile, Split-Screen Mix) or switch audio sources on the fly between the Live Stereo Print (Print001.mp3 / .flac) and subsequent Offline Mixdowns (Mix001.flac, Mix002.flac). Continuous drift-free audio/video synchronization keeps video frame presentation locked to the active audio print with zero timeline restart.
  • Smart Mobile Storage Quota Cache Tiering: To prevent multi-gigabyte 1080p50 camera files from filling up a bandmate's device storage, Cave Companion enforces a three-tier local cache policy (Pinned Offline .mp3 Prints & Manifests, On-Demand .flac & .mp4 within a 2 GB to 16 GB ceiling with manual Remove Local Video per Take, and automatic camera outbox cleanup once desktop or cloud transfer is verified).

7.6.5 Realtime Wireless MIXER & STAGEBOX (MY MONITOR vs. FULL MIXER & MIXER LOCK)#

  1. Wireless DAW MIXER (MIXER on Tablets, CONSOLE -> MIXER on Phones):
    • Synchronizes live with desktop MIXER at 50 Hz (SYNCING CONSOLE… until initial state arrives), providing full transport (START, PLAY/PAUSE, STOP, REC), 12-CH VIEW / 18-CH VIEW tablet density toggle, quick Snapshots, Android FULL immersive taskbar toggle, layer banking (ALL 18, CH 1-8, CH 9-16, AUX, BUS), pinned Master strip (MAIN, DIM, MONO, CLR S, CLR !), SENDS ON FADERS (tablet) / BUS SENDS (phone) with 4x FINE clutch, geared zero-jump relative touch faders (2-finger 4x fine clutch, double-tap unity, inline numeric keypad), universal [M] (Mute Amber) / [S] (Solo Gold) / [R] (Record Crimson) strip controls, and the docked Focus Strip (HW GAIN, TRIM, 600 ms hold 48V, Ø, HPF, PAN, 4-Band PEQ with two-finger pinch Q, and VCA/FET/Opto compressor).
  2. Wireless Hardware STAGEBOX (STAGEBOX on Tablets, CONSOLE -> STAGEBOX on Phones):
    • Enforces server-side cryptographic role permissions so musicians and engineers can share the same stagebox safely:
    • MY MONITOR (Personal Musician IEM / Wedge View): Pins the musician's device to their assigned monitor bus (BUS 1..6), offering channel contribution faders, a continuous MORE ME slider, an AUX USB playback/click spotlight fader, and MY BUS MASTER with zero exposure to +48V phantom power, Main PA faders, or hardware routing.
    • FULL MIXER (Engineer FOH View Behind MIXER LOCK): Protected by MIXER LOCK (0.6 s hold to claim / Release Mixer Lock pill), granting full wireless tablet and phone control over SENDS ON FADERS / BUS SENDS, 4-band PEQ over live 100-bin RTA, 31-Band GEQ, the 55-FX rack, TAP TEMPO, VIRTUAL SOUNDCHECK, MUTE GRP, and CLEAR SOLO.
    • Offline Stagebox Preview in SAMPLE STUDIO SESSION (UNPAIRED SAMPLE): Even without a connected X-Air or X32 hardware mixer, entering SAMPLE STUDIO SESSION from the PAIR tab hydrates both MY MONITOR and FULL MIXER with a realistic rehearsal band patch so musicians and engineers can practice monitor balance, SENDS ON FADERS, PEQ, GEQ, and FX navigation offline.

7.6.6 Cave Companion Wireless GROOVEBOX & SAMPLER Remote (SEQ + SYNTH, 16 PADS, SAMPLER & ARRANGER)#

Selecting GROOVEBOX on a tablet (or CONSOLE -> GROOVEBOX on a phone) connects directly to the desktop workstation's 6-Archetype Groovebox & Studio Sampler over the low-latency studio wireless link (50 Hz telemetry and continuous fractional playhead updates, with Android FULL immersive taskbar toggle and immediate coupled Master Playback STOP / |< response):

  1. Zero-Scroll Exact-Fit Hardware Chassis (SEQ + SYNTH): Dynamically banks voice rows at >= 48 dp touch pitch across all phone and tablet viewports with always-visible playhead hairline, melodic ANALOG BASS note labels and violet Tie Bridge Bars, [2D | NOTE | VEL] step drag, two-handed touch Parameter Locking, in-dock ARCH switching across all 6 voices (MEM, SNR, MET, MOD, BAS, SMP), contextual Bass Setup, the pinned METRONOME + symmetric [POCKET | CLUB] 13-kit selector (+GROOVE opt-in), and Live Deck (CTRL ALL, STASH, RELOAD KIT, MORPH, HOLD FILL, SLIP BEAT-REPEAT).
  2. 16 PADS Live Finger-Drumming Surface: 16 color-coded, velocity-sensitive drum pads with vertical Y-axis strike velocity ([PADS 1-8 | PADS 9-16] banking on compact landscape phones).
  3. SAMPLER Adaptive Tablet & Phone Surface (Zero-Scroll):
    • Wide Tablet (>= 840 dp/pt, Dual-Pane): Left pane combines voice/sample header, inline history strip (11 Files · 272 MB with Keep Latest 3, Empty Trash…, HIDE), 1x..16x pinch-zoomable waveform with draggable slice markers, SuperFlux slicer controls (TRANS / GRID / PAD, APPLY KIT, APPLY TRK), and capture/bounce actions (REC/STOP, CROP, NORM, REV, BPM FIT, FX BOUNCE). Right pane pairs S01..S64 SLICE CHOP PADS (BANK A..D, Y-axis velocity), playback/filter/LFO controls, and the 2 x 4 touch-bar macro deck.
    • Compact Phone (< 840 dp/pt): Zero-scroll 3-page mode switcher in Plain Studio Language: [WAVE | SLICES | MANGLE] (WAVE waveform & slicing, SLICES chop pads S01-08 / S09-16 across BANK A..D, and MANGLE macros, filter/LFO, resample, bounce, and Sample History pruning).
  4. ARRANGER Paginated Scene Launcher & Pattern Bank: Launches and chains S01..S16 Scenes with DIRECT / NEXT BEAT / NEXT BAR quantization, paginated blocks, and per-block voice mute overrides. Mutating Groovebox or Sampler state requires Full Control + Camera role.
Part IV · Chapter 8

Actions, Shortcuts, Studio CLI & Python Automation Reference

Complete reference for all 62 bindable keyboard actions (updated CMD/CTRL+1..0 workspace order) and built-in Studio Coach (?) shortcuts across macOS, Windows, and Linux, console, timeline, MIDI Sync, Groovebox, Studio Sampler, Stagebox, Remote workspace, and mobile touch gestures, the Keymap View, Studio Pad Surface dual-personality hardware button, SAMPLING, and pad shortcuts, desktop command-line options, and the complete caverec-cli, caverec-headless, sample-clocked Meter and Probe pipeline, POSIX FIFO bridge, Python client (extras/python/caverec.py), and 6 embedded Studio Engineering Skills reference.

Cave Recorder is engineered for fast, eyes-on-the-band operation during live rehearsals and studio tracking sessions, paired with a scriptable command-line and Python automation interface for live control and offline analysis. Every transport command, workspace switch, marker placement, channel strip toggle, timeline zoom action, and snapshot operation can be triggered from the keyboard, mouse/trackpad, Dual-Screen Pad Controller, or caverec-cli.

This chapter provides the complete reference for all 62 keyboard-assignable studio actions (plus built-in ? Studio Coach and arrow navigation keys) across macOS, Windows, and Linux, all mouse, trackpad, Groovebox, MIDI Sync, Stagebox, and Cave Companion touch gestures, the interactive KEYMAP configuration workspace (CMD + 8 on macOS, CTRL + 8 on Windows and Linux), desktop launch flags, Studio Pad Surface hardware shortcuts, and the complete caverec-cli, caverec-headless, sample-clocked Meter and Probe pipeline, POSIX FIFO bridge, Python client (extras/python/caverec.py), and 6 Studio Engineering Skills reference.

8.1 Complete Keyboard Shortcut Reference (All 62 Actions by Scope)#

Cave Recorder organizes its 62 bindable actions into seven execution scopes so that single-key shortcuts can be reused across different workspace views without colliding:

  • Platform Modifier Mapping: Cave Recorder supports four modifier keys across platforms: the primary command modifier maps to CMD on macOS and CTRL on Windows and Linux, the alt modifier maps to OPT (ALT) on macOS and ALT on Windows and Linux, the shift modifier maps to SHIFT on all platforms, and the secondary control modifier maps to CTRL on macOS and SUPER (WIN) on Windows and Linux. Keymap profiles saved on one operating system automatically translate to the native modifiers on the other platforms.
  • Modal Priority (PROJECT MODAL): While the PROJECT (Project & Session Browser) modal is open, only PROJECT MODAL actions (ENTER and ESC) respond to keyboard input.
  • View-Specific Priority & Global Fallback: When a workspace view tab (TIMELINE, MIXER, CHANNEL STRIP, MARKERS, or TAKES) is active, Cave Recorder checks that view's dedicated shortcuts first and then falls back to GLOBAL actions. Unmodified single-letter keys (R, O, C, M, K, L) remain reserved for global transport and cue marker actions, ? toggles [?] Studio Coach whenever no text field is active, and channel strip toggles on MIXER use SHIFT combinations (SHIFT + M, SHIFT + S, SHIFT + A, SHIFT + I, SHIFT + P) so you never accidentally mute or disarm a track while dropping a marker.

These 10 actions belong to the GLOBAL / TRANSPORT category (GLOBAL scope) and are active from every workspace view whenever the Project Browser modal is closed.

Toggle Retroactive RAM Ring Unbound (Assignable in KEYMAP) Unbound (Assignable in KEYMAP) Enables or disables continuous background 30-minute ● RETRO capture across record-armed inputs.
Toggle Timeline Auto-Scroll Unbound (Assignable in KEYMAP) Unbound (Assignable in KEYMAP) Toggles SCROLL so the Timeline viewport follows the advancing playhead automatically.

8.2 Complete Mouse & Trackpad Gesture Reference#

All faders, rotary knobs, horizontal drag bars, meter overload lamps, processor rack slots, interactive EQ and compressor graphs, and timeline rulers share consistent mouse and trackpad gestures across Cave Recorder.

Control / Surface Mouse / Modifier Gesture Behavior
Faders, Rotary Knobs & Value Bars Click + Drag (Vertical on faders and knobs, Horizontal on strip bars) Sweeps the parameter smoothly along its logarithmic dB, frequency, or percentage taper.
Faders, Rotary Knobs & Value Bars SHIFT + Drag (can be pressed or released mid-drag) Engages 10x fine precision adjustment (0.1 dB steps on faders, trims, sends, and thresholds, sub-Hz on EQ, 0.01 on Q).
Faders, Rotary Knobs & Value Bars Double-Click or OPT/ALT + Click Resets any fader or trim to 0.0 dB unity, any PAN or BAL bar to center (C), and any processor knob to its factory default.
Faders, Rotary Knobs & Value Bars Mouse Scroll Wheel Steps the hovered fader, knob, or horizontal bar up or down in calibrated increments.
Numeric Value Entry (Faders, Knobs & Value Bars) Right-Click any value slider/knob (or Click fader/knob readout), type value, press ENTER Opens an inline numeric entry field showing the current formatted value so you can type an exact target (such as -3.5, 56.3, or 0) and press ENTER to apply, or ESC to cancel.
Peak/RMS Meters & Clip Lamps Click red clip indicator or CLR CLIP button Resets latched red 0.0 dBFS overload lamps and floating yellow peak-hold markers on the channel or Master Bus meter.
8-Slot Processor Rack (Slots 1..8) Click slot label (1:PLUGIN, 2:12B EQ, 3:VCA CMP, ! MISSING) Selects that rack slot and opens the inline SLOT N PROCESSOR picker to swap processor types, assign a discovered .clap or macOS Audio Unit (AUv3 / AUv2) plugin, open a floating PLUGIN GUI window, or relink a Ghost Slot via LOCATE....
8-Slot Processor Rack (Slots 1..8) Drag :: handle vertically or Click ^ / v arrows Reorders processor slots (1:PLUGIN, 2:12B EQ, 3:VCA CMP, 4:AUX SND, or loaded third-party CLAP and macOS Audio Unit plugins) live in real time with clickless crossfading and zero audio dropouts.
8-Slot Processor Rack (Slots 1..8) Click B button on any rack slot Bypasses or re-engages that individual processor slot in place (illuminates amber when bypassed) for instant A/B listening.
8-Slot Processor Rack Header Click SWAP EQ/CMP or RESET SWAP EQ/CMP exchanges the slot order of 12B EQ and VCA CMP in one click. RESET restores all built-in channel processors to flat defaults.
12-Band Parametric EQ Graph (2:12B EQ) Click + Drag band node horizontally / vertically Sweeps the band's center/corner frequency (20 Hz to 20 kHz) and gain (-24.0 dB to +24.0 dB) simultaneously over the live Dual-Trace RTA.
12-Band Parametric EQ Graph (2:12B EQ) Mouse Scroll Wheel over node or SHIFT + Drag Scrolling over a node narrows or widens filter bandwidth (Q, 0.10 to 18.00). Holding SHIFT while dragging engages 10x fine frequency and gain resolution.
12-Band Parametric EQ Graph (2:12B EQ) Double-Click band node (or OPT/ALT + Click) Resets the band's gain to 0.0 dB (or toggles band bypass when double-clicking a band selector pill).
VCA Compressor Graph (3:VCA CMP) Click + Drag threshold or ratio handle on transfer curve Adjusts compressor THRESH (-60.0 dB to 0.0 dB) and compression RATIO slope (1.0:1 to 20.0:1) directly against the scrolling GR trace.
Waveform Timeline Ruler & Canvas Single-Click (< 4 px travel) on ruler or waveform canvas Repositions the green Playhead or amber Position Cursor to the clicked timestamp, snapping to Take start (00:00:00.000) and Take end within 8 px.
Waveform Timeline Ruler & Canvas SHIFT + Click or SHIFT + Drag Bypasses Take-boundary snapping so you can place or scrub the Playhead and Position Cursor at exact sub-sample coordinates.
Waveform Timeline Ruler & Canvas Click + Drag Horizontally (left / right) Dragging horizontally on the ruler scrubs the Playhead across the Take. Dragging horizontally on the waveform canvas pans the visible time window.
Waveform Timeline Ruler & Canvas Click + Drag Vertically (up / down) Performs continuous exponential 2D Scrub-Zoom anchored at the sample under the cursor (or around the Playhead when LOCK PH/CUR is active).
Waveform Timeline Viewport Two-Finger Horizontal Trackpad Scroll or SHIFT + Mouse Wheel Smoothly pans the horizontal waveform viewport backward or forward across the active Take.
Waveform Timeline Viewport CMD + Mouse Wheel (macOS) / CTRL + Mouse Wheel (Win/Linux) Zooms the waveform timeline horizontally in or out anchored at the mouse pointer position.
Marker (MKR) & Range (RNG) Lanes Click + Drag cyan marker flag or amber range [ / ] handles Moves a standalone cue marker or adjusts the start and end sample boundaries of a loop range directly on the timeline.
MIDI Sync Modal (MIDI SYNC) Press T (4-Tap Count-In) or ESC (Cancel MIDI LEARN) Registers 4-tap count-in beats directly from the keyboard while MIDI SYNC & HARDWARE CALIBRATION is open, or cancels an armed MIDI LEARN capture.
Drum Machine Step Matrix (DRUM MACHINE) Click empty cell + vertical drag / Click active cell Activates a HIT and drags velocity (1..127) on percussion rows in one motion. Releasing an active cell with < 4 px travel toggles it off while preserving stored notes, P-locks, and articulations.
Drum Machine Melodic Bass Rows (ANALOG BASS) Drag in [2D | NOTE | VEL] (SHIFT = ±12 st octave, OPT/ALT or CMD = secondary axis) / Right-Click NOTE In 2D mode, vertical drag steps chromatic pitch (8 px / st) and horizontal drag paints or retracts sustained Tie chains (OPT/ALT or CMD + vertical drag adjusts velocity). NOTE locks off horizontal Tie painting. VEL swaps plain drag to velocity (OPT/ALT or CMD = pitch). Right-Click on the Step Inspector NOTE slider accepts note names (Eb2, F#1) or MIDI numbers (36).

Dragging P1/P2 reticles on the Storage-CRT sweeps paired archetype macros in 2D (for ANALOG BASS: CUTOFF × RESONANCE and ENV MOD × DRIVE).

Studio Sampler Waveform & Pad Bank (DRUM MACHINE -> SAMPLER) Mouse Scroll Wheel / Drag Start, End, or Slice markers (SHIFT = 0.20x fine) / Click waveform or 4x4 Pads (A..D) Zooms the sample waveform around the cursor (Z-, Z+, 1:1), fine-trims boundaries against the ±96-frame Split Zero-Crossing Zoom lens, drops zero-crossed slices in LIVE PAD mode, or auditions slices S01..S64 across bottom-up Banks A..D.
Camera Filmstrip Lane (WAVEFORM TIMELINE) Hover / Skim Pointer over filmstrip / Drag Camera Trim (Double-Click or OPT/ALT + Click to reset) Reveals the cyan skimmer hairline, floating 16:9 BT.709 Frame Loupe Popover (#F<frame> · <MM:SS.mmm>), and vertical transient guide across audio tracks. Dragging Camera Trim nudges visual sync to exact samples.
Cave Companion Mobile Touch Gestures 2-Finger Drag (4x fine) / 2-Finger Pinch (EQ Q & SAMPLER 1x..16x zoom) / 600 ms Hold (+48V) / Y-Axis Strike (16 PADS & SAMPLER chop pads) / Bass [2D | NOTE | VEL] / Tap FULL Engages 4x fine precision on faders and drum encoders, adjusts EQ bandwidth (Q) or zooms the SAMPLER waveform via pinch, guards +48V phantom power, maps vertical strike position to velocity on 16 PADS and SLICE CHOP PADS, edits ANALOG BASS pitch and ties directly on the step grid, and toggles Android full-screen immersive taskbar mode (FULL).

8.3 Customizing Shortcuts in the KEYMAP View (CMD/CTRL + 8)#

Pressing CMD + 8 on macOS (CTRL + 8 on Windows and Linux) or clicking KEYMAP in Row 1 Right of the Top Transport Deck opens the KEYMAP & SHORTCUT CONFIGURATION workspace covering all 62 bindable studio actions (37 global actions across Transport, Navigation, Markers, and Session plus 23 view-scoped actions and 2 Project modal actions).

8.3.1 Searching by Action Name, Reverse-Searching by Key Chord & Filtering by Scope#

The KEYMAP view provides three complementary ways to inspect bindings across all 62 studio actions:

  1. Text Search (Search actions or keys...): Type any action name (Phase Align, Snapshot, Pass Lanes, Groovebox, Stagebox, Remote), action identifier (transport_record), scope name (MIX CONSOLE), or key chord (SHIFT + M, CMD + 1) into the left search box to filter the table in real time. Click CLR to clear the text query.
  2. Interactive Reverse-Search by Shortcut (FIND BY SHORTCUT:): Click inside the CLICK & PRESS KEYS TO FIND... capture well in the top header bar. Its status indicator switches from IDLE to LISTENING... and the prompt changes to HOLD MODIFIERS OR PRESS KEY...:
    • Hold Modifier Keys (MODS: [...]): Hold down any combination of modifiers (CMD/CTRL, OPT/ALT, SHIFT) without pressing a letter key to filter the table immediately to every action whose shortcut includes those held modifiers.
    • Press a Trigger Key (EXACT: [...]): Press any non-modifier key (such as SPACE, R, or 1) to lock the complete key chord and isolate the exact action(s) bound to that shortcut across all scopes.
    • Clear Reverse Search (CLR KEY): Click CLR KEY beside the capture box to clear the key filter and restore all 62 rows.
  3. Scope & Status Quick-Filter Pills: Click any of the eight filter pills in the toolbar (62/62 ROWS) to isolate a specific subset of actions (ALL, GLOBAL, CONSOLE, TIMELINE, INSPECTOR, REEL/MRK, BOUND, MODIFIED).

8.3.2 Recording Custom Shortcuts, Unbinding & Resetting Defaults#

Every row in the KEYMAP table includes an interactive SHORTCUT (CLICK TO ASSIGN) capture well and row action buttons on the far right:

  1. Enter Capture Mode (ASSIGN or Click Capture Well): Click the ASSIGN button on the target row, or click directly inside its SHORTCUT (CLICK TO ASSIGN) box (UNBOUND - CLICK TO SET). The row's capture well highlights and prompts PRESS KEYS, THEN APPLY, while the right-hand action column switches to APPLY, CANCEL, and UNBIND.
  2. Press Your Desired Key Combination: Hold any desired modifier keys (CMD/CTRL, OPT/ALT, SHIFT) and press a character key (A..Z, 0..9, [, ], -, =, ,, .), function key (F1..F12), or named navigation key (SPACE, ENTER, TAB, BACKSPACE, DELETE, HOME, END, PGUP, PGDN, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT). Shifted punctuation symbols (such as { or +) are automatically normalized to their canonical physical base key (SHIFT + [ or SHIFT + =) for consistent cross-platform matching.
  3. Commit the Binding (APPLY): Click APPLY to validate and save the captured key chord, or click CANCEL (or click outside the capture well) to exit without changing the shortcut.
  4. Unbind or Reset Individual Actions (UNBIND / RESET): Click UNBIND on any row to clear its shortcut to UNBOUND, or click RESET to restore that single action to its factory default binding.
  5. Restore Factory Defaults Across the Entire Studio (RESET ALL DEFAULTS): Click RESET ALL DEFAULTS at the top right of the KEYMAP header to restore all 61 actions to their original factory keybindings in one step.

8.3.3 Live Scope Conflict Detection, Shared Non-Conflicting Scopes & OS Warnings#

When you assign a custom shortcut, Cave Recorder validates the key chord against two safety layers before writing to disk:

  1. Scope Clash Detection (CLASH DETECTED Confirmation Banner):
    • Overlapping Scopes (Blocked Without Confirmation): Because GLOBAL shortcuts are active across every workspace view, assigning the same key chord to two GLOBAL actions, to two actions in the same workspace view, or to a GLOBAL action and a workspace view action creates an ambiguous collision. When you click APPLY on a colliding chord, Cave Recorder pauses and displays the amber Clash Detection Banner at the top of the KEYMAP view (CLASH DETECTED: [SPACE] conflicts with "Play / Pause Transport" (GLOBAL) in overlapping scope [GLOBAL]. Overwrite and unbind existing?). Click CONFIRM OVERWRITE to assign the shortcut and automatically unbind the conflicting action, or click CANCEL to keep your existing bindings untouched.
    • Non-Conflicting Sibling Views (Allowed & Highlighted in Green): Because only one workspace view tab is visible at a time, sibling view scopes (MIX CONSOLE, WAVEFORM TIMELINE, CHANNEL INSPECTOR, SESSION REEL, and MARKERS & RANGES) never conflict with each other, and PROJECT MODAL only runs while the modal browser is open. When two actions in separate views share the same key (such as E bound to Expand All Track Pass Lanes in WAVEFORM TIMELINE and Toggle Pass Lanes on Inspected Channel in CHANNEL INSPECTOR), the DESCRIPTION, SCOPE & WARNINGS column highlights SHARED IN NON-CONFLICTING SCOPE: CHANNEL INSPECTOR in emerald green.
  2. Operating System Shortcut Conflict Warnings (OS WARN):
    • If you assign a key combination commonly intercepted by the host desktop environment, Cave Recorder displays an amber OS WARN (<Platform>): <System Function> badge in the row description so you know the operating system may capture the key press first:
    • macOS Warnings: CMD + Q (Quit Application), CMD + H (Hide Window), CMD + M (Minimize Window), CMD + W (Close Window), CMD + SPACE (Spotlight Search), CMD + TAB (Application Switcher), CMD + SHIFT + 3/4/5 (System Screenshot), and CTRL + Arrow keys (Mission Control / Desktop Spaces).
    • Windows & Linux Warnings: ALT + F4 (Close Window), ALT + TAB (Window Switcher), ALT + SPACE (Window Menu), CTRL + W / CTRL + Q (Close / Quit), CTRL + SHIFT + ESC (Task Manager), CTRL + ALT + T / DELETE (Terminal / Session Dialog), and SUPER (WIN) + L/D/E/R/I/TAB/SPACE/Arrow keys.

8.3.4 Persisting, Backing Up & Sharing Studio Keymap Profiles (keymap.json)#

Every change you make in the KEYMAP view is saved immediately to a human-readable JSON profile (keymap.json) inside your user configuration folder (stored alongside preferences.json and recent.json):

  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/caverec/keymap.json
  • Linux: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/caverec/keymap.json (or ~/.config/caverec/keymap.json when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset)
  • Windows: %APPDATA%\caverec\keymap.json (or %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\caverec\keymap.json)
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "bindings": {
    "console_trigger_group_phase_align": {
      "modifiers": {
        "command": false,
        "control": false,
        "alt": false,
        "shift": true
      },
      "key": {
        "kind": "character",
        "value": "G"
      }
    }
  }
}

To transfer your custom studio keymap to a second rehearsal computer or back it up to version control:

  1. Copy keymap.json from the source workstation's configuration directory into the target workstation's caverec configuration directory while Cave Recorder is closed, and launch caverec.
  2. On startup, Cave Recorder automatically normalizes character symbols, maps command: true to CMD on macOS and CTRL on Windows and Linux, populates any omitted actions with their factory defaults, and sanitizes the table so no two overlapping scopes can ever load with a conflicting shortcut.

8.4 Command-Line & Automated Studio Verification Reference#

In addition to launching Cave Recorder from your desktop application menu, studio engineers and system integrators can run caverec from a terminal shell to execute automated 18-channel signal-path verification or generate offscreen workspace captures for studio documentation and rig sign-off.

# 1. Standard interactive desktop studio launch
caverec

# 2. Run the 18-channel studio self-test & signal-path verification
caverec --self-test
caverec --stress-test

# 3. Render all 25 workspace & modal inspection presets (29 manual PNGs including crops)
caverec --screenshot-dir .tmp/caverec-shots

# 4. Render a single workspace preset at custom dimensions
caverec --screenshot-dir .tmp/caverec-shots \
  --screenshot-view console-18ch \
  --screenshot-size 1680x960

8.4.1 Command-Line Arguments Reference#

Command-Line Flag Arguments / Values Studio Function
(No arguments) None Launches the interactive Cave Recorder desktop workstation (1680x960 default window), loads user keybindings (keymap.json) and studio preferences (preferences.json), and opens the PROJECT browser modal to select or create a Session.
--self-test
--stress-test		 None Runs the automated 18-Channel Studio Self-Test & Hardware Verification Suite and exits with code 0 on pass or 1 on failure. Verifies 18-in/20-out routing (CH01..CH08 analog preamps, CH09..CH10 S/PDIF, CH11..CH18 ADAT optical), 48.0 kHz / 44.1 kHz sample-rate clock switching, multi-mic drum phase alignment, 30-minute retroactive memory capture, simultaneous 14-track playback + 4-track overdub pass recording, and offline mixdown and stem rendering.

8.5 Studio Pad Surface Hardware Control & Shortcut Reference#

All shortcuts below apply to a connected Dual-Screen Pad Controller (Section 2.8). Touching any of the 8 display encoders (E1..E8) brackets continuous adjustments into a single coalesced Undo gesture, and holding SHIFT while turning any encoder engages 10x fine precision.

8.6 Studio CLI (caverec-cli), Headless Engine (caverec-headless), Probes, Python Client & Studio Skills#

Direct desktop distributions of Cave Recorder include the lightweight caverec-cli command-line client (sub-5 ms cold startup) and the caverec-headless offline studio daemon alongside the zero-dependency Python client extras/python/caverec.py. Together they expose 100% live-versus-offline parity: every console, processor, Groovebox, Studio Sampler, Stagebox, metering, audio probing, and export command works identically against a running desktop Cave Recorder window (--live) or a closed session folder running offline at 20x to 100x real time (--offline --session <dir>).

8.6.1 Installation, Authentication & Global Flags#

  • One-Click Setup from Desktop: Open AUDIO SETTINGS (CMD/CTRL + ,) and click INSTALL CAVEREC-CLI & STUDIO SKILLS... under CLI & STUDIO SKILLS (CAVEREC-CLI) (or run caverec-cli setup-path followed by caverec-cli skills install in a terminal).
  • Local Loopback Security: Running instances publish an owner-only endpoint file (<config_dir>/run/instances/<role>-<pid>.json, 0600 permissions on macOS/Linux and owner-only ACL on Windows) bound strictly to 127.0.0.1 with a 256-bit bearer token. Offline invocations automatically launch and reuse a warm caverec-headless serve --idle-timeout-secs 300 daemon (or use --oneshot for single-command teardown). Note that the Mac App Store edition omits bundled CLI executables from its .pkg archive, while still accepting loopback 127.0.0.1 connections from an externally installed caverec-cli.
  • Global Flags: --json, --ndjson, --live, --offline, --session <dir>, --instance <id|pid>, --dry-run, and --print-request-json.

8.6.2 Complete 30-Command Group Reference#
